same M27 bare-global rule `nixVersion`/`currentSystem` already follow
(confirmed: bare `storeDir` is also "undefined variable" on real Nix).

## M72 scope notes: bumped `derivation`'s attribute-count cap; `d.nix` reaches completion

Found continuing to chase `d.nix` right after M71: the next (and, it
turned out, final) blocker was "asnix: derivation: too many attributes
(max 64)" -- `derivation.c`'s `asnix_prim_derivation` stores every
input attribute into a few fixed-size C stack arrays
(`env[ASNIX_DRV_MAX_ENV]`, `json_syms`/`json_vals[ASNIX_DRV_MAX_ENV]`,
M69's `__structuredAttrs` support), bounded at a hardcoded 64 -- never
hit by any fixture or conformance case so far, but a real
`stdenv.mkDerivation` call (the structuredAttrs-era
`make-derivation.nix`, M67/M69's own area) unconditionally sets a
couple dozen attributes (`enableParallelBuilding`, `strictDeps`,
`depsBuildBuild`, `depsHostHostPropagated`, `__structuredAttrs`, `env`,
`outputChecks`, ...) before the package itself contributes any of its
own, exceeding 64 easily once a few package-specific attributes are
added on top.

Fix: bumped `ASNIX_DRV_MAX_ENV` from 64 to 256. These are plain fixed-
size stack arrays, not an arena allocation -- the only cost of a larger
bound is a few more KB of stack per `derivation {...}` call, negligible
at this size (`ASNIX_DRV_MAX_ARGS`, the separate, unrelated `args`-list
cap, left at 64 -- not what tripped this). Verified with a synthetic
100-attribute `derivation {...}` call (new `tests/e2e/m72_*` fixture)
that previously hit the cap and now succeeds on both engines.

**`./asnix d.nix` now evaluates to completion with no crash** --
the exact standing goal this whole `d.nix`-driven bug-chase (every
milestone from M33 through this one, across many single-session passes
and seven parallel background agents) was aimed at. It prints a real-
looking Nix store path for `hello.outPath`:
```
asnix:      "/nix/store/z7zqhkm36dgjarhrwn6sf7akzx00zc0p-hello-2.12.3"
real Nix:   "/nix/store/wpr3vw194dl8g7bj94d54rj76v3rp3c0-hello-2.12.3"
```
The STRING SHAPE matches (a valid-looking `/nix/store/<32-char-hash>-
hello-2.12.3` path), but the HASH itself does not match real Nix's --
expected and out of scope, not a bug to chase further: bit-exact
derivation-hash equality across `hello`'s entire real dependency
closure (the full stdenv bootstrap chain, every intermediate
derivation's exact `.drv` content) would require this project's
already-and-repeatedly-documented scope cuts to not exist at all --
real string-context/`hashDerivationModulo` tracking through actual
input derivations (M61, M62's own notes), exact real-Nix-matching
`__structuredAttrs`/`__json` serialization (M69's own documented
scope), fixed-output multi-output derivations, and more. Getting the
hash to match would mean building all of that, a vastly larger project
than "find and fix crashes" -- this milestone's success criterion was
always "evaluates without crashing," which is now met.

`make test`/`test-e2e`/`test-conformance` all green (one new `m72_*`
fixture). `make test-nix-conformance`: `pass=624 fail=34 skip=148`,
unchanged (this fix isn't exercised by that corpus -- no test case

## M73 scope notes: fixed-output derivations' real `makeFixedOutputPath` formula

Found while scoping M74's `hashDerivationModulo` work (the user asked
for `d.nix`'s computed `hello.outPath` to actually MATCH real Nix's,
not just stop crashing) -- M74's own verification plan calls for a
"fixed-output input" test case (since `<nix/fetchurl.nix>`, M46, is
fixed-output, and `hello`'s own `src` comes from it), which immediately
exposed a pre-existing, **separate** bug: a fixed-output
`derivation {...}` call's `outPath` never matched real Nix at all.
`validate_output_hash_fields`'s own pre-existing comment admitted this
outright ("it does NOT change how the derivation's store path is
actually computed") -- the function only ever validated `outputHash`'s
SHAPE, then let the output path fall through to the ordinary masked-
ATerm-digest scheme every other (non-fixed-output) derivation uses,
which is simply the wrong formula for this case. Confirmed directly:
`derivation { ...; outputHashAlgo="sha256"; outputHashMode="flat";
outputHash="00...00"; }.outPath` gave a different path on asnix than
on real `nix-instantiate --eval --strict`.

**Fix**: ported real Nix's actual `makeFixedOutputPath`
(`~/nix/src/libstore/store-dir-config.cc`) verbatim. Two cases:
- `sha256` + `outputHashMode = "recursive"`: the output path comes
  straight from the content hash itself (`makeStorePath("source", hash,
  name)`) -- no extra hashing step.
- every other combination (the common case: `"flat"` mode, which is
  `<nix/fetchurl.nix>`'s own default, M46): hash a
  `"fixed:out:<r:-or-empty><algo>:<hex-hash>:"` payload string with
  SHA-256, then feed *that* into the ordinary `makeStorePath("output:out",
  ..., name)` formula (`compute_store_path`, unchanged, M8/M62). Renamed
  `validate_output_hash_fields` to `decode_output_hash` (same
  validation, now also returns the decoded raw digest bytes + resolved
  algorithm so the above can actually use them -- a new
  `compute_fixed_output_path` function implements the two-case formula,
  reusing `compute_store_path` in both branches rather than
  reimplementing its preimage/outer-hash/base32 pipeline a third time).

A second, related gap found verifying the "recursive" case specifically:
real Nix's `.drv` ATerm for a fixed-output derivation's `Outputs` entry
carries real `hashAlgo`/`hash` fields (confirmed directly against a
real `.drv`: `("out",path,"sha256","0d5f6015...")`, not `("out",path,
"","")`, which is what every *other* derivation's entry correctly
still has) -- needed because this derivation's own `drvPath` is hashed
from this REAL (unmasked) ATerm text, so a wrong Outputs entry means a
wrong `drvPath` even when `outPath` itself is already correct (exactly
what the "recursive" verification case caught: `outPath` matched,
`drvPath` didn't, until this was fixed). `"recursive"` mode additionally
prepends `"r:"` to that ATerm field specifically (confirmed: `("out",
path,"r:sha256",hash)`) -- a real Nix detail (`makeFileIngestionPrefix`)
distinct from (and in addition to) the path-formula's own `"r:"`
handling above. `AtermOutput` (`aterm.h`/`aterm.c`) gained `hash_algo`/
`hash` fields, NULL for the ordinary (non-fixed-output) case every
other derivation still uses unchanged.

Verified against real `nix-instantiate --eval --strict`, both `outPath`
AND `drvPath`, across: flat+sha256 (hex), SRI-format (`sha256-base64`,
`outputHashAlgo=""`, `<nix/fetchurl.nix>`'s own shape, M48), recursive+
sha256, and flat+md5 -- all four now match exactly.

`make test`/`test-e2e` green (`tests/c/test_aterm.c` and its 4 call
sites updated for `asnix_build_derivation_aterm`'s new `inputDrvs`/
`inputSrcs` parameters, added ahead of M74's own need for them, passed
as empty for now; `test_multi_output`'s unaffected by the new
`AtermOutput` fields since C zero-initializes trailing struct-literal
members). `make test-conformance` (mined subset) unchanged.
`make test-nix-conformance`: `pass=624 fail=34 skip=148` before this
fix, `pass=626 fail=32 skip=148` after -- +2 net, zero regressions.

## M74 scope notes: real `hashDerivationModulo` (input-derivation hashing)

The user explicitly rejected "`d.nix` evaluates without crashing" as
good enough (M72's own stated goal) once it was pointed out that the
computed `hello.outPath` hash didn't actually match real Nix's. Root
cause: `hello`'s derivation depends on several other derivations
(`bash`, `stdenv-linux`, a `fetchurl`-fixed-output source, etc.), and
real Nix's `hashDerivationModulo` requires substituting each input
derivation's *own* hash in place of its literal `.drv` path before
hashing the dependent derivation -- `derivation.c` had no concept of
"this attribute value references another derivation" at all, so it
always string-coerced every attribute and lost that information
entirely, making this substitution impossible.

Two pieces, neither needing real store/file I/O:

- **A narrow, call-scoped input-reference collector**
  (`asnix_collect_input_refs`), *not* a persistent Value-level string-
  context feature (that broader feature -- a 4th tagged Value kind
  touching ~101 call sites -- was declined twice already, M61 and
  implicitly M45/M54/M60, as disproportionate to its own user-facing
  payoff). This one only needs to know, for the duration of one
  `derivation {...}` call, which attribute values are (or contain) a
  derivation-output reference. Walks each already-forced attribute
  value: an attrset with `type`/`drvPath`/`outputName` (every
  derivation Value has these, M58's wrapper) records a `Built` ref;
  a list recurses into every element; a bare Path already under
  `/nix/store/` records an `Opaque` `inputSrcs` ref. Nothing else is
  tracked (scope cut, matching M61's own precedent of naming what's
  deferred): no `DrvDeep` context, no copying arbitrary local files
  into a content-addressed store (no precedent for that anywhere in
  this project; M45's `toFile` explicitly declined the equivalent).
- **A process-global, in-memory masked-hash cache**
  (`g_masked_hash_cache`, modeled directly on M65's `g_import_cache`
  precedent and real Nix's own `derivation::masked::hashes`). Real
  Nix's `nix-instantiate --eval` normally writes real `.drv` files to
  `/nix/store` as a side effect and could read them back, but its
  OWN `--read-only-mode` falls back to exactly this kind of pure
  in-process memoization instead -- since Nix's call-by-need
  evaluation guarantees a referenced derivation was already forced
  (hence already cached) before anything can reference it, asnix can
  replicate read-only-mode's behavior with no real store at all. A
  cache miss is fatal (a real invariant violated), not a silent
  fallback, matching this project's standing convention.

`aterm.c`/`aterm.h` generalized to accept real `InputDrvs`/`InputSrcs`
sections (previously hardcoded to `"],[],[],"`) -- `AtermInputDrv`
is `(drv_path, [output_names...])`, matching real Nix's own ATerm
shape exactly. `derivation.c` groups the collected `Built` refs by
`drv_path` (a small, bounded, linear-scan grouping, same convention as
every other small array in this file), builds TWO parallel
`AtermInputDrv` lists -- `real_input_drvs` (literal `.drv` paths, for
this derivation's own on-disk `.drv` content/`drvPath` hash) and
`masked_input_drvs` (each group's `drv_path` replaced by its cached
masked hash, hex, no algorithm prefix -- the actual substitution) --
and passes each into its own `asnix_build_derivation_aterm` call.

Three distinct, non-obvious bugs found and fixed chasing this through
increasingly complex verification cases (each isolated by comparing
asnix's own ATerm text, via gdb, against a real `.drv` dump, and
cross-checking suspect hash computations by hand in Python):

1. **Wrong cache value for regular (non-fixed-output) derivations.**
   Initially cached `masked_digest` (the `maskOutputs=TRUE` variant,
   with THIS derivation's own outputs blanked) as the value a later
   derivation substitutes in for this one. Wrong: real Nix's
   `hashDerivationModulo`'s `maskOutputs` parameter only ever controls
   whether OUTPUT paths are blanked -- it does NOT affect whether
   `inputDrvs` get hash-substituted (that substitution always
   happens). The correct cached value is a THIRD ATerm variant never
   otherwise built: this derivation's REAL (filled-in) outputs
   combined with the SAME hash-substituted `inputDrvs` the masked pass
   already uses. Fixed by building `cache_aterm` from `real_outs` +
   `masked_input_drvs` specifically for the cache-insert step.
2. **Wrong `type` string for a derivation's own `drvPath`.** Even
   after fix 1, a 2-level chain's dependent derivation's `outPath`
   matched but its `drvPath` didn't, despite the real ATerm text being
   byte-identical (confirmed via `diff`) to real Nix's actual `.drv`
   file. Root cause: a `.drv`'s own store path is a content-addressed
   "text" path whose TYPE string is NOT the bare `"text"` this project
   previously used -- it's `"text:" + every inputSrcs/inputDrvs path,
   sorted` (`infoForDerivation`, `~/nix/src/libstore/derivations.cc`):
   a `.drv` genuinely "references" everything it mentions. Every PRIOR
   fixture had zero references, so this was unnoticed until M74's own
   2-level verification case gave it something to catch. Fixed by
   building `drv_type` from the sorted union of `group_paths`/
   `refs.srcs` before the final `compute_store_path` call.
3. **Wrong `InputDrvs` ordering for the masked pass specifically.**
   The `nativeBuildInputs = [ a b2 ]` (two distinct input derivations)
   verification case still mismatched after fixes 1/2, even though the
   REAL pass's `InputDrvs` section (sorted by literal `.drv` path) was
   byte-identical to real Nix's actual `.drv`. Root cause: real Nix's
   substitution doesn't just swap each `inputDrvs` entry's path for
   its resolved hash in place -- it rebuilds `inputDrvs` as a NEW
   `std::map<string, StringSet>` keyed by the hash STRING itself
   (`~/nix/src/libstore/derivations.cc`), and a `std::map`'s iteration
   (which `unparse` walks) is sorted by ITS OWN key -- so the MASKED
   pass's `InputDrvs` section must be sorted by the substituted hash
   hex string, independently of whatever order the literal paths
   sorted in. Confirmed: `b2`'s masked hash sorts before `a`'s despite
   `a.drv` sorting before `b2.drv`. Fixed by re-sorting
   `masked_input_drvs` by its own (already-substituted) `drv_path`
   field, separately from `real_input_drvs`'s literal-path order.

Two more bugs surfaced only once this was run against real nixpkgs
(`d.nix`, not any of this milestone's own small verification cases --
every prior fixture had too few references/inputs to hit either):
`compute_store_path`'s `preimage` buffer was a fixed 512 bytes, too
small once `type` itself became `"text:" + N references` for a
derivation with many direct inputs/sources; and the companion
`drv_type` accumulation buffer (`derivation.c`) was a fixed 4096
bytes with no overflow check on its own `snprintf` return value (a
silent-truncation risk, not just a size cap). Both are now sized
dynamically (`malloc`, exact required length) instead of guessing a
bigger constant. A third, related issue: `ASNIX_DRV_MAX_INPUT_DRVS`
(the grouping arrays' bound) was 64, too small for `stdenv-linux`
alone (well over 64 distinct direct input derivations in real
nixpkgs) -- bumped to 1024, but moved from the stack to `malloc`,
since resolving one derivation's input refs can recursively force
(hence recursively call `asnix_prim_derivation` for) a dependency
several levels deep in nixpkgs's own derivation graph, and 1024
entries' worth of these arrays on the stack per nested call actually
overflowed the real stack chasing `d.nix` to this point.

Verified against real `nix-instantiate --eval --strict`, all 5 cases
from this milestone's own plan: a plain 2-level chain, a 3-level
chain, a fixed-output input, a multi-output input (referenced by name,
`a.dev` not just `a.out`), and a list of two distinct inputs
(`nativeBuildInputs = [ a b2 ]`, the case that caught bug 3 above) --
every case's `outPath` AND `drvPath` match exactly
(`tests/e2e/m74_input_*`).

**Still open, deliberately out of this milestone's scope** (per the
plan's own Phase 1/Phase 2 split): `./asnix d.nix` now runs to
completion with the real substitution logic in place (no longer
crashing on the input-derivation-count/stack-depth bugs above), but
`hello.outPath` still doesn't bit-for-bit match real Nix's
(`n0m8hzqnp3bj0if010gjial5402xvgym...` vs real's
`wpr3vw194dl8g7bj94d54rj76v3rp3c0...`). This milestone's own scope
boundary explicitly anticipated this: there may be independent gaps
elsewhere in the full nixpkgs/stdenv chain (real Nix's internal
corepkgs builder/setup shell scripts, which this project doesn't
embed, being the leading suspect) that this milestone's narrow,
controlled verification cases can't surface. Chasing that down is a
separately tracked follow-up, using the same gdb/direct-`.drv`-diff
methodology this milestone itself used.

`make test`/`test-e2e` green (5 new `m74_input_*` fixtures, each
verified byte-for-byte against real `nix-instantiate --eval --strict`
before being written). `make test-nix-conformance`:
`pass=627 fail=31 skip=148` -- +1 net over M73, zero regressions.

## M75 scope notes: real store-copying (NAR-hash) for local Path literals

Chasing `d.nix` past M74: `hello.outPath` still didn't match real
Nix's. Root cause, confirmed by diffing real Nix's actual
`hello-2.12.3.drv` byte-for-byte against this project's own computed
ATerm: real Nix's `inputSrcs`/`args` embed `/nix/store/...-source-
stdenv.sh` and `/nix/store/...-default-builder.sh` -- `pkgs/stdenv/
generic`'s own local `.sh` files, referenced as plain Path literals
and copied into the content-addressed store when coerced to a string.
`asnix` had never implemented this at all: `value_util.c`'s
`coerce_to_string_for_interp` had an explicit, long-standing, *known*
comment admitting as much ("real Nix additionally copies the path to
the store... not implemented... produces the plain path text instead"),
and `derivation.c`'s own M74 input-reference collector only ever
tracked a bare Path already under `/nix/store/`, never one that still
needed copying there first.

**Fix**: a new `src/c/nar.c`/`nar.h`, `asnix_copy_path_to_store`,
implementing real Nix's own `addToStore` (method=NixArchive/
"recursive", hashAlgo=sha256) exactly: NAR-serialize the path (file,
directory, or symlink -- format verified byte-for-byte against
`~/nix/src/libutil/archive.cc`/`serialise.cc`: each string field is an
8-byte little-endian length, the raw bytes, then zero-padded to the
next 8-byte boundary; directory entries sorted ascending by name),
SHA-256 the result, then feed that digest through the EXACT SAME
`makeStorePath("source", digest, name)` formula M73's
`compute_fixed_output_path` already implements for its own
sha256+recursive branch -- no new path-computation logic needed, only
the NAR-serialization step was missing. Like `derivation`/`toFile`,
does not perform the real filesystem side effect (no actual
`/nix/store` writes) -- only the resulting path *string* is computed,
same stance this project has taken since M8. Memoized by literal
input path (linear-scan array, M65's import-cache convention) so the
SAME local path being both collected (M74's `asnix_collect_input_refs`)
and coerced (the actual env-var/string value) doesn't get NAR-hashed
twice.

Wiring turned out to need THREE call sites, not one, because real
Nix's `coerceToString` has independent `coerceMore`/`copyToStore`
flags and this project previously only had the two combinations that
happen to share neither:
- `coerce_to_string_for_interp` (genuine `"${...}"` string
  interpolation, `copyToStore=true`, `coerceMore=false`): now actually
  performs the copy where it previously only had the existence check
  (M67f) in front of a documented no-op.
- A brand new `asnix_coerce_to_string_for_derivation`
  (`value_util.c`/`.h`): `derivation {...}`'s own attribute coercion
  needs `coerceMore=true` (plain ints/bools/null become "7"/"1"/""
  like `toString`, verified: ordinary nixpkgs derivation attributes
  are frequently non-strings) **and** `copyToStore=true` together --
  a combination neither `asnix_coerce_to_string` (has the former, not
  the latter) nor `coerce_to_string_for_interp` (has the latter, not
  the former) provides alone. Recurses into itself (not
  `asnix_coerce_to_string`) for nested ATTRS (`__toString`/`outPath`)
  and LIST cases, so a Path nested inside either also gets copied --
  matches real `hello.drv`'s own `args` list, which contains exactly
  two such local-file references. `derivation.c`'s three existing
  coercion call sites (`args`, `outputs`, the generic per-attribute
  path) switched to it.
- `asnix_collect_input_refs`'s bare-Path case (M74, `derivation.c`):
  previously only recorded an `inputSrcs` entry for a path ALREADY
  under `/nix/store/`; now computes (via the same memoized
  `asnix_copy_path_to_store`) and records the COPIED path for anything
  else, so the `.drv`'s `inputSrcs` section agrees with what the
  coercion above actually embedded as the literal env-var/arg text --
  required, since a `.drv`'s `inputSrcs` and its own attribute values
  have to name the same store path.

**Regression found and fixed in the same pass**: `tests/e2e/
m67_path_interp_exists.nix` (`"${/.}"`, M67f) exercised this new copy
path for the first time and tried to NAR-serialize the entire
filesystem root -- which even REAL Nix fails on, on this machine
(`error: opening '/boot/System.map-...': Permission denied`,
confirmed directly). That fixture's choice of `/.`  was always a
placeholder (its own M67 scope notes already flagged "note its own
exact output isn't byte-identical to what real Nix would do," since
the copy wasn't implemented yet at the time) -- not a real scenario
worth preserving now that copying actually happens. Changed it to
self-reference the fixture file itself (always exists, small,
deterministic), and corrected its `.expected` to the real computed
store path (removing the long-standing caveat).

Verified against real `nix-instantiate --eval --strict`: a plain file
interpolated into a string, a whole directory (recursive NAR,
multiple files/subdirectories) interpolated into a string, and a
local file referenced from inside a `derivation {...}`'s `args` --
all three match exactly (`tests/e2e/m75_path_copy_*`).

**Still open**: `./asnix d.nix`'s `hello.outPath` STILL doesn't match
real Nix after this fix (it changed -- confirming this fix did take
effect -- but didn't converge). Diffing asnix's own computed ATerm for
`hello-2.12.3` against real Nix's actual `.drv` found the next gap is
qualitatively different and larger than either M74 or M75: real Nix's
`hello.drv` has FOUR `inputDrvs` (`bash`, `stdenv-linux`,
`version-check-hook`, the `fetchurl` source), but asnix's only has
THREE -- missing `bash` entirely, even though `bash`'s own store path
*is* correctly present as the literal `builder` string. Root cause:
nixpkgs sets `builder = stdenvShell;` where `stdenvShell` ultimately
traces back to `shell = "${stage0.bash}/bin/bash";` (`pkgs/stdenv/
linux/default.nix`) -- a STRING INTERPOLATION of a derivation
reference, concatenated with a literal suffix, evaluated to a plain
string long before `derivation {...}`'s primop ever sees it. By the
time `asnix_collect_input_refs`'s structural walk (M74: looks for a
bare derivation attrset, a list of derivations, or an already-resolved
store Path) sees the `builder` attribute's value, it's just an opaque
string with no trace of "this came from derivation bash's output" --
exactly the information real Nix's actual *string context* (an
invisible, attached-to-the-string-Value dependency set, threaded
through `coerceToString`/concatenation/substring/etc.) exists to
preserve. This is the same broader feature M61 (and implicitly M45/
M54/M60) already explicitly declined as disproportionate to its own
user-facing payoff (`getContext`/`hasContext`/
`addDrvOutputDependencies`) -- M74's plan deliberately scoped around
it with a narrower, call-scoped structural collector specifically
because the full feature is large. That narrower collector is
necessarily blind to the (idiomatically very common in real nixpkgs)
case of a dependency reference flowing through a string
interpolation rather than staying a bare attrset/Path -- which is
exactly what `hello`'s own `builder` attribute does. Separately
(smaller, independent): asnix's `__json` blob also has two EXTRA keys
real Nix's doesn't (`__ignoreNulls`, `userHook`) -- real Nix's
structured-attrs serialization drops any attribute whose value is
`null` when `__ignoreNulls = true` is set (including `__ignoreNulls`
itself), not yet implemented here. Both are tracked as a follow-up,
not blocking this milestone's own (verified, scoped) completion.

`make test`/`test-e2e` green (3 new `m75_path_copy_*` fixtures --
file, directory, and derivation-attribute cases -- plus the
`m67_path_interp_exists` fixture/expected correction above).
`make test-nix-conformance`: `pass=628 fail=30 skip=148` -- +1 net
over M74, zero regressions.

## M76 scope notes: real string context

Chasing `d.nix` past M75: `hello.outPath` still didn't match real Nix.
Diffing asnix's own computed ATerm for `hello-2.12.3` against real Nix's
actual `.drv` found the gap was qualitatively different and larger than
M74/M75: real Nix's `hello.drv` has FOUR `inputDrvs` (`bash`,
`stdenv-linux`, `version-check-hook`, the `fetchurl` source), but asnix's
only had THREE -- missing `bash` entirely, even though `bash`'s own store
path *was* correctly present as the literal `builder` string. Root cause:
nixpkgs sets `builder = stdenvShell;`, which traces back to `shell =
"${stage0.bash}/bin/bash";` (`pkgs/stdenv/linux/default.nix`) -- a STRING
INTERPOLATION of a derivation reference, concatenated with a literal
suffix, evaluated to a plain opaque string long before `derivation
{...}`'s primop ever sees it. M74's structural collector
(`asnix_collect_input_refs`: looks for a bare derivation attrset, a list
of derivations, or an already-resolved store Path) is blind to this by
construction -- once a reference becomes a STRING via interpolation,
there's no structure left to walk. This is the same feature M61 (and
implicitly M45/M54/M60) already declined once, for being disproportionate
to its own user-facing payoff (`getContext`/`hasContext`/
`addDrvOutputDependencies`) -- the user explicitly chose to implement it
anyway, since it turned out to also be load-bearing for hash parity.

**Key design simplification vs. the originally-declined scope**: that
earlier estimate (~101 call sites, a new tagged Value kind touching the
asm layer) assumed context would be baked into the STRING HEAP LAYOUT
itself (like Path/Float's marker-byte trick, `include/asnix/heap.h`).
Instead, a new `src/c/string_context.c`/`.h` attaches context via a SIDE
TABLE keyed by the string Value's own arena pointer (a linear-scan array,
same convention as `eval_file.c`'s import cache / `derivation.c`'s
masked-hash cache) -- ordinary string reads (every asm op: equality,
printing, hashing, `OP_STR_CONCAT`'s own byte-copying) stay COMPLETELY
untouched, since they never need to know a context exists. Only the
specific C-level functions that *construct* a new string from existing
string/attrs/list inputs need to query-and-propagate -- a literal survey
of every such function (an Explore agent cross-referencing both this
codebase and real Nix's own `coerceToString`/`primops.cc`) found ~20 call
sites, not ~101, and zero asm changes.

`AsnixStringContext` (`drvs: {drv_path, output_name}[]`, `srcs: path[]`)
reuses exactly M74's own `BuiltRef`/`InputRefSet` vocabulary.
`asnix_string_attach_context(v, ctx)`/`asnix_string_context_of(v)` are the
only two public entry points -- a no-op/`NULL` for the overwhelmingly
common case (every plain-literal/arithmetic/non-derivation string never
gets a table entry at all).

**Origin points** (where context is *synthesized*): `asnix_prim_derivation`
(`derivation.c`) now attaches `Built(drv_path, output_names[o])` to each
output-path string it builds for the self-referential `strict` attrset --
this is exactly what `pkg.out`/`pkg.${name}` resolve to, which is what
`"${pkg}/bin/x"`-style interpolation reads via the `outPath`-lookup
coercion path (`drvPath` itself stays context-free -- that's real Nix's
separate `DrvDeep` context, referencing a derivation's whole closure,
explicitly out of scope, same as M74's own collector never handled it).
Coercing an already-`/nix/store/...` Path to a string, and M75's NAR-copy
result, both now attach `Opaque(path)` -- this subsumes M74's bare-Path
structural detection entirely.

**Propagation points** (forward/union existing context, no new entries):
`asnix_coerce_to_string`'s ATTRS (`__toString`/`outPath`) and LIST
branches; the same two branches in `asnix_coerce_to_string_for_derivation`
(M75); `coerce_to_string_for_interp`'s Path branch; `concat_strings_impl`
(backs both `"${...}"` interpolation and `+`'s string/path-concat case --
the single highest-traffic site). Each follows the same mechanical
pattern: accumulate each piece's own context via `asnix_string_context_of`,
union into a local `AsnixStringContext`, attach to the result if
non-empty. Scoped OUT of this milestone (matching M74's own precedent of
naming what's deferred, not silently skipping it): propagation through
`substring`/`concatStringsSep`/`baseNameOf`/`dirOf`/`replaceStrings`/
`stringToCharacters`/`toJSON`/`toXML`; `getContext`/`appendContext`'s real
Nix-level attrset shape (currently still hardcoded no-ops);
`unsafeDiscardStringContext` actually stripping an entry (currently still
a harmless identity pass-through, same as before this milestone, since
nothing had context to discard either way); `toFile`'s context-validation-
and-fold-into-NAR-references nuance. None of these are hit by `hello`'s
own attribute shapes -- real but not load-bearing for this milestone's
goal, tracked as a follow-up.

**`derivation.c` rewiring**: `asnix_collect_input_refs` (M74) is extended,
not replaced -- it still recognizes a bare derivation attrset/list
structurally (needed for e.g. `src = a;` where `a` is a derivation
attrset not yet coerced to a string), but now ALSO: (a) reads attached
context off any plain-string leaf it visits (the actual fix -- an
interpolated `builder` string, by the time it reaches here, carries its
`Built(bash's drvPath, "out")` ref from M76's propagation above, with no
structure left to inspect), and (b) recurses into a GENERIC (non-
derivation-shaped) attrset's own nested attribute values too, instead of
treating it as a dead end. (b) was found necessary, not just thorough-for-
its-own-sake: confirmed directly that real `hello.drv` itself uses
`__structuredAttrs = true;`, whose non-special attributes bypass the
normal string-coercion call entirely and reach this collector only as a
raw, uncoerced Value -- matching real Nix's own JSON serializer
(`printValueAsJSON`), which performs the identical recursive walk to
collect context from a structured-attrs blob.

**Found and fixed in the same verification pass, not string-context
itself but directly blocking the same goal**: `__ignoreNulls = true;`
(nixpkgs' `make-derivation.nix` sets this unconditionally) was not
implemented at all -- real Nix's `derivationStrictInternal`
(`~/nix/src/libexpr/primops.cc`) unconditionally skips the
`__ignoreNulls` attribute itself (regardless of its own value or
`__structuredAttrs` mode) and additionally skips every OTHER attribute
whose forced value is `null` when the flag is set. Confirmed directly:
real `hello.drv`'s own `__json` blob has neither `__ignoreNulls` nor
`userHook` (a null-valued attribute nixpkgs sets) at all; asnix previously
emitted both verbatim, a second, independent source of `__json` byte
mismatch on top of the missing `bash` inputDrv.

Verified against real `nix-instantiate --eval --strict`: the exact
`hello`-shaped pattern (`builder = "${a}/bin/sh";`, a derivation reference
reaching `derivation {...}` ONLY through a prior string interpolation,
never as a bare attrset) and a `+`-concatenated variant both match
exactly (`tests/e2e/m76_interp_dep.nix`/`m76_plus_dep.nix`); all 5 of
M74's own verification fixtures re-verified unchanged (the context-based
collection produces IDENTICAL results to the old structural-only walk for
every case it already handled).

**Re-ran `d.nix`**: `hello.outPath` still does NOT match real Nix
bit-for-bit, but the gap changed character entirely. Before this
milestone: 3 of 4 expected `inputDrvs` (missing `bash`), and the `__json`
blob had 2 extra keys real Nix's doesn't. After: all 4 `inputDrvs` present
(sorted correctly), identical `inputSrcs`, and the `__json` blob now has
the EXACT SAME KEY SET as real Nix's (confirmed by direct comparison,
key-by-key) -- every remaining difference is a VALUE mismatch for keys
whose values are themselves derived from upstream packages (`bash`,
`stdenv-linux`, `version-check-hook`, the fetched source tarball) not yet
matching real Nix's own hashes. Dumping real `bash-5.3p15.drv` directly
found it has its OWN 21 `inputDrvs` (`bootstrap-stage4-gcc-wrapper`,
`bootstrap-stage4-stdenv-linux`, `bison`, 15 individual patch derivations,
...) -- this is the full nixpkgs bootstrap chain, not a leaf. Reaching bit-
exact `hello.outPath` parity means reaching bit-exact parity for every
package in that chain, an open-ended, much larger undertaking than any
single milestone so far -- explicitly flagged to the user as such rather
than silently continuing into it; tracked as a separate, indefinite
follow-up to the standing `d.nix` bug-chase, not a blocker on this
milestone's own (verified, scoped) completion.

`make test`/`test-e2e` green (2 new `m76_*` fixtures, each verified
byte-for-byte against real `nix-instantiate --eval --strict` before being
written). `make test-nix-conformance`: `pass=628 fail=30 skip=148` --
unchanged from M75 (this corpus doesn't exercise multi-derivation
hashing), zero regressions.

## M77 scope notes: a real-nixpkgs correctness regression test, plus two bugs it found

The user pointed out, correctly, that M58-M76's entire `d.nix` bug-chase
had zero automated regression coverage of its own actual target --
`hello.outPath` parity against real Nix -- only small, synthetic,
hand-written fixtures (`tests/e2e/m74_input_*`/`m75_*`/`m76_*`). Every
check against the real target was a one-off manual `nix-instantiate`
comparison, re-done by hand each session, with no way to notice a
regression (or measure forward progress) automatically.

New `make test-nixpkgs-hash` (`tests/nixpkgs-hash/attrs.txt` +
`pkgs.nix`): for every nixpkgs attribute path listed, checks
`.outPath`/`.drvPath` byte-for-byte against real `nix-instantiate --eval
--strict`, using `-A` (both tools already support dotted attribute-path
selection -- `main.c`'s own `select_attrpath`, added for exactly this
kind of use, ported from real Nix's own `-A`). Deliberately
**non-gating**, same convention as `test-nix-conformance`: this corpus
is EXPECTED to have real failures for a long time (the standing bug-chase
being open-ended), so a hard-fail-the-build gate would make the target
useless the moment any single upstream package doesn't fully match --
reports pass/fail, a crash and a hash MISMATCH both counted as failures
but labeled distinctly (`(crash)`/`(mismatch)`), a real-Nix eval failure
for a listed attribute silently skipped (typo/doesn't-exist, not an
asnix correctness question).

Building the corpus immediately found two real, fixable bugs, both
before even reaching the harness's final form:

1. **`builtins.toFile`'s result never carried its own store-path as
   context.** `hello.src.drvPath` didn't match real Nix even though
   `hello.src.outPath` did and `hello.src` is a near-leaf fixed-output
   derivation (not deep in the bootstrap chain) -- diffing asnix's own
   computed ATerm against real `hello-2.12.3.tar.gz.drv` found asnix's
   `inputSrcs` was missing a `mirrors-list` entry that WAS correctly
   present (same computed path!) inside the `__json` blob's
   `mirrorsListFile` field. Root cause: `<nix/fetchurl.nix>`'s own
   `mirrorsListFile = toFile "mirrors-list" (...)`-- real Nix's
   `builtins.toFile` (`mkStorePathString`, `~/nix/src/libexpr/eval.cc`)
   attaches `Opaque(selfStorePath)` as the RESULT string's own context
   (NOT forwarded from its `contents` argument, a separate, still-
   unimplemented nuance -- see `prim_toFile`'s own header comment);
   `asnix`'s M45-era `prim_toFile` never attached any context to its
   result at all, so by the time this path reached M76's
   `asnix_collect_input_refs`, it was already an opaque string with no
   trace of being a store reference. Fixed by attaching the same
   `Opaque(out_path)` context `asnix_prim_derivation`'s own M76 origin
   point already does. Verified: `hello.src.drvPath`'s `inputDrvs`/
   `inputSrcs`/`__json` now match real Nix's shape exactly (output
   PATHS still differ -- `bash`/`curl`/`stdenv-linux-no-cc` are
   themselves unresolved bootstrap-chain packages, expected).
2. **`curl.outPath` crashes** (`concatStringsSep: expected a string
   argument`, confirmed via gdb to be a bare ~93-attribute derivation-
   shaped attrset reaching `concatStringsSep` where real Nix would have
   a plain string) -- traced to `pkgs/stdenv/generic/problems.nix`'s
   meta-validation machinery (`concatMapStringsSep ", " (el: el.name)
   kindGroup`-shaped code), several layers into nixpkgs' own
   `checkMeta`/problem-reporting system. NOT root-caused or fixed this
   milestone -- registered in the new corpus as a known-failing
   `(crash)` case instead of silently working around or hiding it,
   since making it VISIBLE or, is the entire point of this milestone;
   a real, separate bug to chase as its own follow-up.

Current `make test-nixpkgs-hash` baseline: `pass=1 fail=7` (`hello`,
`hello.src`, `bash`, `curl`, each `.outPath`/`.drvPath` --
`hello.src.outPath` is the only pass; everything else is either a
genuine upstream-bootstrap-chain hash mismatch, already expected and
documented in M76's own scope notes, or `curl`'s crash above). This
number is the actual, truthful state of the standing bug-chase's own
goal -- expected to only improve from here as the bootstrap-chain work
continues, and any future regression in what little passes now will be
caught immediately instead of discovered by accident.

`make test`/`test-e2e`/`test-conformance`/`test-nix-conformance` all
green, zero regressions (the new target is additive and non-gating).

## M78: `asnix_apply`/`asnix_eval` never-free scratch-buffer waste (memory)

Following up a direct question ("memory usage seems high compared to
`nix eval`"): measured `./asnix d.nix`'s peak RSS at 226 MB vs. real
`nix-instantiate`/`nix eval`'s ~125 MB (~1.8x). Root cause confirmed via
`asnix_arena`'s own `total_allocated` counter (`include/asnix/arena.h`):
4.69 GB had been requested from the bump arena over the course of one
evaluation, vs. only 226 MB of that ever actually becoming resident
(RSS) -- the gap is virtual-address-space waste from mmap'd-but-never-
written pages (anonymous mmap is lazily committed; "allocated" via the
bump pointer is not the same as "physically touched"), harmless to the
OS on its own, but a strong signal that something is requesting far
more than it uses.

Found two instances of the exact pattern M74's own perf fix
(`perf: cache asnix_force_for_print's scratch buffers per recursion
depth`, this session, src/asm/force.S) had already fixed for
`asnix_force_for_print`, just never applied to its two siblings:
`src/asm/apply.S`'s `asnix_apply` (the re-entrant "call this Value from
C" entry point `map`/`filter`/`foldl'`/etc. use) and `src/asm/
dispatch.S`'s `asnix_eval` itself (the MAIN entry point, re-entered
fresh for every `import` of an uncached file, per `eval_file.c`) were
both still minting a brand-new VALSTACK+RETSTACK pair from the
never-free arena on EVERY call -- `asnix_apply`'s own header comment
even says so explicitly ("own fresh VALSTACK+RETSP via
asnix_arena_alloc ... modeled closely on asnix_force_for_print's self-
contained-dispatch-context pattern"), written before that pattern's own
inefficiency was known.

**Fix**: the identical per-depth-cache treatment, extended to both
(`force_scratch.c`/`.h` gained two more independent depth-keyed caches --
`asnix_apply_scratch_*`/`asnix_eval_scratch_*`, each with its OWN depth
counter, `asnix_apply_depth`/`asnix_eval_depth`, deliberately NOT shared
with `asnix_force_depth` or each other, matching each call site's own
existing "never shared with whatever else might be active" header
comment). `asnix_eval`'s own buffers (8 MiB + 2 MiB, 10x
force/apply's 256 KiB + 64 KiB each) turned out to matter far more:
a full nixpkgs evaluation imports hundreds of distinct files, each
previously paying this cost fresh.

Safety argument identical to M74's own fix: VALSTACK/RETSTACK are pure
scratch space for ONE evaluation's active execution -- the eventual
"result" is always an 8-byte `Value` word copied out into a register
(`asnix_op_halt`'s `movq (%r12), %rax`), never a pointer lingering INTO
the stack itself (actual heap data -- strings, lists, attrsets -- lives
in separate arena allocations the stack only ever points AT), and depth
is strictly LIFO (single-threaded, nesting only ever happens via the
native C call stack returning before a shallower depth's slot could be
reused) -- the same two invariants that already made the force.S fix
safe apply unchanged here.

Verified: `asnix_arena.total_allocated` evaluating `d.nix` went
4.69 GB -> 2.5 GB (`asnix_apply`'s fix alone) -> 151 MB (`asnix_eval`'s
fix on top) -- a ~97% reduction, essentially eliminating the
virtual-memory waste entirely. Peak RSS: 226 MB -> 171 MB (`apply`) ->
169 MB (`eval`, no further RSS change expected or seen, since the
remaining waste was already almost entirely unwritten pages) -- net
~25% real memory reduction, narrowing the gap to real Nix from ~1.8x to
~1.35x. The residual gap is the expected, accepted cost of this
project's "never free anything" bump-arena design (no GC at all, by
design) -- not something this milestone attempts to close further.

`make test`/`test-e2e`/`test-conformance`/`test-nix-conformance`/
`test-nixpkgs-hash` all identical to the pre-fix baseline (same
628/30/148, same nixpkgs-hash pass=1/fail=7 with the exact same 7
failures) -- zero behavioral change, confirming the two new caches are
correctness-preserving, matching every expectation the safety argument
above already set.

## M79 scope notes: `d.nix`/`e.nix` reach bit-exact parity with real Nix

The standing bug-chase's own goal, set back when M72 only achieved
"evaluates without crashing" and the user pushed back ("We don't
reproduce the same value"), is now met: `./asnix d.nix`
(`hello.outPath`) and `./asnix e.nix` (`hello.drvPath`) both match real
`nix-instantiate --eval --strict`'s output on the real nixpkgs checkout
byte-for-byte, confirmed directly.

Three background investigations, each independently chasing a
different symptom of the same underlying class of bug (a Nix-level
value's dependency provenance getting silently dropped somewhere
between being produced and being read back by `derivation.c`'s M74/M76
collection machinery), converged on three real, distinct asnix fixes
that only together closed the whole remaining gap:

1. **`concatStringsSep` dropped string context entirely, and required
   every element to already be a bare string.** `lib.makeBinPath`/
   `lib.makeSearchPath` (nixpkgs-level, `concatStringsSep ":" (map (p:
   "${p}/bin") pkgs)`) is exactly how a bootstrap derivation's `PATH`
   env var gets built -- without context propagation through this
   function, every referenced derivation silently vanished from
   `InputDrvs` (confirmed: asnix's own `bootstrap-coreutils-5.0.drv`
   had only 2 of the real 7 entries, the missing 5 appearing only
   inside its `PATH` var's joined string). Separately, `curl`'s build
   passes a bare derivation attrset (not yet string-coerced) into a
   `concatStringsSep` call, which the function's own stricter
   `as_string` helper fataled on. Fixed by coercing each element the
   same way genuine `"${...}"` interpolation would (new
   `asnix_coerce_to_string_for_concat_sep`, matching real Nix's
   `prim_concatStringsSep`'s own `coerceToString` call exactly) AND
   unioning each coerced element's context into the joined result.
2. **The `+` operator's `copyToStore` was wrongly tied to
   `check_path_exists`.** Real Nix's `ExprConcatStrings::eval`
   (`~/nix/src/libexpr/eval.cc`) ties `copyToStore` to whether the
   WHOLE `+`-chain's first operand was a string (`firstType ==
   nString`), completely independent of the existence-check gating --
   confirmed directly against real Nix's own source. A `+` chain
   starting with a string (e.g. nixpkgs's own `minimal-bootstrap/mes/
   libc.nix`: `libc_gnu1_SOURCES + " " + ./ldexpl.c`) DOES copy a later
   Path operand to the store and attach its context; asnix previously
   never did this for `+` at all. Split `coerce_to_string_for_interp`'s
   single flag into two independent ones.
3. **`builtins.toJSON`'s Path handling never copied to the store.** A
   known, documented gap since M8/M15 (before this project had any
   `AddToStore` infrastructure at all) that M75 fixed for every OTHER
   coercion call site but missed this one. `bash-interactive`'s own
   `__structuredAttrs`-mode derivation embeds raw Path literals
   (`separate-debug-info.sh`, `pgrp-pipe-5.patch`) straight into its
   `__json` env var via this encoder, silently rotating its hash even
   though `inputSrcs` (collected separately, from the raw attribute
   Values) already had the correctly-copied paths.

Each was found and verified independently (in isolated worktrees,
against real `nix-instantiate --eval --strict`, with `make test`/
`test-e2e` green throughout) -- the key insight tying them together is
that NONE of them alone fully explained `hello`'s own remaining
mismatch, but merging all three onto the same tree did, since the
bootstrap chain's dependency graph exercises all three gaps
simultaneously across its ~30+ packages.

`make test-nixpkgs-hash`: `pass=1 fail=7` (baseline before this
milestone) → **`pass=8 fail=0`** -- every attribute path in the corpus
(`hello`, `hello.src`, `bash`, `curl`, `.outPath`/`.drvPath` each) now
matches real Nix exactly. `make test`/`test-e2e`/`test-conformance`/
`test-nix-conformance` all green, zero regressions.
## M80: right-sizing the M78 scratch buffers against a real measurement

M78 fixed the *never-free-a-fresh-buffer-per-call* waste by caching one
VALSTACK+RETSTACK pair per recursion depth, but left the per-buffer
SIZES themselves exactly as they'd always been -- round-number guesses
(`asnix_eval`: 8 MiB VALSTACK / 2 MiB RETSTACK; `asnix_apply`/
`asnix_force_for_print`: 256 KiB / 64 KiB each) never checked against
real usage. This milestone measures the real high-water mark each kind
reaches and shrinks the constants with a safety margin, instead of
guessing a second time -- and, after two real-world cross-checks each
caught the measurement under-selling the true requirement, ends up only
shrinking `asnix_eval`'s own buffers, leaving `asnix_apply`/
`asnix_force_for_print` at their original sizes.

**Measurement method**: temporary instrumentation (not committed --
added, measured, then fully reverted), guarded by a `-DASNIX_HWM_DEBUG`
build flag so it never touches a normal build. Three pieces, since every
VALSTACK/RETSP push in this codebase funnels through
`include/asnix/stackcheck.h`'s `ASNIX_CHECK_VALSTACK`/`ASNIX_CHECK_RETSP`
macros (the one choke point shared by all three dispatch contexts):
(1) three new globals (`asnix_hwm_kind`, `asnix_hwm_valstack_base`,
`asnix_hwm_retstack_base`) set/restored at each of
`dispatch.S`/`apply.S`/`force.S`'s own entry and exit points, exactly
mirroring the existing `asnix_valstack_limit`/`asnix_retsp_limit`
save/restore discipline those files already have (same reasoning: each
context can run nested inside another); (2) the two check macros,
extended to call a small helper (`asnix_hwm_track`) that computes
`current_pointer - base` and keeps a running max per kind (eval=0/
apply=1/force=2); (3) a print at `main`'s exit. Two real bugs surfaced
and were fixed *in the instrumentation itself* before it produced
trustworthy numbers (both reverted along with everything else,
documented here so a future attempt doesn't repeat them):
- The entry-point save blocks push an odd number of extra qwords (3:
  kind/valstack_base/retstack_base), breaking the carefully-maintained
  16-byte stack alignment every `call` mid-dispatch relies on --
  segfaulted inside unrelated libc code (`asnix_lex`) the instant any
  op handler made a `call` after the push. Fixed by padding to 4 qwords.
- `builtins.tryEval`'s `longjmp` catch path (`src/c/builtins_tryeval.c`)
  already has to explicitly save/restore `asnix_valstack_limit`/
  `asnix_retsp_limit` around its `setjmp`, with a comment explaining
  exactly why: a caught `throw`/`assert` skips the normal epilogue that
  would otherwise restore them. The new debug globals needed the
  identical explicit save/restore, or a caught exception permanently
  left `asnix_hwm_valstack_base` pointing at the abandoned nested
  force's buffer -- the next check anywhere computed a bogus huge
  distance from that stale base and permanently poisoned that kind's
  running max (observed directly: one single reading of 16 MB that
  never moved again, traced via a conditional breakpoint to a
  `prim_tryEval` frame on the stack).

**Measured peaks**, running `./asnix -A <attr>.<outPath|drvPath>
tests/nixpkgs-hash/pkgs.nix` against real nixpkgs for `hello`,
`hello.src`, `bash`, `gcc`, and `stdenv` (chosen for dependency-chain
diversity; `curl`/`ffmpeg` already fail for unrelated pre-existing
reasons, see `test-nixpkgs-hash`'s own known failures):

| kind  | valstack max | retstack max | old size (V/R)  |
|-------|-------------:|-------------:|-----------------|
| eval  | 28,944 B     | 5,312 B      | 8 MiB / 2 MiB   |
| apply | 352 B        | 864 B        | 256 KiB / 64 KiB|
| force | 1,680 B      | 960 B        | 256 KiB / 64 KiB|

Every attribute/field combination produced *identical* numbers --
strong evidence the measurement is dominated by the shared nixpkgs/lib/
overlay bootstrap common to all of them, not the specific package, but
also a strong signal (confirmed twice over, below) that five packages'
worth of measurement doesn't exercise every real usage pattern.

**Cross-check #1 -- VALSTACK, caught by this project's own test suite**:
the first attempt shrank ALL FOUR buffer pairs using only the table
above (e.g. `asnix_apply`/`asnix_force_for_print`'s VALSTACK: 256 KiB ->
64 KiB, a ~40x margin over the 1,680-byte measured peak). `make
test-e2e` immediately caught a real regression: `tests/e2e/
m9_large_list.nix` (a literal 15,000-element list passed straight to
`builtins.length`, a deliberate M9-era stress test for VALSTACK/RETSP's
bounds check -- see that milestone's "Known bugs" entry) failed with a
genuine `asnix: value stack overflow` abort. Root cause: `op_call.S`'s
primop-call path forces every argument via `asnix_force_for_print`
(M25's comment on that call site) *before* handing it to the native C
function -- so a primop argument that's a large literal list/attrset
gets *constructed* (every element's `OP_MK_THUNK` push, replaced by one
`OP_MK_LIST` pop) entirely inside `force.S`'s own nested dispatch
context, using its VALSTACK, not `dispatch.S`'s much larger top-level
one. 15,000 elements at 8 bytes each needs ~120,000 bytes -- far more
than the tiny 1,680-byte peak the five real packages above ever touched
(none of them happens to pass a large literal straight into a primop).
Bisected directly (binary-searching `ASNIX_APPLY_VALSTACK_BYTES`/
`ASNIX_FORCE_VALSTACK_BYTES` with everything else held fixed): 65536
fails, 131072 passes, confirming ~120 KiB is a real hard floor for this
one visible case alone.

**Cross-check #2 -- RETSTACK, caught by comparing against real Nix's
own source**: mid-session, asked directly whether real Nix has an
analogous limit worth emulating. It doesn't have a literal VALSTACK/
RETSTACK pair -- real Nix (`nix-instantiate`/`nix eval`, C++
`libexpr`) is a recursive tree-walking evaluator, not a bytecode-VM
with an explicit operand/call-frame stack; every `Expr::eval` call and
every intermediate `Value` lives directly on the native C++ call stack.
But it has two closely analogous, deliberately-chosen limits, confirmed
directly from a local checkout of the real Nix source
(`/home/tbereknyei/gnix/nix`, not from memory):
- `src/libexpr/eval.cc`'s `EvalState` constructor calls
  `nix::ensureStackSizeAtLeast(60 * 1024 * 1024)` once per process --
  real Nix bumps its OWN native stack (`setrlimit(RLIMIT_STACK, ...)`,
  `src/libutil/unix/current-process.cc`) to 60 MiB specifically because
  the default OS stack (commonly 8 MiB) isn't enough for its own
  recursive evaluation style. This is the rough analog of asnix's
  *combined* VALSTACK+RETSTACK budget (both serve the same underlying
  purpose -- bounding how deep/wide one evaluation can recurse/branch
  before something has to give -- just split into two separate
  explicit heap buffers in asnix's bytecode-VM design instead of one
  native stack).
  - `src/libexpr/include/nix/expr/eval-settings.hh`'s `maxCallDepth`
  `Setting<unsigned int>` defaults the `max-call-depth` nix.conf option
  to **10,000** function calls -- a deliberately *friendlier*,
  explicit-counter guard (`EvalState::addCallDepth`/`callDepth`,
  `eval-inline.hh`) that fires well before the 60 MiB native stack
  would actually be exhausted, so a deeply-recursive (or infinitely
  recursive) Nix program gets a clean `StackOverflowError` instead of a
  SIGSEGV. `print.cc`/`print-ambiguous.cc` reuse the same
  `maxCallDepth` setting to bound recursive *printing* depth too (the
  direct analog of asnix's own `force.S`-driven nested-value forcing).
  Notably, ordinary thunk-forcing (`EvalState::forceValue`'s
  `expr->eval(...)` call for a plain, non-`App` thunk) does NOT
  increment `callDepth` at all -- only actual function applications
  do -- so a long `let`-chain of dependent bindings is bounded only by
  the raw 60 MiB stack, not the friendlier 10,000 counter; a nuance
  that didn't change anything here but is worth knowing before trusting
  `max-call-depth` as a universal proxy for "how deep can recursion go."

  This directly exposed a problem with the first attempt's RETSTACK
  numbers: `asnix_eval`'s own RETSTACK (meant to hold ordinary
  in-language `OP_CALL` recursion -- the same role `maxCallDepth`
  plays) had been shrunk to 8,192 call frames, which is *smaller* than
  real Nix's own 10,000-call default -- meaning a real, deeply recursive
  Nix program real Nix would accept right up to its own configured
  limit could now get rejected by asnix with a tighter cap than before
  this milestone (the original 65,536-frame RETSTACK was comfortably
  above 10,000). Separately, `asnix_apply`/`asnix_force_for_print`'s own
  RETSTACK (2,048 frames originally) was ALREADY below Nix's 10,000-call
  guarantee even before this milestone touched anything -- a
  pre-existing gap (deeply recursive user code invoked *through*
  `map`/`filter`/`foldl'`, an entirely ordinary nixpkgs pattern, runs
  its own `OP_CALL` chain against this smaller nested RETSTACK, not
  `asnix_eval`'s) -- and the first attempt's further shrink to 512
  frames would have made that pre-existing gap 4x worse with no
  real-usage evidence it was safe to.

**Final sizes chosen**, after both cross-checks:
- `asnix_eval` (`dispatch.S`'s `ASNIX_VALSTACK_BYTES`/
  `ASNIX_RETSTACK_BYTES`, mirrored in `force_scratch.h`'s
  `ASNIX_EVAL_*_BYTES`): VALSTACK 8 MiB -> **1 MiB** (131,072 Values,
  >35x margin over the 28,944-byte measured peak, independently
  confirmed to still hold `m9_large_list.nix`'s ~120,000-byte literal
  with >8x headroom); RETSTACK 2 MiB -> **1 MiB** (32,768 call frames,
  sized against real Nix's own 10,000-call `max-call-depth` default
  rather than the 5,312-byte/166-frame measured peak -- >3.2x margin
  over that much better-grounded reference point, still a 2x reduction
  from the original).
- `asnix_apply`/`asnix_force_for_print`: **left at their original
  sizes** (256 KiB VALSTACK / 64 KiB RETSTACK each) -- both
  cross-checks above landed on this same context, and with no
  real-usage evidence covering either failure mode (large literals
  passed to primops; deep recursion inside a `map`/`filter`/`foldl'`
  callback), shrinking either further wasn't defensible this
  milestone.

**Verification**: `make test`/`test-e2e`/`test-conformance` all green;
`make test-nix-conformance` pass=628/fail=30/skip=148, identical to the
pre-change baseline (confirmed across repeated runs -- the corpus has a
`timeout 10`-per-file ceiling that occasionally flakes under system load
regardless of this change, reproduced identically on the unmodified
baseline too); `make test-nixpkgs-hash` pass=1/fail=7 with the exact
same 7 failures as baseline. `./asnix d.nix`/`./asnix e.nix`
(`hello.outPath`/`hello.drvPath`) byte-identical to their pre-change
output; `tests/e2e/m9_large_list.nix`/`m9_large_attrset.nix`/
`m9_deep_let_chain.nix` (the project's own existing stress tests for
exactly these buffers) all still pass.

**Memory impact**: `asnix_arena.total_allocated` evaluating `d.nix`
(`hello.outPath`): 151 MB -> **126 MB** (~17% reduction) -- a real cut
to the virtual-allocation footprint, smaller than the first (reverted)
attempt's ~24% since only `asnix_eval`'s own buffers shrank in the end.
Peak RSS (`/usr/bin/time -v`) and `/proc/<pid>/smaps_rollup`'s
`Rss`/`Pss_Anon` (same gdb-breakpoint-then-`shell sleep`-then-read-
from-another-shell technique M78 used), however, showed **no
measurable change** for this specific workload: ~169,080 KiB -> ~169,224
KiB RSS, within noise. This matches M78's own precedent exactly ("no
further RSS change expected or seen, since the remaining waste was
already almost entirely unwritten pages"): `hello.outPath` only ever
reaches a handful of distinct recursion depths (consistent with the
tiny measured peaks above), so most of the *old*, larger per-depth
buffers were already virtual/untouched rather than resident --
shrinking them reduces bookkeeping and address-space reservation, not
pages that were actually costing real memory for *this* shallow
workload. A deeper/wider real evaluation that touches many more
distinct depths (more nested `import`s specifically, since that's the
one buffer kind that did shrink) would be expected to show a more
visible RSS win from this change, proportional to how many of those
per-depth slots actually get written into; not independently
re-measured here beyond `d.nix`/`e.nix` and the full test suite.

**Confidence caveat** (per this project's own stated preference for a
conservative, honest partial win over an aggressive unverified one):
this milestone's real deliverable ended up being narrower than its
starting goal -- only `asnix_eval` shrank, and even that was corrected
mid-session once real Nix's own `max-call-depth` reference exposed the
first RETSTACK number as too aggressive. `asnix_apply`/
`asnix_force_for_print` are UNCHANGED from before this milestone,
including the pre-existing (not newly introduced) gap where their own
RETSTACK (2,048 frames) is already smaller than real Nix's 10,000-call
default -- a real, narrow limitation this milestone surfaced but didn't
fix, left as-is because fixing it defensibly would need either a wider
real-usage sample than five packages or a deliberate decision to just
match real Nix's number outright, neither of which this session did.

## M81: nix-conformance sweep -- 7 parallel fixes merged

Seven background agents each independently triaged a disjoint slice of
`numtide/nix-conformance`'s remaining failures in isolated worktrees;
their changes were merged into one tree, resolving overlaps by hand
where two agents touched the same function (builtins_shared.c's
curry-stage marker, main.c's printer, derivation.c's per-attribute
loop, and -- the one real design conflict -- `builtins.path`, where
two independent full implementations existed and the more complete one
(context-aware, with `filterSource`, reusing M73's
`asnix_compute_fixed_output_path` formula) was kept and extended with
the other's base32/"nix32" `sha256` decoding to satisfy both agents'
target fixtures). `make test-nix-conformance`: `pass=628 fail=30
skip=148` before this sweep -> see the commit history immediately
below this section for the exact final count. `make test-nixpkgs-hash`
stayed `pass=8 fail=0` throughout -- none of these fixes touch
`derivation.c`'s hash-computation path in an incompatible way (the one
`derivation.c` change that's new, the literal `__json` attribute's
parse+renormalize step and the `drvPath` self-referential `DrvDeep`
context tag, are both additive and don't affect `asnix_collect_input_
refs` or the ATerm serialization any existing fixed-output/hash-parity
test depends on).

Six genuine fixes landed:

1. **Real string-context introspection** -- `getContext`/
   `appendContext`/`addDrvOutputDependencies`/
   `unsafeDiscardOutputDependency`/`hasContext` (ported from Nix's
   `context.cc`), context propagation added to `baseNameOf`/`dirOf`/
   `substring`/`replaceStrings`/`toJSON`, a third context kind
   (`DrvDeep`, "allOutputs") attached to a derivation's own `drvPath`,
   `${...}` dynamic attribute names rejecting string context, and
   `builtins.toFile` rejecting non-opaque context while folding opaque
   references into its own store-path formula. New `builtins.path`/
   `builtins.filterSource` (previously entirely absent), accepting
   `sha256` in either hex or nix32 form. New bare-URL-literal lexing
   (`http://example.com`), ported from Nix's own `lexer.l` URI regex,
   including its `x:x+1`-lexes-as-a-URL footgun.
   **Left out of scope (at the time):** `eval-okay-context-inputs.nix`'s
   `drvPath` case needs a real store-reference-graph + transitive-
   closure walk (`computeFSClosure`) this codebase doesn't have --
   **fixed in M86** via two in-memory closure/output-name caches
   substituting for a real on-disk store walk; `both` turned out to
   already be passing at the time M86 re-checked it, so the pairing
   with `drvPath` here was itself stale.
2. **`==`/`!=` own direct operands never pointer-hack-equal two
   functions** -- real Nix's `ExprOpEq::eval` always fresh-copies its
   own two operands, so two function values are never `==` at that
   level even `let f = x: x; in f == f`.
   **Left out of scope:** the `maybeThunk` slot-identity-sharing cases
   (`eval-okay-eq-slot-elem/identity.nix`) need a real identity-bearing
   allocation layer this codebase's flat `Value` representation
   doesn't have -- re-investigated in M86 and reconfirmed with a
   sharper counterexample (`id id`'s own self-returned closure), see
   that milestone's own notes.
3. **Printer distinguishes `<PRIMOP>`/`<PRIMOP-APP>`/`<LAMBDA>`** for
   multi-arg native builtins, via one shared canonical marker `Value`
   every native-currying constructor stamps into its `Closure`'s
   `OFF_FORMALS` field.
4. **`inherit (expr) a b;` evaluates `expr` once, shared** (a new
   synthetic hidden `AstBinding`, filtered out of the compiled
   attrset), the pretty-printer's ATTRS `«repeated»` dedup is now
   whole-print-call scoped (matching real Nix's `printAttrs`) instead
   of ancestor-only, `__curPos` is a real non-shadowable special form,
   and `unsafeGetAttrPos` on a native builtin returns `null`.
   **Left out of scope:** per-attribute/per-formal source positions
   (`eval-okay-getattrpos*.nix`, `eval-okay-inherit-attr-pos.nix`) need
   runtime `Attr`/`AstFormal` growth across every attrs-producing op.
5. **`derivation {...}`'s literal `__json` attribute** is now parsed
   and re-dumped in normalized form (sorted keys, shortest-roundtrip
   numbers, last-wins duplicate keys) instead of stored verbatim,
   matching real Nix's `StructuredAttrs::parse`/`unparse`. Also fixed a
   pre-existing duplicate-key bug in the JSON parser's object handling.
6. **Regex engine rejects two obscure POSIX collating-symbol forms**
   libstdc++'s `std::regex(extended)` rejects but glibc's `regcomp`
   accepts: a non-alphabetic single-character `[.name.]`, and any
   collating symbol used as a range's high endpoint.

Also left out of scope by the agents, confirmed rather than assumed,
and not revisited during the merge: `eval-okay-print.nix`'s
self-referential-list `«repeated»`-nesting-depth gap,
`eval-okay-tryeval-failed-thunk-reeval.nix` (thunk-failure memoization),
`eval-fail-fromTOML-timestamps.nix` (a real-Nix build-time library
quirk, not a language fact -- "fixing" it would regress asnix's own
already-correct TOML date support), and `(a){24998}`-shaped regex
inputs real Nix rejects via libstdc++'s internal NFA-state-count limit
with no equivalent signal in glibc's `regcomp` to repurpose.

## M82: real `builtins.fetchGit` -- `./asnix d.nix` now runs to completion

Picking back up `d.nix` (`let a = /home/tbereknyei/nixpkgs/default.nix; in
(import a {}).ffmpeg.outPath`) after M81: it had progressed from
crashing immediately all the way to `asnix: undefined variable
'fetchGit'`, reached transitively through ffmpeg's rust-toolchain
dependency chain (`sphinx`/`requests`/`charset-normalizer`/
`ast-serialize`/`cargo`/`rustc`/`llvmPackages`) into
`pkgs/build-support/rust/import-cargo-lock.nix`, which references the
bare top-level `fetchGit` builtin -- real Nix provides it, asnix didn't
implement it at all (`fetchTarball`/`fetchGit`/`fetchMercurial`/
`fetchTree`/`fetchFinalTree` were all still-documented gaps as of
builtins.h's own "not yet implemented at all" list).

**The actual root cause was narrower than it looked.** Reading
`import-cargo-lock.nix` line-by-line: the only `fetchGit` call site is

```nix
else if allowBuiltinFetchGit then
  fetchGit { inherit (gitParts) url; rev = gitParts.sha; allRefs = true; submodules = true; }
else
  missingHash;
```

with `allowBuiltinFetchGit ? false` -- and grepping all of
`/home/tbereknyei/nixpkgs` for `allowBuiltinFetchGit` turns up no call
site anywhere that ever sets it `true`. So this branch's `fetchGit`
*call* is never actually reached at runtime evaluating
`ffmpeg.outPath` -- the crash was a pure **static name-resolution**
problem: this codebase compiles an entire imported file's whole AST up
front (`compiler.c`'s `compile_expr`, invoked once per file from
`asnix_eval_file`), including BOTH arms of every `if`, and
`compile_expr`'s `AST_VAR` case resolves every free variable against
the static scope chain *at compile time* -- a direct, deliberate port
of real Nix's own `bindVars`, which is equally whole-file/static there.
Real Nix's `bindVars` succeeds on this file because `fetchGit` is one
of its registered bare-global primop names (every `addPrimOp` entry
without a `__` prefix, per the existing M18/M27 "bare globals" rule
documented on `builtins.h`/`compiler.c`); asnix's static scope chain
simply didn't know the name at all, so merely *importing* this file --
which happens for every nixpkgs package that transitively pulls in
Rust's `buildRustPackage` -- failed before any of `allowBuiltinFetchGit`
was ever consulted.

**Fix, in proportion to what's actually needed:** `fetchGit` is now a
real, working builtin (not a stub) -- `src/c/builtins_fetchgit.c`/`.h`
(new), wired into `builtins.c`'s plain `BUILTINS[]` table
(`builtins.fetchGit`) and into `compiler.c`'s `init_builtins_frame`/
`eval_file.c`'s `make_root_env_ex` (bare global `fetchGit`, slot 15 of
what's now a 16-slot root env -- the single source-of-truth site each
already documents for exactly this kind of addition). One small,
purely additive export was needed from `nar.c`/`nar.h`:
`asnix_hash_path_nar_sha256` (NAR-hash a path without also computing
its store path) -- `fetchGit`'s result attrset needs `narHash` AND
`outPath` side by side, and the existing `asnix_copy_path_to_store_ext`
only ever returned the latter; this reuses the exact same file-local
`nar_dump`/hashing machinery rather than threading a new out-parameter
through an already-verified M73/M80 formula. No other change to
`derivation.c`/`value_util.c`/`string_context.c`/the rest of `nar.c`.

Implementation: shells out to a real `git` binary (`popen`/`pclose`,
same "plain external process" category docs/abi.md already describes
for primop calls in general -- there is no git-object-store
implementation in this codebase, and building one would be wildly
disproportionate here) to do a real bare clone of the given
URL/path, resolve `ref`/`rev`/bare-HEAD to a concrete commit (with a
best-effort `git fetch origin <rev>` retry if that rev isn't reachable
from the default clone's fetched branches/tags -- a practical stand-in
for real Nix's `allRefs`-driven "fetch everything", without needing to
replicate libfetchers' exact refspec/cache logic), `git archive`s that
rev (which, as a side effect, gets real Nix's default `exportIgnore`
behavior for free -- `git archive` already honors `export-ignore`
`.gitattributes` entries on its own), then runs the extracted tree
through M75/M80's existing NAR-hash store-copy machinery -- the exact
same formula a fixed-output derivation or `builtins.path` already
uses, so `outPath`/`narHash` are genuinely real, not placeholders.

**Verified directly against `nix-instantiate --eval --strict`**
(network access turned out to work fine in this environment, so this
wasn't a "scope it out, no network" situation) across four cases, all
byte-for-byte identical output including `outPath`/`narHash`:
a local repo with `{ url; ref; }`, the bare-string shorthand
(`fetchGit "/path/to/repo"`), the EXACT shape
`import-cargo-lock.nix`'s own unreachable branch uses (`{ url; rev;
allRefs = true; submodules = true; }`), and a real remote HTTPS GitHub
clone pinned to a specific `rev`. Also checked the original crash
repro directly: `builtins.typeOf (import
.../import-cargo-lock.nix)` now returns `"lambda"` instead of dying
with "undefined variable 'fetchGit'".

**Deliberate, documented scope cuts** (none exercised by anything this
project has actually needed to evaluate -- confirmed by the
"nothing sets `allowBuiltinFetchGit=true`" grep above, so these are
real, narrow gaps, not guesses): `submodules = true` doesn't actually
recurse into/fetch submodule content (the field is echoed back
correctly, matching real Nix's attrset shape, but the hashed tree
itself won't contain real submodule content); local *dirty* working
trees (uncommitted changes, real Nix's empty-sha1 `rev`/`dirtyRev`
fallback) aren't modeled -- every target is treated as a plain clone
and always resolves to a real committed rev; `verifyCommit`/
`publicKeys` signed-commit verification, an explicit `exportIgnore =
false` override, `lfs` smudging, a pinned `narHash`/`lastModified`
argument to skip re-fetching, and flake-ref-shorthand strings
(`"github:..."`) are accepted-and-ignored or simply not special-cased;
unknown attrset keys beyond the handled set are silently accepted
rather than validated against real Nix's fetcher-specific
`allowedAttrs` schema; fetch failures are a plain fatal error, not a
catchable `EvalError`. See `builtins_fetchgit.c`'s own header comment
for the full list.

`make test`/`make test-e2e`: unchanged, all green.
`make test-nix-conformance`: `pass=646 fail=12 skip=148` both before
and after this change (confirmed via a full stash/rebuild/retest
cycle) -- zero regressions, and, as expected, zero fixes either (no
numtide/nix-conformance fixture exercises `fetchGit`).
`make test-nixpkgs-hash`: `pass=8 fail=0`, unchanged.

**`./asnix d.nix` now runs to completion** -- no crash, no hang:

```
"/nix/store/f372whziay4smpsdkvvldaxaf7wj6qlc-ffmpeg-9.0.1-bin"
```

**A new gap surfaced immediately after, as expected going in:** real
`nix-instantiate --eval --strict -E '(import
/home/tbereknyei/nixpkgs/default.nix {}).ffmpeg.outPath'` returns a
*different* store path:

```
"/nix/store/29iacg6h530yx7rxz4k1fhvi0kxxhsam-ffmpeg-9.0.1-bin"
```

Same derivation name/version (`ffmpeg-9.0.1-bin`), different hash --
meaning asnix now evaluates the entire dependency graph far enough to
construct a plausible `ffmpeg` derivation (attribute names, builder
wiring, output naming all shaped correctly), but SOME ancestor
derivation feeding into its `drvPath`/`outPath` hash chain diverges
from real Nix's own computed hash somewhere upstream. This is
confirmed NOT caused by this milestone's own `fetchGit` work --
`fetchGit`'s actual call site is never reached at runtime for this
specific evaluation (see above) -- so the divergence was already
latent, just unreachable before this fix let evaluation run past the
M81 crash point. Not chased down this session: ffmpeg's dependency
closure is large (the rust-toolchain chain alone is five-plus packages
deep), and isolating which single ancestor's hash first diverges needs
a binary-search-style comparison (e.g. walking `drvPath`s of
intermediate derivations in both asnix and real
`nix-instantiate --eval --strict --json` for the same attribute paths)
that's its own multi-step investigation, not a quick follow-up. This
is the next thread to pull on `d.nix`.
## M83: five more nix-conformance fixes -- import-follows-symlink,
tryEval failed-thunk memoization, fromTOML date rejection, and a regex
group-repetition memory limit

Picked up the 5 tractable-looking failures M81's sweep didn't attempt
(`make test-nix-conformance`: `pass=646 fail=12 skip=148` going in).
Result: **`pass=651 fail=7 skip=148`** -- all 5 fixed, zero
regressions (`make test`/`make test-e2e` both stayed green throughout;
`make test-nixpkgs-hash` stayed `pass=8 fail=0`). The remaining 7
failures are exactly M81's already-confirmed-large 7 (`eval-okay-
context-inputs`/`eq-slot-elem`/`eq-slot-identity`/`getattrpos`/
`getattrpos-functionargs`/`inherit-attr-pos`/`print`) -- see M81's own
notes, plus this milestone's own `eval-okay-print.nix` re-confirmation
below.

1. **`eval-okay-import-follows-symlink.nix`** -- real Nix's
   `resolveExprPath` (`eval.cc`) follows a symlink chain on the exact
   literal path handed to `import` itself (not any symlinked
   *directory* component reached along the way -- that's a genuinely
   different rule, M57h's own `eval-okay-symlink-resolution.nix` fix,
   and the two don't conflict: `lstat`/`readlink` only ever inspect the
   FINAL path component, so a regular file reached through a symlinked
   parent directory is untouched by this). Added `follow_symlink_chain`
   (`eval_file.c`) -- an `lstat`+`readlink` loop bounded at 1024 hops,
   mirroring cppnix's own loop exactly -- called from `resolve_file_
   path` after the existing (symlink-blind) lexical canonicalization.
   This also fixed `__curPos.file` for files reached via `import`: it
   used to always report the OUTERMOST file asnix was invoked on (an
   M80-documented approximation) -- now `asnix_compile`/`asnix_compile_
   scoped` take an explicit `file_path` parameter (the resolved path,
   threaded from `eval_file.c`'s own `resolved` variable at each of
   their 3 call sites) instead of calling `asnix_eval_top_level_file()`
   unconditionally, so a `__curPos` token inside an IMPORTED file now
   reports THAT file's own path. (`line`/`column` were already exact,
   M80.) The pre-existing import-value cache (M65, keyed by resolved
   path) needed no changes -- it already gives two imports that resolve
   to the same real file the identical cached `Value`, which is exactly
   what makes the test's second import print `«repeated»` (M80's own
   whole-print-call ATTRS dedup, M81, already keys off this same
   pointer identity) while a `scopedImport` of the same path (which
   intentionally bypasses the cache) prints in full again.

2. **`eval-okay-tryeval-failed-thunk-reeval.nix`** -- "Since Nix 2.34,
   errors are memoized": forcing a thunk whose body already threw once
   must re-raise the SAME failure (catchable again) on a second force,
   not re-run the body (no duplicate side effects) and not blackhole
   (it's not a genuine cycle). `tryeval.h`'s own pre-existing comment
   candidly documented this as a known, unfixed limitation: a `longjmp`
   back to `builtins.tryEval`'s `setjmp` skips every op_*.S/force.S
   epilogue between the throw and the catch, so any thunk that went
   `IN_PROGRESS` in that range stays stuck that way forever -- re-
   forcing it later hit the SAME blackhole guard as a genuine `let x =
   x; in x` cycle, aborting the whole process even inside a `tryEval`.
   Fixed with a new `ASNIX_THUNK_STATE_FAILED` (`ir.h`) plus
   `asnix_inprogress_head` (`stacklimits.S`): an intrusive Thunk*-stack,
   linked through each IN_PROGRESS thunk's own `env` field (dead at that
   point -- already consumed to jump into the body, and not read again
   until FORCED repurposes it for the cached value) -- every site that
   sets IN_PROGRESS (`op_var_ref.S`, `op_with.S`'s `OP_WITH_TRY`,
   `op_select.S`, `op_select_or.S`, `force.S`) pushes itself on; the one
   site that transitions IN_PROGRESS -> FORCED (`op_call.S`'s
   `asnix_op_ret`, which already memoizes every force uniformly
   regardless of which op started it) pops itself back off, since
   forcing nests strictly LIFO under normal completion. `builtins.
   tryEval` (`builtins_tryeval.c`) saves the head before forcing its
   argument and, ONLY on the caught-exception path, walks from the
   live head down to that saved marker (`asnix_tryeval_unwind_
   inprogress`, `tryeval.c`) marking everything in that range FAILED
   instead of leaving it IN_PROGRESS -- this correctly leaves an OUTER,
   still-legitimately-in-progress force (e.g. a `tryEval` called from
   within another thunk's own forcing) completely untouched, since that
   range is strictly ABOVE the saved marker. Each op's own `IN_PROGRESS`
   check gained a sibling `FAILED` check that re-raises
   (`asnix_tryeval_raise_or_fatal`) instead of either re-running or
   blackholing. Also restored `asnix_force_depth` (same "longjmp skips
   the epilogue" root cause, harmless for correctness but wasteful --
   `force_scratch.c`'s per-depth buffer cache would otherwise never
   reuse a lower depth again after any caught exception). Found via
   `gdb`: an EARLIER version of this fix (push-only, no pop) corrupted
   the intrusive list the very first time any UNRELATED thunk finished
   successfully while still linked on it -- `asnix_op_ret` must pop on
   every successful completion, not just leave failed ones to be
   cleaned up reactively, or the next, unrelated `tryEval` catch walks
   into a `prev` pointer that's actually a stale cached Value and
   segfaults.

3. **`eval-fail-fromTOML-timestamps.nix`** -- M81's merge notes claimed
   "fixing" this would regress asnix's "already-correct" TOML date
   support (M23/M51). Re-checked directly: EVERY TOML date/time literal
   (`builtins.fromTOML "x = 1979-05-27T07:32:00Z"`, and every other
   shape in `corpora/toml.nix`'s own `times` list) makes the
   `nix-instantiate` actually installed in this environment
   (Determinate Nix 3.22.5 / Nix 2.35.2) throw `error: while parsing
   TOML: Dates and times are not supported`, unconditionally -- a real
   behavior difference from whatever older Nix generated `lang/eval-
   okay-fromTOML-062..076.exp` (M23's claim was correct for ITS time,
   not a mistake). Crucially, ALL 77 `lang/eval-okay-fromTOML-*.nix`
   files -- including every one of -062..-076 and the exhaustive
   `-timestamps` file -- carry their own `.flags` sidecar, so `test-
   nix-conformance` skips every single one: nothing currently SCORED
   depends on dates succeeding, so M81's stated regression risk doesn't
   actually exist. `classify_date_or_time` (`toml.c`) now calls
   `toml_fatal("Dates and times are not supported")` (same message,
   same fatal-exit convention floats/`inf`/`nan` already use) once a
   date/time token is validated as syntactically well-formed, instead
   of returning a `{ _type = "timestamp"; ...}` attrset --
   `make_timestamp_value` is kept (dead code, `(void)`-cast) rather than
   deleted, in case a future milestone needs to special-case a specific
   shape once proven the installed Nix still accepts it.

4. **`eval-fail-regex-invalid-034-match.nix`/`-split.nix`** (one fix,
