   as expected) -- `(a){24998}`: a capture GROUP repeated this many
   times trips libstdc++ `std::regex`'s internal NFA-state-count limit
   ("memory limit exceeded"), well below glibc's own `regcomp` limit
   (which still accepts it -- unlike flat `a{99994}`-shaped bare
   repetition, which asnix already rejects "for free" since regcomp's
   OWN limit happens to trip at a nearby count). Binary-searched the
   real boundary directly (`nix-instantiate --eval --strict -E
   'builtins.match "(a){N}" "aaa"'`): accepted through exactly N=24997,
   rejected at N=24998. Reproducing libstdc++'s exact internal state-
   cost accounting for an arbitrary group body (a costlier body trips
   at a LOWER N) is genuinely out of scope, as M81 concluded -- but
   fixing just this one, real, already-known boundary doesn't require
   that: `group_repeat_bound_too_large` (`builtins_regex.c`) rejects any
   `(...)` capture group immediately followed by a `{m}`/`{m,}`/`{m,n}`
   interval whose bound exceeds `ASNIX_GROUP_REPEAT_SAFE_MAX` (1000) --
   comfortably above every group-repetition count anywhere in numtide/
   nix-conformance's corpora (`corpora/regex.nix`'s own cases top out at
   `{1,3}`) and comfortably below the real ~24998 limit, so it can't
   misclassify anything currently exercised either way. A conservative
   approximation of real Nix's actual limit, deliberately not a
   faithful reproduction of it.

**Left out of scope, re-confirmed (not re-attempted further):**
`eval-okay-print.nix`'s self-referential-list `«repeated»`-printing
depth (`let x = [ x ]; in x` prints `[ «repeated» ]` here vs. real
Nix's `[ [ «repeated» ] ]`). Traced to the exact same root cause as
M81's `eq-slot-elem`/`eq-slot-identity` cut: cppnix's printer keys its
cycle-detection `seen` set by `&v` -- the ADDRESS of the `Value` struct
occurrence being printed, not its content -- and a plain variable
reference's `ExprVar::eval` copies the referenced Value's CONTENT into
a NEW struct address every time it's dereferenced (while a Thunk, once
forced, keeps its OWN address forever, distinct from whatever it
resolved to). Confirmed by fetching cppnix's actual `print.cc`
(`printList`: `seen->insert(&v)`) and empirically binary-searching
through `nix-instantiate` on `let x = [x]; in x` /
`let x = [x x]; in x` / `let a = [1]; x = [a a]; in x` /
`rec { a = [a]; }` until a single consistent model explained all four
outputs: a bare self-reference goes through ONE extra Value-copy
indirection (the `let`-body's own `ExprVar::eval`) that a `rec`-
attrset's own internal self-reference does not, which is exactly why
`let x = [x]; in x` needs TWO bracket levels before collapsing but
`rec { a = [a]; }` only needs ONE. asnix's `Value` is a plain 8-byte
tagged word copied freely everywhere, with no notion of "the address
this particular occurrence happens to live at" distinct from "the
heap object its tag points to" -- reproducing cppnix's exact behavior
here means giving every Value occurrence (env slot, thunk, list/attrs
element) that same struct-identity, which is a core representation
change, not a printer-local fix -- the same scope boundary M81 already
drew for `maybeThunk` slot-identity sharing, just reached from the
printer instead of from `==`.

## M84: root-caused and fixed the M82 `ffmpeg` mismatch -- `asnix_collect_input_refs` over-collecting through non-derivation attrsets

Picked up the exact thread M82 left off: `./asnix d.nix`
(`ffmpeg.outPath`) ran to completion but didn't match real Nix's hash.
Bisected the ~60-wide dependency closure the same binary-search way
every prior hash-parity bug this session was found: dump each
candidate's own ATerm with `ASNIX_DEBUG_DRV=<name>`, diff it
(hash-normalized) against the real `.drv` `nix-instantiate` writes to
the store for the same attribute, and recurse into whichever
`InputDrvs` entry's hash actually differs (several entries differ
textually but are false leads -- see below). The chain, each one
confirmed by directly comparing that package's own `.outPath`/
`.drvPath` against real `nix-instantiate --eval --strict`:

```
ffmpeg -> sdl2-compat -> sdl3 -> { pipewire, zenity }
zenity -> gtk4 -> gst-plugins-bad -> { openal-soft, spandsp }
pipewire -> { ffado, roc-toolkit, spandsp }
ffado -> scons -> python3.14-distutils -> python3.14-jaraco-envs
  -> python3.14-tox -> python3.14-pyproject-api -> python3.14-furo
  -> furo-web (passthru.web, a buildNpmPackage) -> { furo-web-npm-deps
     (FOD), npm-config-hook } -> prefetch-npm-deps
     (rustPlatform.buildRustPackage)
```

**False leads worth naming** (so a future bisection doesn't waste time
re-discovering this): `spandsp` showed up as a hash mismatch inside
*two* unrelated parents' `InputDrvs` (`gst-plugins-bad` and
`pipewire`), and `furo-web-npm-deps` (the `fetchNpmDeps` FOD) showed up
inside `furo-web`'s -- in both cases the mismatched entry's own
`.drvPath` (the literal `.drv` *file's* store path) differed, but its
own `.outPath` (what the entry's `hashDerivationModulo` actually
produces) was byte-identical to real Nix. This is expected, not a bug:
`hashDerivationModulo`'s whole purpose (M74) is to substitute each
input's *recursive modulo-hash* into a derivation's own hash
computation, not that input's literal file path -- so a `.drv`-file-
only divergence somewhere *else* in that input's own ancestry (one
that doesn't change ITS OWN `hashDerivationModulo`) can cosmetically
perturb a dependency's `InputDrvs`-listed path without ever touching
the hash that actually matters. Confirmed directly: `nix-instantiate
--eval --strict -E '(import nixpkgs {}).spandsp.outPath'` and the
asnix equivalent agree exactly, even though `.drvPath` doesn't -- the
real divergence had to be chased elsewhere (`openal-soft`, whose
`.outPath` genuinely disagreed, led to the real `pipewire` ->
`ffado` branch).

**Root cause, isolated with a 7-line minimal repro** (not ffmpeg --
`derivation { ...; srcAttr = lib.cleanSourceWith { src = ./sub;
filter = name: type: baseNameOf name != "drop.txt"; }; }`, `./sub`
containing one kept and one dropped file): real Nix's `.drv` lists
exactly one `inputSrcs` entry (the filtered copy, store-name
`source`); asnix's listed *two* -- the correct filtered `source`
entry, PLUS a second, spurious entry named `sub` (the UNFILTERED
original directory's own basename), never built by real Nix at all.

`lib/sources.nix`'s `cleanSourceWith`/`fromSourceAttributes` (the
mechanism behind `lib.cleanSourceWith`, and therefore anything using
it -- `rustPlatform.buildRustPackage`'s default `src` filter among
many others) returns a plain attrset shaped `{ _isLibCleanSourceWith
= true; origSrc; name; filter; outPath = builtins.path { ... }; }` --
*not* a `type = "derivation"` attrset. `origSrc` is the ORIGINAL,
UNFILTERED `Path` (here, the whole `prefetch-npm-deps/` source
directory); `outPath` is the actual filtered copy real Nix's
`coerceToString` ever looks at when this attrset flows into a
derivation attribute.

`derivation.c`'s `asnix_collect_input_refs` -- a call-scoped walk
(M74/M76) that reconstructs which of a `derivation {...}` call's
attribute values reference another derivation's output or a plain
store path, mirroring the union of context real Nix's own
`coerceToString` calls would collect -- had exactly one recursion
rule for an ATTRS value that isn't itself a derivation: recurse into
*every* nested attribute value, unconditionally. That rule exists for
a real, narrower need (M76): a `__structuredAttrs`-mode attribute's
raw value gets walked by real Nix's `printValueAsJSON` in full, so a
derivation reference buried inside a *JSON-serialized* nested attrset
genuinely needs the same full walk. But the SAME blind-recursion rule
was also firing for `cleanSourceWith`'s result when it's an ordinary
(non-structured-attrs) attribute value -- where real Nix's actual
coercion (`asnix_coerce_to_string_for_derivation`'s own ATTRS case)
only ever follows `__toString` then `outPath`, nothing else. Walking
`origSrc` too NAR-copied the unfiltered directory a second time
(M75's `asnix_copy_path_to_store`) and registered that copy as its
own bogus extra `inputSrcs` entry.

Fix: `asnix_collect_input_refs` now takes an explicit `json_mode`
flag. Reaching a non-derivation ATTRS value with `json_mode` true
(a genuine `__structuredAttrs`-blob attribute) keeps the old blind
walk, recursing with `json_mode` still true. Reaching one with
`json_mode` false now mirrors `asnix_coerce_to_string_for_derivation`
exactly instead: follow `__toString` (calling it) if present, else
`outPath` if present, else contribute nothing (matching that function
falling through to a fatal "can't coerce" real Nix would also hit --
nothing a real coercion could ever reach either). The call site
(looping over a `derivation {...}` call's own attributes) now computes
`json_mode` per-attribute as `structured_attrs && !is_special &&
!is_args_key` -- the exact set of attributes that flow into the
`__json` blob raw rather than through ordinary string coercion
(`args` is carved out even in structured-attrs mode: real Nix always
coerces it per-element regardless, confirmed by this file's own
pre-existing comment on that `continue`). `LIST` recursion threads
`json_mode` through unchanged (a list's own elements get the same
treatment as their container, in both real Nix and this project
already, independent of this fix).

Verified the fix closes every hop of the bisected chain above (each
one's `.outPath`/`.drvPath` now matches real `nix-instantiate --eval
--strict` exactly, not just the leaf `prefetch-npm-deps` the minimal
repro targeted) and, at the top:

```
"/nix/store/29iacg6h530yx7rxz4k1fhvi0kxxhsam-ffmpeg-9.0.1-bin"
```

-- `./asnix d.nix` now matches real Nix's
`(import nixpkgs {}).ffmpeg.outPath` byte-for-byte, closing the gap
M82 left open.

`make test`/`make test-e2e`/`make test-conformance`: unchanged, all
green. `make test-nix-conformance`: `pass=646 fail=12 skip=148`,
identical to the pre-fix baseline -- zero regressions (expected: no
numtide/nix-conformance fixture happens to exercise a non-derivation
attrset with an `outPath`/`__toString` inside a `derivation {...}`
attribute value). `make test-nixpkgs-hash`: `pass=8 fail=0`,
unchanged (the pre-existing 4-package corpus never reached this code
path either -- see the next milestone for why a much wider corpus was
overdue).

## M85: `tests/nixpkgs-hash/attrs.txt` expanded from 4 packages to 74

The M77 corpus (`hello`/`hello.src`/`bash`/`curl`) was a smoke test, not
a real sweep -- four packages sharing mostly the same shallow shape.
Expanded `tests/nixpkgs-hash/attrs.txt` to 74 real nixpkgs top-level
attribute paths (148 `outPath`+`drvPath` checks total), deliberately
spread across the categories the task asked for rather than just
picking 70 more packages that look like `hello`:

- common CLI tools (`ripgrep`, `fd`, `bat`, `jq`, `tree`, `fzf`, `tmux`,
  `htop`, `neovim`, `rsync`, `openssh`, `which`, `less`, `nano`, `vim`,
  `fish`, `zsh`, `yarn`, `git`/`git.src`)
- GNU-coreutils-family / classic Unix tools (`coreutils`, `findutils`,
  `diffutils`, `patch`, `gnugrep`, `gnused`, `gawk`, `gnutar`, `gzip`,
  `bzip2`, `xz`, `zstd`)
- compilers/toolchains (`gcc`, `clang`, `llvm`, `rustc`, `go`, `jdk`)
- scripting-language interpreters (`python3`/`python3.src`, `python311`,
  `perl`, `ruby`, `nodejs`)
- common C libraries, several genuinely multi-output (`zlib`,
  `openssl`, `libxml2`, `sqlite`, `pcre2`, `ncurses`, `readline`,

- build-system tooling (`cmake`, `pkg-config`, `autoconf`, `automake`,

- a GUI/graphics stack slice (`boost`, `cairo`, `pixman`, `freetype`,

- fetcher-based/fixed-output derivations beyond the pre-existing
  `hello.src` (`curl.src`, `git.src`, `python3.src`)
- `nix` itself, a large real-world multi-output C++ derivation

Confirmed (not assumed) the `__structuredAttrs` category is real
coverage, not just hoped-for: queried every candidate's own
`drvAttrs.__structuredAttrs` and found ~40 of the 74 (`ripgrep`, `bat`,
`jq`, `fzf`, `tmux`, `neovim`, `coreutils`, `findutils`, `diffutils`,
`patch`, every `gnu*` tool, `gzip`/`bzip2`/`xz`/`zstd`, `zlib`,
`openssl`, `libxml2`, `sqlite`, `pcre2`, `ncurses`, `readline`,
`glibc`, `util-linux`, `cmake`, `pkg-config`, `autoconf`, `automake`,
`libtool`, `ninja`, `boost`, `glib`, `gcc`, `clang`, `llvm`, `go`, ...)
genuinely set it, so this corpus's `__structuredAttrs` ATerm-encoding
path (M69/M80) gets real exercise, not a single lucky hit.

Deliberately left `ffmpeg`/`sdl2-compat`/`prefetch-npm-deps` out of
this list: `ffmpeg.outPath` alone takes several seconds to evaluate
(a much larger closure than anything else here) and is already
tracked separately by the repo root's `d.nix` plus M82/M84's own
notes, not by this smoke-sweep corpus.

Run post-M84 (the `asnix_collect_input_refs` fix): **pass=148
fail=0** -- every single check in the expanded corpus passes. No NEW
divergence was found beyond the one M84 already root-caused and
fixed (expected: none of these 74 attribute paths route through
`rustPlatform.buildRustPackage`'s `cargoLock.lockFile` ->
`lib.cleanSourceWith`-shaped `src` the way `ffmpeg`'s `sdl2-compat` ->
... -> `prefetch-npm-deps` chain did -- the bug class M84 fixed is
real and triggers for any `derivation {...}` attribute whose value is
a non-derivation attrset exposing both an unfiltered `Path` field and
an `outPath`, not unique to `prefetch-npm-deps`, but this particular
corpus's 74 picks happen not to hit that specific shape). Confirms
M84's fix, not this corpus's own breadth, is what closed the `ffmpeg`
gap -- and that the fix didn't regress anything else reachable from a
much wider, more diverse slice of real nixpkgs than this project had
ever swept before.

`make test`/`make test-e2e`/`make test-conformance`: unchanged, all

## M86: real `DrvDeep` string-context closure propagation -- `eval-okay-context-inputs.nix` now passes; `eq-slot-elem`/`eq-slot-identity` re-investigated and re-declined, with a sharper counterexample

### Part 1: `eval-okay-context-inputs.nix`

Re-checked this fixture from scratch rather than trusting M81's own
scope note (which blamed BOTH the `drvPath` and `both` cases on a
missing `computeFSClosure`/transitive-closure walk). Running it
against the current tree first: **8 of 9 cases already matched**
real `nix-instantiate --eval --strict`'s `.exp` output byte-for-byte
(`out`, `dev`, `both`, `drvOnly`, `file`, `plain`,
`substringEmpty`, `appended`) -- M74-M85's cumulative string-context
work had already closed every gap except exactly one: `drvPath =
show d.drvPath;` (passing a derivation's own `drvPath` string
directly, not through string interpolation or a named output, as
another derivation's attribute value). `both` was in fact already
correct; M81's note was stale.

Root cause, confirmed directly against
`~/nix/src/libexpr/primops.cc`'s `derivationStrictInternal`: a
`NixStringContextElem::DrvDeep` context element (attached to a
derivation's own `drvPath` string value, M80) is handled completely
differently from `Built`/`Opaque`:

```cpp
[&](const NixStringContextElem::DrvDeep & d) {
    /* !!! This doesn't work if readOnlyMode is set. */
    StorePathSet refs;
    state.store->computeFSClosure(d.drvPath, refs);
    for (auto & j : refs) {
        drv.inputSrcs.insert(j);
        if (j.isDerivation())
            drv.inputDrvs.map[j].value = state.store->readDerivation(j).outputNames();
    }
},
```

Every member of `d.drvPath`'s FULL transitive closure (itself
included -- `computeFSClosure` is root-inclusive) becomes an
`inputSrcs` entry, and every member that's itself a derivation ALSO
becomes an `inputDrvs` entry keyed by that member's COMPLETE own
output set -- not just whichever output(s) happen to be referenced
elsewhere. Contrast with `Built` (what `"${d}"`/`d.dev` already
produce): that only ever adds ONE `(drvPath, outputName)` pair to
`inputDrvs`, never touching `inputSrcs`. `asnix_collect_input_refs`
(`derivation.c`) read `ctx->ndrvs`/`ctx->nsrcs` (Built/Opaque) but
never consulted `ctx->ndeep` at all -- a `DrvDeep`-tagged string used
as an attribute value silently collected zero input refs (M80's own
comment said as much: "deliberately NOT read ... zero risk to
M74-M79's hash-parity work" -- correct for hash-parity at the time,
but exactly the gap this fixture exercises).

asnix has no real on-disk store to run `computeFSClosure` against,
but doesn't need one: this process's own call-by-need evaluation
order already guarantees every derivation a `DrvDeep` element could
ever name was fully constructed -- hence already cacheable -- before
a string carrying that context element could exist. Exactly the same
"read-only-mode, in-memory substitute for reading a `.drv` back off
disk" precedent `g_masked_hash_cache` (M74) already established for
`hashDerivationModulo`. Added two small per-drv-path linear-scan
caches (`derivation.c`), populated once, right after each
derivation's own `drv_path`/`output_names` are finalized
(`cache_own_drv_closure`):

- `g_drv_outputs_cache`: `drv_path` -> that derivation's own complete
  output-name list (needed to expand a closure member into "all its
  outputs", not just one specific referenced output).
- `g_drv_closure_cache`: `drv_path` -> the already-flattened set of
  every OTHER drv path and plain src path transitively reachable
  from it (itself included), built by unioning each DIRECT input
  drv's own closure entry (already cached, already flat, by the
  call-by-need guarantee above) -- so no recursion is needed at
  lookup time, only at insertion time, and only one level deep.

`asnix_collect_input_refs`'s PTR-string case now additionally walks
`ctx->deep`, resolves each entry through these two caches, and adds
every closure member to `inputSrcs` (unconditionally) and to
`inputDrvs` with its full output set (if it's itself a derivation) --
replicating the real-Nix loop above exactly. A string carrying an
unresolvable `DrvDeep` path (not built by this process -- e.g. a
synthetic path from `addDrvOutputDependencies`) falls back to a bare
`inputSrcs` entry, the same degenerate case real Nix's own
`realiseContext` hits when it can't expand a `DrvDeep` element
further.

One more real, independent bug surfaced building this: `drv_type`'s
own "text:" reference-list computation (used for a `.drv`'s OWN
content-addressed store path, M74) concatenated `group_paths`
(direct input-drv paths) and `refs.srcs` (direct src paths) on the
assumption that they're always disjoint -- true before this
milestone ("a path is either a derivation or a plain source, never
both"). `DrvDeep` breaks that invariant ON PURPOSE: a closure member
that's a derivation now ALSO lands in `inputSrcs` (matching real
Nix's own unconditional `inputSrcs.insert(j)` for every closure
member, derivation or not), so the same path can legitimately appear
in both arrays now. Real Nix's `references` is a deduped
`StorePathSet`; asnix's `drv_refs` concatenation wasn't deduped,
double-counting the colliding path in the TYPE string and producing
a wrong `drvPath` hash even after the closure/output caches
themselves were already correct (confirmed by hand: before this
second fix, the `drvPath` case's `outPath` already matched but its
`drvPath` still didn't -- the `outPath` only depends on the MASKED
pass, which never touches `drv_type`, while `drvPath` depends on the
REAL pass's own store-path TYPE string, which does). Fixed by
deduping `drv_refs` after sorting, immediately before building
`drv_type`.

Verified against the fixture's own `.exp`: `eval-okay-context-
inputs.nix` now matches byte-for-byte, all 9 cases.
`make test-nix-conformance`: `pass=651 fail=7 skip=148` ->
**`pass=652 fail=6 skip=148`**. `make test`/`make test-e2e`: still
fully green (no regressions, no new fixtures needed -- the existing
conformance fixture is the verification). `make test-nixpkgs-hash`:
confirmed **`pass=148 fail=0`**, unchanged, both immediately before
and after this change -- `derivation.c` was touched (hash-parity-
critical), but the new code path (a `DrvDeep` context element
reaching `asnix_collect_input_refs`) is only ever exercised by a
`.drvPath` value flowing directly into another derivation's
attribute, a shape none of the 74-package real-nixpkgs corpus's
`outPath`/`drvPath` checks happen to hit (nixpkgs itself overwhelmingly
passes derivation OUTPUTS around, not bare `drvPath`s), and the
dedup fix only changes behavior when a path appears in both
`group_paths` and `refs.srcs` simultaneously -- impossible before
this milestone's own `DrvDeep` handling made it possible in the
first place.

### Part 2: `eq-slot-elem.nix`/`eq-slot-identity.nix` -- re-investigated, still declined, with a sharper counterexample

Re-traced both fixtures by hand against the actual current asnix
binary (not just against the old write-up) to check for a narrower
opening. Current asnix output vs. expected:

```
eq-slot-elem:     got [ true true true true ]        want [ true false false true ]
eq-slot-identity: got [ true true true true true true true true true true false true true true true ]
                  want [ false false false true false false true true true true false true true true true ]
```

Confirmed exactly which real-Nix mechanism produces `want`, reading
`~/nix/gc-unlock/src/libexpr/eval.cc` directly rather than relying on
memory: `Expr::maybeThunk` (the default, used by every expression
kind EXCEPT the six overrides at `eval.cc:1055-1390` --
`ExprVar`/`ExprString`/`ExprInt`/`ExprFloat`/`ExprPath`/`ExprList`)
always allocates a genuine fresh `Thunk`, a new heap `Value` struct
with its own address, whenever an expression is used as a list
element / attrset-inherit value / lambda-call argument. `ExprVar`'s
override instead returns a POINTER TO THE EXISTING Env-slot storage
directly -- no allocation, so a bare-variable reference threaded
through a list/attrset-literal/call-argument SHARES the exact same
`Value` struct address as its original binding (and as every other
bare-variable reference to the same binding). `ExprOpEq::eval` itself
always evaluates its own two operands into two FRESH, separate local
`Value`s (M81's own fix already covers this half), so `eqValues`'s
`&v1 == &v2` fast path never fires for `==`'s own direct operands --
only for values reached by first passing through a `maybeThunk`-
aliased path (list/attrset literal, call argument) and THEN being
compared (e.g. as list elements, where `eqValues`'s `nList` case
recurses on `*v1.listElems()[i]`/`*v2.listElems()[i]` -- REFERENCES
to the ACTUAL stored `Value*` pointers, not fresh copies). Critically,
`eqValues`'s `nFunction` case is `return false` UNCONDITIONALLY --
with NO content-based fallback of any kind -- so two function values
are `==` in real Nix if and only if they were reached through an
unbroken chain of `maybeThunk`-aliasing back to the literal same
`Value` STORAGE CELL, full stop; the actual closure/environment the
cell happens to hold is irrelevant to the comparison.

asnix's flat 8-byte `Value` already gives closures pointer identity
for free (a `TAG_CLOSURE` word's payload bits ARE the heap address of
the closure object, and `OP_EQ` already compares those bits
directly, per M81) -- which is why the two cases that depend ONLY on
"was a fresh closure object allocated" already come out right by
coincidence: a literal lambda (`x: x`) evaluated twice allocates two
distinct closure objects (same as `ExprLambda::eval` in real Nix), so
`[ (x: x) ] == [ (x: x) ]` is already `false` in asnix, matching real
Nix, with no fix needed.

The NEW, sharper counterexample this re-investigation found (not in
M52/M81's write-ups): `id id` -- applying the identity function to
itself -- evaluates to the exact SAME closure object as `id` itself
(no new closure is ever allocated; `id`'s own body just returns its
argument, which IS the `id` closure, unchanged). So asnix's
pointer-identity rule for `TAG_CLOSURE` -- "same heap address ==
equal" -- says `[ (id id) ] == [ (id id) ]` and `builtins.elem id [
(id id) ]` should both be `true` (it genuinely is the identical
closure object both times). But real Nix says `false` for both
(confirmed directly in both `.exp` files: `eq-slot-elem`'s 2nd
element, `eq-slot-identity`'s 3rd element) -- because `(id id)` is a
call expression (`ExprCall`, no `maybeThunk` override), so each of
its two textual occurrences gets its OWN fresh `Thunk` cell with its
OWN address, and `eqValues`'s `nFunction` case doesn't care that both
thunks resolve to the identical underlying closure -- cell identity,
not referent identity, is literally the only thing being compared.

This proves, independent of M52/M81's own reasoning, that "two
Values with the same CONTENT/POINTER" (the only notion of identity
asnix's flat `Value` can ever express for a heap kind) is NEITHER
necessary NOR sufficient to replicate real Nix's function-equality
rule: not sufficient (this counterexample: same pointer, real Nix
says unequal), and not necessary (M81's own case: `f == f` for a
bare-variable `==` operand is `false` in real Nix despite `maybeThunk`
aliasing existing for `f` as a variable, because `ExprOpEq::eval`
specifically bypasses `maybeThunk` for its own two operands). The
ONLY faithful model is real Nix's own: identity attaches to the
*storage cell an occurrence happens to borrow or get freshly
allocated into*, completely decoupled from the cell's content --
which requires a cell/box indirection distinct from content for
every `Value`, not just closures, since the aliasing-vs-fresh-copy
distinction has to be threaded through every list-literal/attrset-
literal/call-argument/`with`-fallback/select construct a closure
value could flow through on its way to a comparison. Scoping the fix
to "just closures" doesn't reduce that breadth: the breadth comes
from needing to track *how a value arrived*, not from needing to
track every value's *type*, and every one of those "how it arrived"
sites (list literals, attrset literals, call-argument passing,
`with`-fallback, thunk-forcing) already exists in the compiler/asm
core for EVERY value, closures included. Confirmed, a second time
from an independent angle, that this remains exactly the
"infrastructure genuinely out of proportion" scope cut M52 and M81
already drew -- not attempted here, to avoid a partial/heuristic
rule (e.g. "closures reached via a call are always unequal") that
would silently produce wrong answers on cases this session didn't
happen to check (real Nix's actual rule has nothing to do with
"was it a call" specifically -- `with`-fallback and `select` hit the
exact same `false`, and plenty of OTHER call shapes, like
`(x: x: x) 1` partially applied, would need their own hand-verified
behavior before any such heuristic could be trusted).

No code changes for this part. `eq-slot-elem.nix`/`eq-slot-
identity.nix` remain in `make test-nix-conformance`'s failing list,
unchanged from before this investigation.

## M87: perf/memory regression triage -- `intersectAttrs` O(n log m)-vs-O(m log n) fix, three non-arena memory leaks

The user flagged that performance (and separately, memory usage)
"seems to be suffering" on the repo root's `d.nix`
(`(import /home/tbereknyei/nixpkgs/default.nix {}).ffmpeg.outPath`,
a ~100-derivation real nixpkgs closure). Measured first, rather than
guessing: `perf stat -e instructions,cycles ./asnix d.nix` showed
**~51.3 billion instructions / ~18.4 billion cycles / ~5.7s wall**,
against real `nix-instantiate --eval --strict` on the identical
expression's **~12.0 billion instructions / ~6.1 billion cycles /
~2.0s wall** -- asnix, a hand-written assembly interpreter with no
GC, was running *slower* than real Nix on real work. That shouldn't
be possible for a well-tuned interpreter and was worth chasing
rather than accepting as "the no-GC tradeoff" (the same discipline
established earlier this session for the M78 memory investigation).

### CPU: `builtins.intersectAttrs` walked the wrong side

`perf record -g` + `perf report --no-children` on `./asnix d.nix`
found `intersectAttrs2_impl` (`src/c/builtins_m23.c`) and its
`asnix_bshared_attrs_find`/`asnix_bshared_attrs_sym` helpers
responsible for **~18% of all sampled cycles alone** -- by far the
single largest hotspot, well ahead of anything else. The existing
implementation always iterated over `e2` (the second argument) and
binary-searched each of its symbols into `e1` (the first), on the
theory that "both inputs are sorted, so a merge-style walk needs no
re-sort" -- true, but the code didn't actually do a merge walk, it
did `n2` binary searches into `e1`, i.e. O(n2 log n1).

Instrumenting the function directly (temporary call-counter +
`fprintf`, reverted before committing) confirmed the real-world
shape: real nixpkgs's own `lib.callPackageWith`
(`pkgs/top-level/lib/customisation.nix`-equivalent in every
`callPackage`-based package set) computes `intersectAttrs
(functionArgs f) autoArgs` once per `callPackage` call -- `e1` is a
handful of a function's formal-argument names (single digits to a
few dozen), `e2` is `autoArgs`, effectively the *entire* `pkgs`
attrset. Measured directly: evaluating `d.nix`'s ffmpeg closure
calls `intersectAttrs` **~7,700+ times total, ~840 of them with
`e2` at exactly 28,189 entries** (nixpkgs's real top-level package
count) against an `e1` of single digits to dozens. Each such call
was doing ~28,189 binary searches (O(n2 log n1) ≈ 28,189 × log2(20)
≈ 122,000 comparisons) when the correct-but-unused approach (walk
whichever side is smaller, binary-search into the larger) would do
O(n1 log n2) ≈ 20 × log2(28189) ≈ 300 -- a ~400x reduction in
comparison count for this call shape alone.

Fixed by computing both `n1` and `n2` up front and walking whichever
is smaller (binary-searching into whichever is larger), instead of
unconditionally walking `e2`. Correct regardless of which side is
walked: both inputs are sorted by symbol id, so walking either one
in its own order yields an output already sorted by symbol id (no
re-sort needed either way), and the emitted value always comes from
`e2` as before.

Measured impact on `./asnix d.nix` (3-run `perf stat -r 3`, low
variance <0.4%): **instructions 51.3B → 42.1B (-18%)**, cycles
18.4B → 17.8B. (Wall-clock improvement was harder to isolate cleanly
in the moment -- the machine was concurrently running a separate
background agent whose own unscoped filesystem search spiked system
load average to 12+, corrupting timing comparisons; see the
`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`/memory entry this prompted. The instruction-
count reduction, measured via hardware performance counters rather
than wall-clock, is unaffected by concurrent system load and is the
number to trust here.)

### Memory: three non-arena leaks found via an LD_PRELOAD malloc tracer

The user separately pushed back when `./asnix d.nix`'s peak RSS
(measured via `/usr/bin/time -v`) came back at **1,451,720 KB
(~1.42GB)** against real Nix's **374,188 KB (~374MB)** on the same
expression -- a ~3.9x gap, far worse than the ~1.35x gap M78 had
already closed for the much smaller `hello` closure (confirmed
`e.nix`, i.e. `hello.drvPath`, was still exactly at M78's own
169,856 KB figure -- so M78's own fix hadn't regressed, this was a
*new*, ffmpeg-closure-scale problem M78 never touched).

Reading `asnix_arena.total_allocated` directly (temporary debug
hook, reverted) showed only ~538MB -- meaning roughly **900MB of
the 1.42GB peak RSS wasn't going through the arena at all**. Since
the arena is the project's one and only "permanent" allocator
(deliberately never-free, by design -- see arena.h's own header
comment), any OTHER large, persistent memory use has to be a plain
`malloc`/`realloc` call somewhere that's either leaking or carrying
unnecessary slack.

Confirmed precisely via `gdb` (breaking at the process's one exit
point, reading `/proc/<pid>/smaps`/`status` through gdb's own
Python API rather than an external `pgrep` guess, which initially
grabbed the wrong PID and gave a wildly wrong answer) and
`malloc_stats()` called into the stopped inferior: glibc's main
malloc arena alone (`[heap]`) was **~756MB resident, 99.95% "in
use"** by glibc's own accounting -- not fragmentation slack, genuine
live, unreleased allocations.

Rather than guess which call site, wrote a small LD_PRELOAD shim
(`malloc`/`calloc`/`realloc`/`free` interposition, header-prefix
technique to recover each block's allocation site and size in O(1)
at `free()` time without a second lookup table that would itself
distort the measurement) tracking per-call-site cumulative and
current-outstanding bytes, resolved via `addr2line` against the
PIE binary's own load offset. This directly identified three
distinct leaks/waste sources, ranked by outstanding bytes:

1. **Lexer token array, never freed (`src/c/lexer.c`'s
   `asnix_lex`/`push_tok`).** `~195MB outstanding across only 3,688
   realloc call sites` (i.e. ~53KB average per file's token array,
   consistent with "most files small, a handful huge"). Both call
   sites (`src/c/eval_file.c`'s `parse_resolved_file` and
   `asnix_eval_expr_source`) called `asnix_lex` then
   `asnix_parse(toks, ...)` and simply never freed `toks` afterward.
   Confirmed safe: nothing outside lexer.c/parser.c ever stores a
   raw `Token*` (`asnix_parse` copies out whatever an `Ast` node
   needs -- names/text point into the original source buffer, not
   into the token array). Fixed with a `free(toks)` right after each
   `asnix_parse` call returns.

2. **`IrBuilder`'s `ops`/`pool` arrays carrying permanent
   doubling-growth slack (`src/c/irbuild.c`).** `ib_emit`/
   `ib_pool_add` grow these by doubling (standard, correct amortized-
   O(1) growth) -- but `ib_finish` hands the *still-oversized*
   buffers straight into the permanent, program-lifetime
   `IrProgram` (one per compiled thunk/function/expression -- over a
   **million** of them across a full nixpkgs evaluation) without
   ever trimming to the final `len`/`pool_len`. Whichever fill
   fraction a builder happened to land on when finished (e.g. 55%
   full right after a doubling) was carried forever, times roughly a
   million builders. Fixed with two `realloc`-to-exact-size calls in
   `ib_finish` before the arrays are stored into `prog` (safe:
   shrinking `realloc` never moves/invalidates the still-needed
   prefix). This was the single largest contributor found --
   trimming eliminated the vast majority of what had shown up at
   `ib_emit`'s own (pre-trim) call site.

3. **`BTVec`'s backing arrays never freed after `insert_attrpath`'s
   tree is flattened (`src/c/parser.c`).** Every attrset literal
   (`{...}`/`rec {...}`/`let`'s own binding list) builds a transient
   `BTVec` tree (one node per attrpath segment, handling both plain
   `name = val;` bindings and `a.b.c = val;` attrpath-sugar's nested-
   attrset merging) that gets flattened into ordinary `AST_ATTRSET`
   nodes by `finalize_bt_node`/`finalize_bt_vec` -- but neither
   function freed the `BTVec`'s own `items`/`dyn.items` arrays after
   copying out everything they needed (leaf values are `Ast*`
   already living in the arena; `finalize_dyn_vec` copies its own
   exact-size array). Fixed by freeing `node->children.items`/
   `node->children.dyn.items` inside `finalize_bt_node`'s branch case
   and `vec->items` at the end of `finalize_bt_vec`, after confirming
   (by reading every one of its ~5 call sites) that none of them
   reuse the `BTVec` afterward. A smaller, related leak in the same
   file (`parse_binding_stmt`'s `inherit (expr) a b;` case never
   freeing its own `AttrSegVec names`) was fixed the same way.

Measured impact on `./asnix d.nix`: peak RSS **1,451,720 KB → 917,104
KB (~37% reduction)**. The malloc tracer's own
`sum_of_current_outstanding` dropped from **~903MB → ~366MB**
(consistent with the measured RSS drop once combined with the
arena's own roughly-unchanged ~538MB). Also measured a reduction on
the much smaller `e.nix` (`hello.drvPath`) workload as a sanity
check that these fixes generalize rather than being ffmpeg-closure-
specific: peak RSS **169,856 KB → 133,588 KB**.

`make test`/`make test-e2e`/`make test-conformance`: unchanged, all
green. `make test-nix-conformance`: `pass=652 fail=6 skip=148`,
identical to the pre-existing baseline -- zero regressions.
`make test-nixpkgs-hash`: reconfirmed `pass=148 fail=0` both before
and after (parser.c/irbuild.c/eval_file.c/builtins_m23.c are not
among the project's hash-parity-critical files, but verified anyway
since this touched derivation-construction-adjacent code paths).

Not pursued further in this milestone (left as documented, scoped-
out leads for a future pass, same discipline as declining
eq-slot-elem/-identity rather than half-fixing them): `src/c/
derivation.c`'s `asnix_prim_derivation` doing `strcmp`-based output-
name comparisons where a symbol-id comparison might be cheaper;
`builtins_compare.c`'s `sorted_name_order`/`prim_attrNames` repeated
`strcmp`-based qsort comparator; a list literal's own `AstVec`
(`src/c/parser.c`'s `astvec_push`) carrying the same kind of
doubling-growth slack `IrBuilder` had, just not yet measured as
large enough to prioritize. A separate background agent was
dispatched to continue the CPU-side investigation specifically
(further O(n^2)-pattern hunting, the `strcmp`/`compile_expr`
leads above) -- see its own milestone section, if landed after this
one, for what it found.
## M88: three more O(n^2)-or-worse CPU hotspots fixed -- `cache_own_drv_closure`'s own linear-scan caches (the ones M86 just added), `parser.c`'s `btvec_find`, and `builtins_attrs.c`'s insertion-sort `attrNames`/`attrValues`

Continuing this session's CPU-time investigation (the one that
already found and fixed `intersectAttrs2_impl`'s backwards-walk
bug and flagged `parser.c`'s `btvec_find` as a lead). `perf stat -e
instructions,cycles ./asnix d.nix` (real nixpkgs's `ffmpeg`, ~100
derivations) on this session's starting point (M86's HEAD) measured
**~275 billion `cpu_core/instructions`, ~31.8s wall** for the
identical expression real `nix-instantiate` evaluates in ~12 billion
instructions / ~1.6s -- i.e. M86's own `DrvDeep` closure-propagation
feature (landed immediately before this investigation started) had
itself introduced a severe new regression on top of the ~42B-
instruction baseline the prior session's `intersectAttrs` fix had
reached, even though M86's own correctness work was sound.

### Fix 1: `derivation.c`'s `cache_own_drv_closure` family

`perf record -g` immediately pointed at one place: **73.59% of all
cycles** in `__strcmp_avx2`, almost entirely inlined-called from
`cache_own_drv_closure` (via `asnix_prim_derivation`). M86's own
comment had candidly described the three structures backing it --
`g_drv_outputs_cache`, `g_drv_closure_cache`, and the per-call
`DrvClosureStrSet` scratch set used to flatten one derivation's own
closure -- as "two small per-drv-path **linear-scan** caches". That
phrase was the bug: `g_drv_outputs_cache`/`g_drv_closure_cache` are
append-only for the WHOLE run, so a linear `find` against them is
O(total derivations built so far) per call; worse, `DrvClosureStrSet`
is rebuilt from scratch for EVERY derivation by unioning each direct
input's own already-flattened closure via a linear dedup-check scan
-- O(closure_size) per dedup check, performed closure_size-ish times,
i.e. **O(closure_size^2) per derivation**, for every derivation in
the build. Real nixpkgs closures run into the hundreds of members
once glibc/gcc/stdenv are pulled in, so this dominated the entire
run.

Fixed by converting all three to open-addressing hash
tables/sets, keyed by the drv_path (or closure-member path) string's
own FxHash-style hash (same mix `symtab.c`'s `hash_bytes` already
uses, and the same pattern `string_context.c` was converted to
earlier this session for an identical ptr-keyed diagnosis): a
persistent index (`g_drv_outputs_index`/`g_drv_closure_index`, grown
at 75% load factor) mapping hash(drv_path) -> array index for the two
long-lived caches, and `DrvClosureStrSet` grew its own parallel
`index`/`index_cap` fields so its per-call dedup check is O(1)
amortized instead of O(n). Insertion order into the backing arrays is
preserved exactly (first-seen-wins, same as before) -- only the
dedup-check's cost changed, not its result, so this is a pure
performance fix with no behavior change.

### Fix 2: `parser.c`'s `btvec_find`/`btvec_push`

Already flagged (not yet fixed) by the prior session: `btvec_find`
was a linear memcmp scan over a BTVec's own accumulated items, used
by `insert_attrpath` (every `a.b = v;`-style attrpath-sugar binding,
AND every ordinary attrset literal's dup-key check) -- O(n) per
lookup times n insertions = O(n^2) for one large attrset literal.
Real nixpkgs's own `pkgs/top-level/all-packages.nix` is exactly that
shape: thousands of `name = callPackage ...;` bindings in one literal
block. Fixed the same way as Fix 1: `BTVec` grew its own open-
addressing `index`/`index_cap` fields, maintained by `btvec_push`
(rehashing `items[0..len)` -- which never yet includes the item being
pushed -- before inserting the new entry, so no double-insertion) and
consulted by `btvec_find` in O(1) amortized instead of O(n). All
BTVec mutation in this file already went through `btvec_push`
exclusively (confirmed by grep), so no other call site needed
changes.

### Fix 3: `builtins_attrs.c`'s `sorted_name_order` (backs `attrNames`/`attrValues`)

Re-profiling after fixes 1 and 2 (which cut the top hotspot from
73.59% to near-zero) surfaced a THIRD O(n^2): `sorted_name_order`
was a plain insertion sort, with a comment explicitly reasoning
"attrsets are typically small and this isn't a hot path" -- true for
a hand-written literal, false for what `attrNames`/`attrValues`
actually gets called on in real nixpkgs: the same top-level `pkgs`
attrset `intersectAttrs2_impl`'s own fix (prior session) measured
directly at **28,189 entries**. `perf report` confirmed
`prim_attrNames`/`sorted_name_order`/`__memcmp_avx2_movbe`/
`asnix_sym_name` together consuming roughly a third of all remaining
cycles -- an O(n^2) insertion sort over tens of thousands of entries,
with EVERY comparison re-resolving both sides' symbol name from
scratch via `asnix_sym_name` on top of that. Fixed two ways at once:
switched to `qsort` (O(n log n) comparisons instead of O(n^2)), and
resolved each entry's name exactly ONCE up front into a flat
`NameOrderEntry[]` array the comparator reads directly, instead of
once per comparison. Symbol names are unique within one attrset (no
duplicate keys possible), so `qsort`'s lack of a stability guarantee
is immaterial -- no two entries can ever compare equal.

### Results

Measured via `perf stat -e instructions,cycles ./asnix d.nix`
(`cpu_core/instructions`, the domain capturing ~95-99% of this
process's execution on this hybrid CPU) and `hyperfine --shell=none`,
same machine, same build (`make release`), cumulative after all three
fixes:

| | instructions | wall (hyperfine mean) |
|---|---|---|
| M86 HEAD (this session's start) | ~275 billion | ~31.8s (perf stat elapsed) |
| + Fix 1 (`cache_own_drv_closure`) | ~46.2 billion (-83%) | ~6.77s (perf stat elapsed) |
| + Fix 2 (`btvec_find`) | ~43.9 billion | ~5.94s |
| + Fix 3 (`attrNames` sort) | **~37.9 billion** | **~6.09s** |

Net: **~7.25x fewer instructions, ~5.2x less wall time** than this
session's own starting point, and notably BELOW the ~42 billion
instructions the prior session's `intersectAttrs` fix had reached
(i.e. this fully absorbs M86's regression and then some) -- though
still above real `nix-instantiate`'s ~12 billion instructions / 1.6s
for the identical expression, so there is more headroom left (see
"Investigated but not fixed" below).

`./asnix e.nix` (the `hello` closure, used for fast iteration):
`hyperfine` measured ~337ms mean after all three fixes (`e.nix`'s
closure is far too small to exercise the `DrvDeep`-closure or giant-
attrset-literal hotspots Fix 1/Fix 2 target, so most of its own time
is fixed per-process overhead -- `attrNames`/`attrValues` on nixpkgs'
own `lib`-scale attrsets still benefits from Fix 3).

Verification: `make test`/`make test-e2e` identical output before and
after all three fixes (byte-for-byte, confirmed via diff). `make
test-nix-conformance`: `pass=652 fail=6 skip=148` before and after,
same 6 pre-existing failures (`eq-slot-elem`, `eq-slot-identity`,
`getattrpos-functionargs`, `getattrpos`, `inherit-attr-pos`, `print`)
-- zero regressions. `make test-nixpkgs-hash` (hash-parity-critical
since Fix 1 touches `derivation.c`): `pass=148 fail=0` before and
after, unchanged -- Fix 1 only changes dedup-check cost, never the
resulting `closure_drvs`/`closure_srcs` order or content, so hash
parity was never at risk, and this confirms it directly.

### Investigated but not fixed

- The remaining post-fix profile is dominated by `drv_closure_strset_
  add`/`drv_closure_strset_rehash` (~50% of remaining cycles) --
  Fix 1 made this O(closure_size) amortized per derivation instead of
  O(closure_size^2), but `cache_own_drv_closure`'s fundamental
  approach (eagerly flattening and COPYING each direct input's own
  flat closure array into every ancestor's own closure array) still
  does O(total transitive edges * average closure size) work overall
  for a deep dependency graph, since the same closure members get
  copied into many ancestors' arrays redundantly. A sharing-based
  redesign (e.g. a persistent/shared structure so ancestors reference
  rather than copy their children's closures) would cut this further
  but is a real architecture change to M86's data model, not a
  bounded bug fix -- declined for this session; the O(n^2)-or-worse
  algorithmic wins above already closed the gap this investigation
  was scoped to close.
- `compile_expr`'s deep recursion (`compiler.c`), flagged as a lead by
  the prior session: re-checked in `perf report` after all three
  fixes above and found to cost time strictly proportional to program
  size (recursion depth times a small constant per frame, no
  quadratic re-walking), i.e. this is accounted-for work, not an
  avoidable hotspot -- declined.
- `asnix_prim_derivation`'s own direct (non-`cache_own_drv_closure`)
  `__strcmp_avx2` calls (still ~7% of cycles post-fix, under
  `asnix_op_call` directly) and `prim_import`'s `__strcmp_avx2` (~0.7%,
  almost certainly the import-cache path/dedup check) are both small
  enough relative to the three fixes above that chasing them further
  is micro-optimization, not an algorithmic win -- left for a future
  pass if `d.nix`'s instruction count ever needs to close the
  remaining gap to real Nix's ~12 billion.

## M89: Makefile defaulted to `-O0` -- flipped to `-O2`, added a stale-flag guard

A background agent investigating "should we move more C into assembly
to reduce register spill?" found the real answer was no (checked
`-O2` codegen directly via `objdump`: GCC already keeps live values in
callee-saved registers across calls, no pathological spill pattern to
fix) -- but surfaced something more fundamental in the process: this
project's Makefile defaulted to `OPT ?= -O0` (`make`/`make -s` built
unoptimized C; only `make release` opted into `-O2`), on a documented
but, it turns out, outdated assumption ("the hot path under measurement
is hand-written asm, not compiler-optimized C, so the everyday loop
shouldn't pay -O2 compile cost"). Measured directly on `./asnix d.nix`
(real nixpkgs's `ffmpeg` closure): **`-O0`: ~9.9s user; `-O2`: ~4.9s
user** -- a ~2x difference from the flag alone, no code changes. A
meaningful share of this session's own earlier perf investigations ran
plain `make -s` (i.e. `-O0`) rather than `make release`, since the
project's own convention made that the "normal" way to build -- the
*relative* before/after comparisons within any single investigation
still held (same build type both sides), but several absolute
instruction-count/wall-clock figures reported earlier this session were
measured against an unnecessarily slow build.

Root cause of the outdated assumption: the dispatch *loop* itself is
indeed hand-written asm, but a large and growing share of real work
this session has been chasing (derivation-building, string/JSON/ATerm
encoding, hashing, the M86-M88 closure-cache machinery) lives in plain
C, compiled through this same `CFLAGS`/`$(OPT)` -- unoptimized C doing
real algorithmic work is genuinely much slower than optimized C, even
though the surrounding asm glue code isn't affected by the flag either
way.

Changed: `OPT` now defaults to `-O2`; a new `make debug` target
(`OPT := -O0`) restores the old fast-compile/gdb-friendly build for
anyone actively debugging with breakpoints (this session's own memory-
leak investigation relied on exactly that kind of debugging, where
`-O0`'s lack of optimization-driven variable elision/reordering
genuinely helps); `release` is kept as a now-redundant alias (identical
to the new default) so `bench/run` and any other existing script/doc
referencing `make release` keeps working unchanged.

Also fixed a related latent footgun found in the same investigation:
`-MMD -MP`'s header-dependency tracking has no way to know `$(OPT)`
itself changed (only source/header *files* trigger a rebuild), so
switching between `make`/`make debug`/`make release` without an
explicit `make clean` could silently leave a stale MIX of differently-
optimized `.o` files linked into one binary. Added a `.opt-stamp` file
recording the last-used `$(OPT)` value, checked once at Makefile parse
time (before any recipe/job dispatch, so it can't race with the
parallel `-j` object-compile rules) against whichever `OPT` value the
current invocation will actually use (`$(MAKECMDGOALS)` is checked for
an explicit `debug` goal, since that's the only target that currently
diverges from the global default) -- a mismatch triggers an automatic
`rm` of every object/dep/binary before the normal build rules run.
Verified by round-tripping `make debug` -> `make` twice in a row and
confirming each switch triggers a real full rebuild with the correct
`-O0`/`-O2` flag (checked the actual `cc` invocation lines, not just
the exit code).

`make test`/`make test-e2e`/`make test-conformance`/`make
test-nix-conformance`: unchanged, `pass=652 fail=6 skip=148`. `make
test-nixpkgs-hash`: unchanged, `pass=148 fail=0` (a build-system-only
change, not touching any hash-parity-critical file directly, but
verified anyway since it changes which optimization level every file
compiles at).

## M90: thunk-count reduction -- skip the thunk entirely for compile-time-trivial literals

A separate `/subtask` fork was asked to analyze memory usage with a
specific angle: "any ways we can reduce the number of thunks," with
an explicit pointer to look at real Nix and `~/gnix/iets` for ideas.

Real Nix's `Expr::maybeThunk` (`~/nix/gc-unlock/src/libexpr/eval.cc`)
is the function that decides, at the point a sub-expression is about
to become an argument/binding/list-element, whether to allocate a
fresh thunk or hand back something cheaper. The default always
allocates; six expression kinds override it: `ExprVar` (returns the
existing env-slot pointer directly -- a distinct optimization, see
the `eq-slot-elem`/`eq-slot-identity` investigation elsewhere in this
file, deliberately NOT touched by this milestone) and five pure-
literal kinds -- `ExprInt`/`ExprFloat`/`ExprString` (no
interpolation)/`ExprPath` (no search/interpolation) -- whose whole
point is that a literal costs nothing to evaluate, so deferring it in
a thunk is pure waste.

Checking `compiler.c`: `AST_INT`/`AST_FLOAT`/`AST_BOOL`/`AST_NULL`
already compile to a single zero-allocation push (`ib_push_int`,
`ib_push_true`/`false`/`null`, or a pooled `ib_push_const` for
`AST_FLOAT`'s heap-boxed-but-compile-time-constant value); a fully-
literal `AST_STRING` (no interpolated parts) already folds to one
pooled constant; a plain literal `AST_PATH` (not a search path, not
interpolated) resolves once at compile time the same way; `AST_CURPOS`
is likewise a pure compile-time constant. None of these need a captured
scope or any deferred work -- yet every one of `compiler.c`'s ~10
`ib_mk_thunk` call sites (list elements, let/attrs/rec bindings, call
arguments, `with` values) wrapped ALL of them anyway: a 32-byte
`Thunk` (`ASNIX_THUNK_SIZE`, `ir.h`) plus a whole separate child
`IrProgram` (at minimum the literal's own push op + `ib_ret`, 24 bytes
each per `ASNIX_IROP_SIZE`), forced through the full `OP_CALL`/force
machinery at every future point of use -- for a value that was already
sitting there for free.

Added `is_thunk_free_literal(Ast *node)`: true for
`AST_INT`/`AST_FLOAT`/`AST_BOOL`/`AST_NULL`/`AST_CURPOS`, true for
`AST_STRING` only when every part is non-expr (no interpolation), true
for `AST_PATH` only when `!is_search && interp_count == 0` (a plain
literal path -- a search path's lookup must still happen at eval time,
and an interpolated path still needs real work); false otherwise,
deliberately including `AST_VAR`. Gated all 10 `ib_mk_thunk` sites on
it: when true, `compile_expr` runs directly against the *outer*
builder (pushing the immediate/pooled value straight into the slot the
thunk's result would have occupied) instead of building a child
`IrBuilder`/`IrProgram` and wrapping it. Safe by construction: every
consumer of a list-element/attrs-value/call-argument/`with`-value slot
already has to tolerate either a `Thunk` or an already-forced `Value`
there (that's what `force` means everywhere in this codebase), so
substituting the immediate value for a thunk wrapping the identical
value is observably identical, just cheaper.

Measured via a temporary, since-reverted compile-time counter
(load-independent, unlike `perf stat`/wall-clock -- the machine had
several other background agents actively rebuilding/testing in this
same tree at measurement time, which corrupted an initial `perf stat`
attempt badly enough to report a nonsensical ~56B-instruction/10.7s
result; the counter sidesteps this entirely since it just counts a
compile-time decision, unaffected by concurrent CPU load):
**184,768 of 919,350 thunk-creation call sites skipped (20.1%)**
compiling `d.nix`'s real ffmpeg closure; **10,941 of 43,503 (25.2%)**
on `e.nix`'s much smaller hello closure. Every skipped site avoids a
32-byte `Thunk` plus its child `IrProgram` plus all future force-
indirection at that slot.

`make test`/`make test-e2e`/`make test-conformance`: unchanged, all
green. `make test-nix-conformance`: `pass=652 fail=6 skip=148`,
identical to the pre-existing baseline -- zero regressions.
`make test-nixpkgs-hash`: `pass=148 fail=0`, reconfirmed twice after
an initial run spuriously reported several `(crash)` failures
(`nix.outPath`, then `ncurses`/`readline`/`glibc`) that direct,
isolated re-checks (`nix-instantiate`/`./asnix` run directly on the
same attribute, no 120s-per-check timeout racing against other
processes) immediately proved were NOT real -- every flagged package
matched real Nix byte-for-byte in under 2 seconds in isolation. Root
cause: this session had multiple other background agents (and, per
`ps aux` at the time, an entirely unrelated `nix build` from a
different project on the same machine) competing for CPU, and
`test-nixpkgs-hash`'s Makefile target gives each of 296 sequential
checks its own 120-second timeout -- under enough contention, legitimate
checks occasionally miss that window and get misclassified as
`(crash)`. A clean, uncontended rerun of the full suite confirmed
`pass=148 fail=0` with no flagged packages at all.

## M91: `asnix_bshared_make_attrs` insertion sort -> `qsort`

Continuing this session's CPU-time investigation after M88 (the
`cache_own_drv_closure`/`btvec_find`/`sorted_name_order` fixes).
Re-profiled `./asnix d.nix` (`perf record -g`) looking for the next
algorithmic win. The call-graph attribution for the top two entries
turned out to be a dead end: both resolved (via `nm`/`addr2line`
against the PIE binary's load offset) to a tiny, loop-free
`utf8_encode` helper (JSON/TOML `\uXXXX` escape decoding) -- a
12-instruction leaf function with no loop cannot plausibly own ~29%
of cycles on a workload that barely touches TOML/JSON; this is a
sampling/stack-walk artifact (hand-written asm lacking the frame-
pointer chains `perf`'s unwinder expects), not a real hotspot.
Disregarded rather than chased.

Checked two other candidates the same profile flagged before finding
the real one:

- `eval_file.c`'s `import_cache_find` (a linear `strcmp` scan over
  every previously-imported file, explicitly justified in its own
  comment as "cheap relative to a full parse+compile+eval"). Measured
  directly (temporary call/step counters, reverted): 1,056 distinct
  cached files, 2,063 total lookups, ~784,000 total scan steps on
  `d.nix` -- confirmed the original judgment call still holds at this
  scale; not worth converting to a hash table for a near-zero return.
- `attrs_update.c`'s `asnix_attrs_update` (`//`) and
  `asnix_attrs_insert_dynamic` (`${k} = v;`) -- both already O(n) merge
  / O(log n) binary-search-insert, not the source of the profile's
  `__strcmp_avx2` samples attributed near them (also likely stack-walk
  noise).

The real find: `builtins_shared.c`'s `asnix_bshared_make_attrs` --
the one function every attrset-constructing builtin funnels through
(`listToAttrs`, `zipAttrsWith`, JSON/TOML object parsing,
`intersectAttrs`'s own output, `__overrides` merge, etc.) -- was a
plain insertion sort, O(n²) worst case. Instrumented directly (same
temporary-counter-then-revert technique as every other measurement
this session): **52,539 calls** evaluating `d.nix`'s ffmpeg closure,
one single call with **5,234 entries**, **~699,000 total swaps**
across all calls combined. Real, measurable, and exactly the same
shape as M88's `sorted_name_order` fix (also insertion sort -> a
proper sort, both backing attrset-related operations at real
nixpkgs's actual scale).

Fixed by sorting `(sym, original_index)` pairs via `qsort` instead of
insertion sort, then writing output entries via the sorted pairs'
`idx`. The index is carried specifically to preserve exact stability:
the insertion sort being replaced stopped swapping once `syms[j-1] <=
syms[j]`, so two equal-sym entries kept their original relative
order -- `qsort`'s own tie-breaking is unspecified by the C standard,
so without the index tie-break, a caller that (unusually) passes
duplicate syms could see a different one "win" than before. Checked
every caller of `asnix_bshared_make_attrs` (18 call sites across
builtins_json.c/toml.c/builtins_m54.c/builtins_attrs2.c/
builtins_list2.c/builtins_fetchgit.c/builtins_m23.c/
builtins_tryeval.c/builtins_flakeref.c/builtins_misc.c/compiler.c/
main.c/derivation.c): every one that could plausibly produce
duplicate syms already dedupes before calling this function (e.g.
JSON object parsing's own `existing >= 0` overwrite-in-place check,
`listToAttrs`'s own linear "first occurrence wins" dedup scan), so in
practice this function never sees duplicates today -- but preserving
the stability guarantee costs nothing and removes any risk from a
future caller that doesn't dedupe first.

(Flagged, not fixed, as out of scope for this milestone:
`listToAttrs`'s own duplicate-name dedup scan, `builtins_attrs2.c`
lines 103-106, is ALSO a linear O(n²)-shaped check -- but it's a
different function entirely, and wasn't confirmed hot in this
session's profiling, so left for a future pass rather than scope-
creeping into it here.)

Measured impact on `./asnix d.nix`: instructions **~32.6-32.9 billion
(this session's post-M88 baseline, measured fresh via an isolated
worktree checkout of M88's own commit to avoid any contamination from
concurrent unrelated changes landing on master mid-session) -> ~30.7
billion**, a further ~6% reduction (smaller than M87/M88's own
reductions, matching expectations: 699,000 swaps is real but modest
next to the previous fixes' hundreds-of-millions-of-comparisons
scale). `make test`/`make test-e2e`/`make test-conformance`: all
green. `make test-nix-conformance`: `pass=652 fail=6 skip=148`,
unchanged -- zero regressions. `make test-nixpkgs-hash`
(hash-parity-critical risk: this function underlies nearly every
attrset-constructing builtin, including several in `derivation.c`'s
own code paths): confirmed `pass=148 fail=0`, both via a clean run
and via repeated isolated re-checks of every package a *contended*
run flagged as `(crash)` (multiple heavy background agents were
running concurrently on this shared machine during this milestone's
own verification, at one point pushing load average above 30 --
every single flagged package, checked individually afterward,
evaluated successfully with no issue at all, confirming resource
contention/timeout as the cause rather than any regression from this
change -- see the M89-adjacent note elsewhere in this doc about
`test-nixpkgs-hash`'s per-check timeout under contention).
## M92: real `maybeThunk`-style Env-slot aliasing (a new `Cell` value kind) -- `eq-slot-elem`/`eq-slot-identity`/`print` all now pass, after M52/M81/M86 each independently declined the underlying gap as out of proportion

(Numbered M92, not M88, despite being planned/implemented against an M87 baseline: master had already gained M88-M91 -- all unrelated CPU/perf work, from other parallel agents -- by the time this was ready to commit. This milestone's own diff is based on the pre-M88 tree and has NOT been rebased onto M88-M91; whoever merges this should check M90 ("skip thunk-wrapping for compile-time-trivial literals") in particular, since it very likely touches the same ten `ib_mk_thunk` call sites in `compiler.c` this milestone's own `try_cell_ref` wires into -- a real semantic interaction (two independent thunk-elision optimizations at the same sites), not just textual overlap, that needs a human/agent to reconcile by hand rather than a blind rebase.)

Implemented the exact infrastructure M86's Part 2 (`eq-slot-elem.nix`/
`eq-slot-identity.nix`, re-investigated and re-declined a SECOND time)
concluded was needed and scoped out: real Nix's `Expr::maybeThunk`
slot-aliasing optimization (`~/nix/gc-unlock/src/libexpr/eval.cc`,
`ExprVar::maybeThunk`'s override of the universal "always allocate a
fresh `Value`" default), which is what lets `eqValues`'s `if (&v1 ==
&v2) return true` (eval.cc ~line 2919) and the printer's matching
`seen->insert(&v)` (print.cc ~line 412) recover genuine Value-slot
identity for a bare variable threaded through a list/attrset literal,
a call argument, or a `with`-expression -- something asnix's flat,
copied-everywhere 8-byte `Value` word had no way to express at all
before this milestone (see docs/value-encoding.md).

### The representation: `Cell`, a fourth `ASNIX_TAG_PTR` kind

`include/asnix/heap.h`: `Cell{int64_t marker == ASNIX_CELL_MARKER
(-3); Value *target;}`, riding on the exact same "reserved negative
marker in the leading word" scheme Path (`-1`)/Float (`-2`) already
established -- no new tag bit (all 8 are spent, see value.h), no
storage-layout change anywhere (every Env/List/Attrs slot already
holds one 8-byte `Value` regardless of kind). `target` is always
`&env->values[slot]` for some live (arena-allocated, never freed) Env
-- stable for the program's entire lifetime. `src/c/value_util.c`
adds `asnix_make_cell_value`/`asnix_value_is_cell`/
`asnix_cell_target`, mirroring Path/Float's own helpers exactly.

### Compiler: `try_cell_ref`, wired into all 10 `ib_mk_thunk` call sites

`src/c/compiler.c` adds two helpers:

- `scope_find_lexical`: factored out of `AST_VAR`'s own scope walk --
  scans `scope` outward for a lexical match, returning `(depth,
  slot)`. Returns 0 (not found) exactly when the name only resolves
  via a `with` fallback (or is genuinely undefined) -- `with`-sourced
  names are excluded from aliasing NOT by a special case, but simply
  because they have no fixed compile-time slot to alias in the first
  place (which `with`, if any, actually has the key is a runtime
  fact). `AST_VAR` itself was left using its own original, unchanged
  scan (not refactored to call this) to avoid touching a subtle,
  already-correct piece of code for zero behavioral gain -- both scans
  are provably equivalent (same loop shape, verified by hand against
  the real-Nix `maybeThunk`/`eval` distinction below).
- `try_cell_ref(b, node, scope)`: returns 1 (having emitted
  `OP_VAR_REF_CELL`) iff `node` is a bare `AST_VAR` that
  `scope_find_lexical` resolves; 0 otherwise (caller falls back to the
  ordinary `ib_mk_thunk` path unchanged).

Enumerated and patched every `ib_mk_thunk` call site by hand (ten,
matching the planning agent's own count): `AST_LET` binding values,
`AST_LAMBDA`-pattern field bodies (never actually fires here --
each field's body is always a synthetic `AST_SELECT`/`AST_IF`, never
a bare `AST_VAR` -- but wired for uniformity/future-proofing anyway,
at the cost of one cheap tag check), `AST_APP` call arguments, list
elements, non-`rec` attrset hidden/visible/dynamic bindings, `rec`
attrset bindings and dynamic bindings, and the `with`-expression
itself -- cross-checked against real Nix's own override list
(`eval.cc:1055-1390`: `ExprVar`/`ExprString`/`ExprInt`/`ExprFloat`/
`ExprPath`/`ExprList` -- asnix only needed the `ExprVar` one, since
string/int/float/path literals are already immediate/interned
constants with no allocation to elide, and list literals aren't a
single `ib_mk_thunk` site at all in asnix's IR, each ELEMENT is).

### Force chokepoints: Cell-transparency, five sites plus one shared helper

Enumerated every place a Thunk is force-resolved (grepped
`ASNIX_TAG_THUNK` across `src/asm`): `op_var_ref.S`, `op_select.S`,
`op_select_or.S`, `op_with.S`'s `OP_WITH_TRY`, and `force.S`'s
`asnix_force_for_print` -- five sites, not the three M78-found
scratch-buffer-cache sites (`asnix_force_for_print`/`asnix_apply`/
`asnix_eval`) the task brief's own recollection suggested; those three
are about per-recursion-depth buffer caching (a reentrant-dispatch-
context concern) and are almost entirely orthogonal to WHERE a Thunk
tag is actually interpreted. `asnix_apply`'s own entry dispatch and
`asnix_eval`'s dispatch loop never inspect a raw Thunk/Cell tag
directly -- they rely on the same five chokepoints above having
already resolved whatever they're about to read (confirmed by
tracing every caller).

Each of the five got the identical new "check Cell, not just Thunk"
block, added right where the existing code already falls through on
"not a Thunk": if the tag is `ASNIX_TAG_PTR` with the Cell marker,
call a new shared C helper, `asnix_resolve_cell_chain` (`value_util.c`),
and loop back to re-examine the result (which may still be an
unforced Thunk, or even another Cell -- chained bare-variable aliasing,
e.g. `let y = x; z = y;`, lands a raw Cell directly in `z`'s own Env
slot). Centralizing the chain-walk in ONE C function (rather than
inlining an unbounded dereference in all five .S files) is what made
it practical to bound it -- see the blackhole-regression entry below
for why that bound turned out to be load-bearing, not just tidy.

### The harder-than-expected parts (three real correctness traps, all found and fixed)

Iterating `make test`/`make test-e2e`/`make test-nix-conformance`
after the representation+compiler+force-chokepoint work above
(implemented together, then verified) surfaced three genuine
regressions/gaps the plan's own "FLAGGED OPEN RISK" section didn't
fully anticipate -- each is a real correctness issue, not a design
flaw in the overall approach, and each is now fixed:

1. **`builtins.elem`'s own primop-argument-forcing convention
   destroyed the Cell before equality ever saw it.** `elem x list`
   is arity-2, so asnix curries it into a Closure chain
   (`asnix_bshared_make_curried_native`) -- and that chain's OWN
   bytecode re-reads each captured argument via a plain `OP_VAR_REF`
   when reassembling the final native call, which (correctly, by
   design) FORCES through any Cell. By the time `elem`'s native C
   function ever ran, `x` had already been silently resolved to a
   concrete value, regardless of whether the primop itself was
   force-mode or not. Real Nix's own `prim_elem` (primops.cc)
   deliberately does NOT force its first argument before calling
   `eqValues` for exactly this reason. Fixed with a new op,
   `OP_VAR_REF_RAW` (`op_var_ref_raw.S` -- same depth/slot walk as
   `OP_VAR_REF`, zero forcing, the `OP_FRAME_GET` of depth-relative
   reads), and a new curry-chain builder,
   `asnix_bshared_make_curried_native_noforce`, that uses it instead
   of `OP_VAR_REF` for reassembly AND builds the leaf primop NOFORCE
   (skipping op_call.S's own M25 post-dispatch force-loop too) --
   used only by `elem` (`builtins_list2.c`), which now forces `list`
   manually itself but leaves `x` completely raw.
2. **The naive "Cell-identity shortcut" first draft broke
   `eval-okay-equal-function-direct-identical.nix`.** `let f = x: x;
   in f == f`'s two operands are always evaluated via the ordinary,
   always-forcing `OP_VAR_REF` (never `OP_VAR_REF_CELL` -- that's only
   emitted at `ib_mk_thunk` sites, never for an operand used directly)
   -- so by the time they reach `asnix_bshared_value_eq_op`, they're
   ALREADY the same concrete closure pointer. A blanket `a.raw ==
   b.raw` pre-force check (the first thing tried) wrongly fired on
   that bare content-identity, resurrecting exactly the bug M80 had
   already fixed. Fixed by restricting the shortcut
   (`asnix_bshared_slot_identical`, `builtins_shared.c`) to ONLY two
   cases that genuinely correspond to "same storage slot": two Cells
   with equal `target`, or two values that are literally the same raw
   THUNK (not yet forced at all) -- never a blanket check on already-
   concrete content.
3. **A pure Cell-to-Cell alias cycle has no blackhole detection,
   because Cells have no IN_PROGRESS state the way Thunks do.**
   `eval-fail-blackhole.nix` (`let { body = x; x = y; y = x; }`) used
   to abort immediately via Thunk IN_PROGRESS detection; once `x`/`y`
   became pure Cell aliases of each other (no Thunk anywhere in the
   cycle at all), the naive "dereference and loop" force-chokepoint
   logic chased Cell->Cell->Cell forever with nothing to ever notice
   the cycle -- a real hang, not a crash. This is exactly why
   `asnix_resolve_cell_chain` was centralized into one C function
   rather than inlined five times: it bounds the chase at
   `ASNIX_CELL_CHASE_LIMIT` (1,000,000 -- generous above any
   legitimate bare-variable-alias chain depth a real program would
   write, while still aborting in well under a second on a genuine
   cycle) and reports the exact same "blackhole" wording the Thunk
   path already used.

A fourth issue was a genuine, narrower regression found on the SAME
re-verification pass, not a design gap: `builtins.lessThan`'s own
list-ordering comparison (`asnix_bshared_value_lt`,
`builtins_shared.c`) force-resolved each pair of list elements BEFORE
calling `asnix_bshared_value_eq` to decide "equal, keep comparing the
next element" -- the exact same forcing-before-equality-check mistake
`elem` had, just in a different function. Found via
`eval-okay-eq-slot-sort.nix` (`lessThan [id 2] [id 1]`, where the
shared `id` element needs the Cell shortcut to avoid incorrectly
falling through to "cannot compare these two values", since the
closure-vs-closure default comparison is now unconditionally `false`,
not a pointer-identity check -- see item 2 above). Fixed by swapping
the equality check to run on the raw, pre-force elements, forcing only
if they turn out NOT equal (needed for the actual ordering
comparison).

### Equality (`src/c/builtins_shared.c`)

`asnix_bshared_slot_identical(a, b)` (see item 2 above for exactly
what it does and doesn't check) is consulted at the top of BOTH
`asnix_bshared_value_eq` (covers list/attrs-element recursion,
`elem`, `genericClosure`, `lessThan`'s ordering -- every RAW,
pre-force call site) and `asnix_bshared_value_eq_op` (covers `==`/`!=`
own direct operands, before EITHER of that function's two
`force_for_print` calls -- in practice a Cell basically never reaches
this one directly, since direct operands are always pre-resolved by
an ordinary `OP_VAR_REF`/`OP_SELECT`, but checking is cheap and keeps
the two functions symmetric). `asnix_bshared_value_eq`'s `default:`
case (closures/primops, the only tags left once Thunk is impossible
and INT/IMM/PTR/LIST/ATTRS are handled above) now unconditionally
returns false, matching real Nix's `case nFunction: return false` --
previously `a.raw == b.raw` (forced-object pointer identity), which
happened to coincide with the right answer whenever the SAME
Thunk/Cell was read from two places (no other way to express "same
slot" existed before this milestone) but gave the WRONG answer
whenever two INDEPENDENTLY-computed closures just happened to
evaluate to the literal same heap object (`[(id id)] == [(id id)]`,
`eval-okay-eq-slot-elem.nix`'s `elem foo.bar [foo.bar]`).

**Resolving the planning agent's flagged open risk**: does
`asnix_bshared_value_eq`'s list/attrs-element recursion force before
comparing? Yes, unconditionally, at the very top of the function --
confirmed by reading it directly, not inferred. This was already true
before this milestone and is NOT a latent bug on its own (the generic
equality rules for INT/IMM/PTR/LIST/ATTRS are all content-based and
correct either way) -- the actual problem this milestone had to solve
was narrower and different: the slot-identity SHORTCUT has to run
*before* that existing forcing, in every caller, which is exactly what
`asnix_bshared_slot_identical`'s placement (checked first, in both
`asnix_bshared_value_eq` and `asnix_bshared_value_eq_op`, plus the two
additional call sites `elem`/`lessThan` needed fixing at) accomplishes.

### Printer (`src/c/main.c`)

Restructured `print_value_inner` into a new `print_peel_wrappers` (new)
+ `print_value_concrete` (the old tag-dispatch switch, renamed,
unchanged except as noted below). `print_peel_wrappers` peels off
Cell/Thunk wrappers one at a time -- NOT via one opaque
`asnix_force_for_print` call -- pushing each wrapper's OWN identity (a
Cell's `target` address, or a Thunk's own heap address) onto the
existing ancestor stack (`g_print_active`) individually, exactly
mirroring real Nix's `seen->insert(&v)` (keyed by the Value SLOT's own
address, not whatever it forces to). This distinction is invisible for
every ORDINARY value, but matters for a genuinely self-referential one
built through a Cell (`let x = [x]; in x`): real Nix's `V_outer`
(the enclosing list-element's own copied Value, printed first) and
`V_x` (`x`'s own binding slot, reached one level deeper by following
the shared `elems` array back to its one pointer) are two DIFFERENT
Value-struct addresses that happen to share identical list CONTENT --
only the second, deeper encounter of `&V_x` is the actual repeat.
`ASNIX_TAG_LIST`'s own `print_value_concrete` case had its
`print_active_push`/`pop` on the forced List object's OWN address
REMOVED entirely (not just left alongside the new wrapper-level
tracking) -- keeping both caused the wrong, one-bracket-too-few
collapse, because the SAME heap List object is reachable through two
DIFFERENT wrapper chains in this exact structure, and object-address
tracking matches one level too early. List cycles are structurally
only ever reachable through a Cell or Thunk in the first place (a
plain `OP_MK_LIST` can never embed a not-yet-built list inside itself),
so the wrapper-level tracking alone is sufficient for cycle-safety,
with no loss of the PASSING `repeated-empty-list.nix`-style "siblings
aren't collapsed" behavior (lists use ancestor-only, popped semantics,
unchanged). `ASNIX_TAG_ATTRS`'s own, separate, whole-print-call
`print_attrs_seen_mark` (object-address-keyed, deliberately never
popped, for the DIFFERENT "non-ancestor sibling reuse IS collapsed"
rule attrsets need) is completely unchanged -- confirmed by hand-
tracing `let a = {x=1;}; in {p=a; q=a;}` through the new code (still
`{ p = { x = 1; }; q = «repeated»; }`) and `eval-okay-eq-slot-attrs.nix`
(all 5 cases, still `true`) that it keeps working correctly alongside
the new Cell/Thunk-level ancestor tracking, not instead of it.

### Verification

`make test-nix-conformance`: baseline (re-verified at the START of
this session, not trusted from any prior write-up) `pass=652 fail=6
skip=148` -> **`pass=655 fail=3 skip=148`** -- all three target
fixtures (`eval-okay-eq-slot-elem.nix`, `eval-okay-eq-slot-identity.nix`,
`eval-okay-print.nix`) now pass, plus `eval-okay-equal-function-direct-
identical.nix` and `eval-fail-blackhole.nix` (both briefly regressed
mid-pass by the two bugs above, confirmed fixed) and
`eval-okay-eq-slot-sort.nix` (the `lessThan` bug above, also fixed).
The remaining 3 failures (`eval-okay-getattrpos-functionargs.nix`,
`eval-okay-getattrpos.nix`, `eval-okay-inherit-attr-pos.nix`) are the
SAME pre-existing, unrelated failures present in the baseline,
untouched by this milestone. Re-ran the full suite three times in a
row to confirm `655/3/148` is stable -- an EARLIER re-run under heavy
concurrent machine load (other agents' background jobs, load average
30+ on 22 cores) spuriously showed unrelated fixtures
(`eval-okay-string.nix`, `eval-okay-attrs4.nix`, regex fixtures)
failing due to the harness's 10-second-per-fixture timeout, NOT a real
regression -- confirmed by re-running those specific fixtures directly
(sub-50ms each, byte-exact match) and by the full suite settling back
to the same stable `655/3/148` on every subsequent run.

`make test`/`make test-e2e`: fully green, no regressions (289/289 e2e
fixtures). `make test-nixpkgs-hash`: reconfirmed **`pass=148 fail=0`**
both before this milestone's changes and after -- function/closure
equality and bare-variable-alias chains are rare in real nixpkgs
evaluation (confirmed: zero behavior change across all 74 packages'
`outPath`/`drvPath` hashes).
## M93: lazy union-layering for `//` -- avoids the full-copy on every
attrset update, with a real (measured, not assumed) perf win

A prior planning-only subtask investigated but deliberately did not
implement this (invasiveness concerns); this milestone re-did the
design/analysis from scratch, found the real risk surface was larger
than that subtask's starting list, implemented it, found a real bug
in the first implementation via direct measurement (not just
"it seems correct"), fixed it, and verified the result end to end.

**Design.** `include/asnix/heap.h`'s Attrs layout (`{int64_t count;
Attr entries[count];}`, sorted by sym) reuses the leading `count`
field's sign as a sentinel: a NEGATIVE value there means this
`ASNIX_TAG_ATTRS` object is actually a `UnionHdr`, not a flat array --

```
UnionHdr{ int64_t  neg_leaf_count;  // == -(number of leaves), 1..MAX_LEAVES
          Value    flat_cache;      // raw==0 until materialized, then the
                                     // flattened+deduped, sym-sorted flat Attrs
          Value    leaves[-neg_leaf_count]; }  // lowest-priority (oldest) first;
                                                // each leaf is itself an ordinary
                                                // FLAT Attrs, never another
                                                // UnionHdr (unions never nest --
                                                // asnix_attrs_update always
                                                // resolves a would-be leaf flat
                                                // before storing it)
```

`asnix_bshared_attrs_resolve` (`builtins_shared.c`) is the one place
that knows how to turn a `UnionHdr` into its flat form: returns the
Value unchanged if already flat (one sign-bit check, the overwhelming
