guessed): `op_mk_thunk.S` (creation, now one store not two),
`builtins_shared.c`'s `make_thunk_from` (ditto), the five force-dispatch
blocks (`force.S`, `op_var_ref.S`, `op_select.S`, `op_select_or.S`,
`op_with.S`) -- each now extracts the state tag into a scratch register
(`%r8`/`%rdx`, chosen per site to avoid clobbering the live prog
pointer still held in `%rcx`) while keeping the original tagged word
around to use directly as the prog pointer on the UNFORCED path,
eliminating the old second memory read of `ASNIX_THUNK_OFF_PROG`
entirely; `op_call.S`'s `OP_RET` memoization (unchanged logic, bare
tag overwrite); `tryeval.c`'s `asnix_tryeval_unwind_inprogress`
(unchanged logic); and the two test fixtures that hand-build Thunk
cells (`tests/ir/test_m6_fixtures.c`, `tests/asm/test_stacklimits.c`),
updated to mask with `ASNIX_TAG_MASK` where they compare the
just-constructed UNFORCED state to a literal 0. `force.S` needed one
extra wrinkle: the clean prog pointer has to survive two intervening
`call`s to `asnix_force_scratch_{valstack,retstack}` (ordinary SysV
calls, clobber `%rcx`), so it's stashed in `%rbp` instead -- safe
because `%rbp`'s caller-time value is already preserved on the stack
by this function's own prologue push, leaving the register itself free
scratch until the matching `popq %rbp` in the epilogue.

Verified: `make test`/`test-e2e` all green; `test-nix-conformance`
`pass=655 fail=3 skip=148` unchanged (the 3 failures are the
pre-existing, documented `getattrpos`/`inherit-attr-pos` position-
tracking gaps, unrelated to this change); `test-nixpkgs-hash` `pass=148
fail=0` (two transient single-package timeout flakes during repeated
runs, each reproduced instantly and successfully in isolation --
shared-machine contention from this session's other concurrent
background agents, not a real regression; a clean re-run confirmed
`pass=148 fail=0`). Measured on `./asnix d.nix` (ffmpeg's real
closure): peak RSS 741,976 -> 723,820 KB (~18.2 MB, ~2.5%), same output
(`outPath` byte-identical) both before and after.

As of this commit, the concurrent Value-widening effort (which would
make a boxed `Thunk` moot entirely) had NOT landed on `master`
(`git log` still showed M102 as the latest milestone, `ASNIX_THUNK_SIZE`
still a live, referenced constant) -- this change is a genuine,
independent, smaller-scope complement to that larger effort, not a
duplicate or a race lost.

**Commit:** `include/asnix/ir.h`, `src/asm/force.S`,
`src/asm/ops/{op_call,op_mk_thunk,op_select,op_select_or,op_var_ref,op_with}.S`,
`src/c/{builtins_shared,irbuild,tryeval}.c`,
`tests/asm/test_stacklimits.c`, `tests/ir/test_m6_fixtures.c`,
`docs/architecture.md`.
## M107: bytecode cache does MORE file opens than no caching at all -- mtime+size fast path, content-hash fallback

A background research agent this session (working from a now-stale
local worktree branched at M101, before M102/M103 landed on the shared
`master` -- see this section's own "collision with M103" note below for
why that matters) found two concrete, fixable problems in the M94/M98/
M101 bytecode cache. This milestone implements the first (the open-
count regression); the second (the wire format being larger than the
source it replaced) was independently found and fixed by a *different*
parallel agent in this same session, landed as M103 -- confirmed by
`grep`-ing the live `docs/architecture.md`/`bytecode.c` on `master`
mid-task and finding M103 already does exactly this (zigzag+LEB128,
`ASNXBC01` -> `ASNXBC02`) with the same design. See the end of this
section for how that collision is handled.

### Finding 1, re-verified: the cache cost MORE opens than not caching

Re-measured directly via `strace -f -c` on `./asnix d.nix` (ffmpeg's
real 1056-file closure) before touching any code:

| | `openat` calls |
|---|---|
| cache disabled | **2444** |
| cache enabled, warm (pre-fix) | **3500** (+1056, exactly one extra open per cached file) |

Root cause confirmed exactly as the research agent described:
`asnix_bytecode_cache_lookup`'s key was `sha256(resolved_path, source
bytes)` -- computing that key required opening and reading the ENTIRE
source file on every lookup, hit or miss, before a SECOND open (the
cache entry itself) could even happen. So "caching" cost strictly more
opens than the normal compile path, not fewer.

### The fix

`bytecode_cache.c`'s on-disk entry key is now `sha256(resolved_path)`
alone (path-only, not path+content -- see `bytecode_cache.h`'s updated
header comment for why two different paths still never collide, and
why this is safe). Freshness against whatever currently lives at that
path is validated by a small fixed-width header prepended to each entry
(`CacheHeader`: `mtime_sec`/`mtime_nsec`/`size`, plus a SHA-256 content
hash as a fallback -- 72 bytes total, `CACHE_FORMAT_MAGIC
"ANXCACH1"`/`CACHE_FORMAT_VERSION`, independent of `bytecode.c`'s own
body-level magic), via two explicit steps `eval_file.c`'s
`asnix_eval_file` now calls in order:

1. **`asnix_bytecode_cache_lookup_fast`** -- takes `mtime_sec`/
   `mtime_nsec`/`size` the caller already has (see below) and does
   ZERO source-file I/O. Opens only the cache entry, reads its header,
   and if the recorded mtime+size match exactly, deserializes the body
   and returns -- a single open+read, full stop. Returns NULL + sets
   `*out_entry_exists` if an entry exists but didn't match (ambiguous:
   could be genuinely stale, or just touched) or if there's no entry at
   all (plain miss).
2. **`asnix_bytecode_cache_lookup_verify`** -- only called when step 1
   found a mismatched entry. The caller has, by this point, already
   read the source file anyway (an ordinary cache-miss recompile would
   have needed to regardless), so this computes a real content hash and
   compares it against the one recorded in the SAME entry, distinguishing
   "mtime drifted but content is byte-identical" (e.g. `touch(1)`) from
   "genuinely different file." On a content match it also re-stores the
   entry with the FRESH mtime/size (atomically, via the same write-temp-
   then-rename path `asnix_bytecode_cache_store` always used) -- a
   self-heal that restores the fast path for this path next time, at a
   one-time cost.

**Where the mtime/size come from, free:** `eval_file.c`'s own path
resolution (`resolve_file_path`, built on M83's `follow_symlink_chain`)
already calls `lstat()` on the final target as part of following a
symlink chain -- `follow_symlink_chain` now returns that `struct stat`
directly (instead of just a `is_dir` bool) so the common direct-file-
import case reuses it with **zero additional syscalls**. The one
exception: `import <directory>` resolves to `<directory>/default.nix`,
whose own mtime/size the directory's stat doesn't describe -- one more
`stat()` (not `lstat()`, matching what `fopen`/`fread` would
transparently follow anyway) is genuinely unavoidable there. This is
gated behind `asnix_bytecode_cache_enabled()` so it costs nothing when
the cache is off (see the regression below).

### A regression found and fixed before landing

An earlier version of this fix called that one extra `stat()`
unconditionally inside `resolve_file_path`, regardless of whether the
cache was even enabled -- which silently violated this whole exercise's
own non-negotiable constraint that cache-disabled behavior stay
provably unaffected. Caught directly via the same `strace -f -c`
discipline used to verify the fix in the first place: the disabled
baseline's `newfstatat` count moved from 35587 to 36228 (+641, one per
directory-style import in ffmpeg's closure) purely from code that
should never execute when `ASNIX_BYTECODE_CACHE` isn't set. Fixed by
gating that one `stat()` call behind `asnix_bytecode_cache_enabled()`;
re-verified the disabled baseline is syscall-for-syscall identical
again (`openat`=2444, `newfstatat`=35587, matching the pre-change
numbers exactly).

### One real, expected, harmless edge case found while verifying

`ASNIX_BYTECODE_CACHE_STATS=1` on `d.nix`'s warm-cache run consistently
reports `1056 hits (1055 fast-path, 1 content-verified)`, never
`1056/0`. Tracked down to `compiler.c`'s `ASNIX_FETCHURL_TEMP_PATH`
(`/tmp/.asnix-corepkgs-fetchurl.nix`) -- asnix's own embedded
`<nix/fetchurl.nix>` corepkgs stub, rewritten fresh to a fixed `/tmp`
path on every single invocation. Same content every time, but by
construction a brand-new mtime every run -- self-heal can't fix a file
whose mtime changes on every read. This is precisely the documented
mtime+size-heuristic tradeoff (see `bytecode_cache.h`'s own comment:
the same one ccache's default mode and Nix's own eval cache both
accept) firing correctly: never a wrong answer (output stayed byte-
identical in every verification run below), just a permanently-skipped
fast path for this one synthetic file out of 1056.

### Verification

`make test`/`make test-e2e`: unchanged, all green, cache disabled.
`make test-nix-conformance`: `pass=655 fail=3 skip=148` -- identical to
the session's own re-verified baseline (the three failures are the
pre-existing, unrelated `getattrpos`/`inherit-attr-pos` gaps) -- checked
both with the cache disabled and with `ASNIX_BYTECODE_CACHE=1` pointed
at a fresh private cache dir, cold AND warm, all four runs giving the
identical `pass=655 fail=3 skip=148`.

`make test-nixpkgs-hash` (the gating one): `pass=148 fail=0` with the
cache disabled (the default) -- re-confirmed after one transient
`fail=1` (`patch.outPath(crash)`) that reproduced as a clean pass on
immediate re-run, matching M94's own documented pattern of this
specific shared machine's heavy concurrent-agent load producing false-
positive crashes under `make test-nixpkgs-hash`'s 120s-per-attribute
timeout, not a real regression. Also ran the full 74-package corpus
with `ASNIX_BYTECODE_CACHE=1` against a fresh private cache dir, both
cold (populates it) and warm (exercises the fast+verify lookup paths):
`pass=148 fail=0` both times, each compared against real
`nix-instantiate --eval` output exactly like the default-path run.
Also ran with `ASNIX_BYTECODE_PRODUCER=1` layered on top (the M92
fork-based prefetch producer, which also calls the new
`asnix_bytecode_cache_store` signature) -- `pass=148 fail=0` on
re-run (one transient `python3.src.drvPath(crash)` on the first attempt,
same shared-machine-load pattern as above), with no leftover zombie/
orphan processes (`ps aux` clean after the run).

### Measured, before/after, on `d.nix`'s real ffmpeg closure (1056 files)

| | cache disabled | warm cache, **pre**-fix | warm cache, **post**-fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| `openat` calls (`strace -f -c`) | 2444 | 3500 (+1056) | **2447** (+3) |
| `newfstatat` calls | 35587 | 35587 | 36228 (+641, cache-enabled-only `default.nix` re-stats) |
| cache dir size (1056 entries) | n/a | 91MB (pre-M103 format) | 32MB (post-M103 format, this worktree already includes M103's own fix -- see collision note) |
| `./asnix d.nix` output | baseline | byte-identical | byte-identical |

The remaining +3 opens (not a strict `<=` vs. the disabled baseline)
are fully accounted for by the one self-regenerating stub file from the
section above: its one occurrence needs an open for the source (needed
anyway), a first open of the cache entry (the fast-path attempt, which
mismatches), a second open of the same cache entry (the verify-path
re-read), and one more for the self-heal's temp-file write -- 4 opens
for that one file against the disabled baseline's 1, i.e. +3 overall
across all 1056 files. Judged not worth eliminating (would mean either
dropping the self-heal, which only shifts the same file's cost from
"every run" to "every run anyway, just 1 fewer open," or hard-coding a
special case for a single internal temp file) -- documenting the exact,
fully-understood cause here rather than chasing the last 3 syscalls.

Wall-clock (`hyperfine`, shared machine, `--warmup 2-3`, 20-25 runs,
`ASNIX_BYTECODE_CACHE_DIR` pointed at a private, pre-warmed cache):
**1.16x-1.23x** across two separate measurement runs (noisy -- hyperfine
flagged statistical outliers on this heavily loaded shared machine both
times), consistent with or slightly better than M101's own previously-
measured ~1.1-1.2x and close to M101's own computed ceiling (lex+parse+
compile is only ~200ms of `d.nix`'s ~1.6-2.1s total; a bytecode cache
structurally cannot do better than eliminating that phase alone).

### Collision with M103 -- how it's handled

This work was done in an isolated git worktree branched from `master`
at M101, per this session's standard parallel-agent workflow. Partway
through, a live check of the shared `master` checkout (required by this
task's own "re-verify the next-free milestone number, don't guess"
instruction) found that M102 and M103 had already landed from OTHER
parallel agents -- and M103 is, independently, almost exactly the
"Finding 2" wire-format fix this task also asked for (same zigzag+
LEB128 scheme, same `ASNXBC01`->`ASNXBC02` magic bump, arrived at
independently). This worktree's own `src/c/bytecode.c` change (done
before that discovery) is functionally equivalent to M103's, including
by coincidence the identical magic-number choice, and was kept rather
than reverted since: (1) it's correct and fully verified here, (2) this
worktree's Finding-1 fix below is written and tested against a
`bytecode.c` that already has the M103-equivalent varint change in
place (both fixes share the cache-format-version-bump discipline), and
(3) de-duplicating against M103's specific diff is an integration
concern for whoever merges this branch onto the now-current `master`,
not something resolvable from inside an isolated worktree with no
access to rewrite `master`'s own history. **Whoever integrates this
branch should take only this milestone's `bytecode_cache.c`/
`bytecode_cache.h`/`eval_file.c` changes (the actual novel content --
the mtime+size fast path, nowhere else in the codebase as of this
writing) and skip re-applying this branch's redundant `bytecode.c` diff
on top of M103's already-landed one.**

**Commit:** `src/c/bytecode.c` (redundant with M103, see above),
`src/c/bytecode_cache.c`, `src/c/bytecode_cache.h`, `src/c/eval_file.c`,
`docs/architecture.md`.

## M108: a permanent `ASNIX_SHOW_STATS=1` object-count feature, modeled on real Nix's `NIX_SHOW_STATS=1`

This session's memory-gap investigations repeatedly re-derived the same
per-category allocation counts (envs/thunks/closures/attrs/lists/cells/
strings/primops/paths) via temporary, reverted instrumentation (an arena
allocation-site tracer read back through `addr2line`) -- every fresh
investigation started from zero. This milestone makes those counts a
permanent, always-available feature instead: plain `.bss` global
counters (`include/asnix/stats.h`/`src/c/stats.c`), incremented
unconditionally at each category's real allocation site (a bare
`incq`/`++` is cheap enough to always pay), with printing gated behind
`ASNIX_SHOW_STATS=1` (silent no-op otherwise), dumped to stderr at the
same exit point M98's `ASNIX_BYTECODE_CACHE_STATS` already uses.

**The one real bug found while building this**: `asnix_env_alloc`
(`src/asm/env.S`) looked like the one place Env frames get allocated,
but the file's own header comment already said otherwise --
"`op_var_ref`/`op_let`/`op_call` inline the same logic directly in the
hot dispatch path rather than paying a `call` per use". A first pass
instrumenting only `asnix_env_alloc` undercounted envs by ~3.1x
(533,486 vs the true 1,675,074) on `d.nix`'s real ffmpeg closure.
Found and instrumented the four actually-dominant inlined sites by
grepping for `ASNIX_ENV_OFF_UP` directly instead of trusting the one
named helper: `op_frame.S` (`let`/`rec {}`/attrset frames -- the
largest contributor), `op_let.S`, `op_call.S` (closure-call argument
frames), `op_with.S` (always-1-slot with-frames), and `apply.S`
(`builtins.*`-driven calls, a separate call path from `op_call.S`'s
in-language one).

**Cross-checked against this session's own independent measurement**:
after instrumenting all five sites, `envs=1,675,074` / `thunks=2,342,967`
/ `cells=836,471` on `d.nix` match the arena allocation-site tracer's
own numbers from `docs/memory-accounting-asnix-vs-nix.md` exactly --
strong confirmation this feature counts correctly, not just
plausibly.

**Environment note for whoever reviews this**: this worktree was
shared with (at least) one other concurrent, unrelated change in
progress (`src/c/ast.c`/`ast.h`'s AST-arena-freeing optimization and
`src/c/attrs_update.c`'s attrs-layering threshold retuning, plus
`eval_file.c`'s wiring for the former) -- confirmed broken on its own
(`asnix: undefined variable 'list'` on both `hello.drvPath` and
`ffmpeg.outPath`, reproducible, unrelated to this milestone's own
changes: verified by stashing those four files out, confirming this
milestone's own changes evaluate both correctly on the clean baseline,
then restoring them exactly as found). This commit deliberately does
NOT touch or fix that unrelated, in-progress, currently-broken work --
out of scope for this directive, left for whoever owns it.

Verified (on the clean baseline, i.e. with the unrelated WIP above
stashed out): `make test`/`test-e2e`/`test-conformance` all green;
`make test-nix-conformance`: `pass=655 fail=3 skip=148`, unchanged;
`make test-nixpkgs-hash`: `pass=148 fail=0`, unchanged; `./asnix d.nix`/
`e.nix` still match their known-correct hashes exactly.

**Commit:** `include/asnix/stats.h` (new), `src/c/stats.c` (new),
`src/asm/env.S`, `src/asm/ops/{op_frame,op_let,op_call,op_with,
op_mk_thunk,op_lambda,op_mk_attrs,op_mk_list}.S`, `src/asm/apply.S`,
`src/c/builtins_shared.c`, `src/c/value_util.c`, `src/c/main.c`,
`docs/architecture.md`.

## M109: ported real Nix's `IndexedCallDescriptor` (`tomberek/nix#52`) to `mapAttrs`/`zipAttrsWith` -- shared `f` Env instead of a fresh one per attribute

User-prompted follow-up to the architecture discussion earlier this
session on why `UnionHdr` is heavier than real Nix's `Bindings`
layering, and to a sibling investigation into whether `mapAttrs` could
avoid its 2-arg curried-call overhead (that one correctly declined a
general fix as architecture-sized, since asnix has no multi-arg
call-chain flattening anywhere). This milestone ports a real, narrower,
already-measured-upstream idea instead: `tomberek/nix#52`'s
`IndexedCallDescriptor`.

**What real Nix's PR does**: `mapAttrs`/`zipAttrsWith`-shaped per-
attribute lazy calls all share the same mapping function `f` across N
attributes. The PR adds a `tIndexedCall` Value kind riding on real
Nix's existing "pair of pointers" storage (zero new allocation shape,
since `tApp`/`tThunk`/`tLambda` already share that slot): one
`IndexedCallDescriptor{fun, original}` per call, and one
`IndexedCallThunk{descriptor, packedIndex}` per attribute -- resolved
lazily on force by looking up the attribute at `index` directly and
calling `fun` on it. Real Nix measured -2.1% to -4.2% peak RSS.

**What was ported here -- the narrower half of the idea.** Full parity
with the PR would mean a new asnix Value kind (following M92's `Cell`
precedent -- a reserved negative marker riding on `ASNIX_TAG_PTR`,
`ASNIX_CELL_MARKER` is `-3`, this would be `-4`) plus a new force-path
case resolving `(descriptor, index)` into `(name, value)` by indexing
into the original attrset -- which, for a layered `UnionHdr` original,
would additionally need to reuse M93's own leaf-walk logic. That's real
new asm/force-path work, correctness-sensitive given it's the hottest
code in the interpreter, and was judged out of scope for a one-shot
pass (same discipline as declining the general curried-call fix).

Ported the *allocation-sharing* half instead, which needs none of that:
`asnix_bshared_make_lazy_call2` (`builtins_shared.c`) already builds
one `Thunk` per attribute, each wrapping a fresh 3-slot `Env` holding
`{f, name_val, origvalue}` -- but `f` is identical across every one of
the N thunks a single `mapAttrs`/`zipAttrsWith` call produces, so
re-storing it N times is pure waste. Added:

- `asnix_bshared_make_call2_shared_env(Value f)`: allocates ONE 1-slot
  `Env{values[0]=f}` with `up=NULL`, called once per builtin call,
  before the per-attribute loop.
- `asnix_bshared_make_lazy_call2_indexed(Env *shared, arg1, arg2)`: the
  same `(f arg1) arg2` bytecode body as the generic function, except
  `f` is read via `ib_var_ref(b, 1, 0)` (depth=1, one `up` hop into
  `shared`) instead of depth=0, and the per-attribute `Env` only needs
  2 slots `{arg1, arg2}` with `up=shared`.

Both `prim_mapAttrs_apply2` (`builtins_attrs.c`) and `zipAttrsWith`'s
own implementation (`builtins_m54.c`) now build the shared Env once and
call the indexed variant per attribute/key, instead of the generic
3-slot version.

**Size win per thunk**: `Env(3 slots)=8+24=32B + Thunk=16B = 48B` (old)
-> `Env(2 slots)=8+16=24B + Thunk=16B = 40B` (new), ~17% smaller per
attribute -- the one shared 1-slot Env (24B) is a fixed, one-time cost
per `mapAttrs`/`zipAttrsWith` *call*, not per attribute, so it
amortizes away for any non-trivial attrset.

**Correctness, verified directly, not just via the fixture suite**:
- `builtins.attrNames (builtins.mapAttrs builtins.throw { a = 1; b = 2;
  })` -> `[ "a" "b" ]`, does NOT throw -- confirms the real-Nix-matching
  laziness canary (M18/M23's own fix) still holds: `f` being read one
  `up`-hop away doesn't force it or anything else prematurely.
- `let m = builtins.mapAttrs (n: v: n + "=" + toString v) { a = 1; b =
  2; }; in [ m.a m.b ]` -> `[ "a=1" "b=2" ]` -- correctness of the
  depth-1 `f` read plus the 2-slot per-attribute Env.
- `builtins.zipAttrsWith (n: vs: builtins.foldl (a: b: a + b) 0 vs) [ {
  a = 1; b = 2; } { a = 10; b = 20; } ]` -> `{ a = 11; b = 22; }`.

`make test`/`make test-e2e`/`make test-conformance`: unchanged, all
green. `make test-nix-conformance`: `pass=655 fail=3 skip=148`,
identical to the pre-existing baseline. `make test-nixpkgs-hash`:
`pass=148 fail=0` (hash-parity harness unaffected, as expected -- this
touches builtin-call allocation shape, not derivation/hash machinery).

**Measured real-world impact**: before/after RSS on `./asnix d.nix`
(real nixpkgs's `ffmpeg.outPath`), measured by stashing and restoring
this milestone's own diff within the same build to eliminate
machine-load noise between runs: **674,584 KB -> 670,796 KB (~0.56%
reduction)**. Modest, honestly reported as modest -- real Nix's own
measured gain for the identical idea was -2.1% to -4.2%, and ffmpeg's
actual dependency closure apparently doesn't lean on `mapAttrs`/
`zipAttrsWith` heavily enough to see the larger end of that range. The
win should scale with how `mapAttrs`/`zipAttrsWith`-heavy a given
nixpkgs evaluation actually is -- not separately measured here beyond
the one real workload this session has consistently used as its
yardstick.

**Left as a documented follow-on, not attempted**: the fuller
`IndexedCallThunk` design (deferring the attribute-name `String`'s
construction until the thunk is actually forced, eliminating today's
eager `asnix_make_string_value` call for every attribute regardless of
whether it's ever forced) -- real correctness-sensitive work needing a
new Value kind and force-path case, flagged for a dedicated pass if the
`ASNIX_SHOW_STATS`-measured `mapAttrs`/`zipAttrsWith` call volume on a
`mapAttrs`-heavy real nixpkgs evaluation ever justifies it.
## M110: Ast nodes freed after compile -- fixing a prior attempt's real bug (malloc vs. zero-filled arena)

An earlier attempt this session at freeing an Ast tree right after
compiling it (same idea as M87's `toks` free, extended to the AST)
passed `make test`/`test-e2e`/`test-conformance` cleanly but crashed on
the real workload: `./asnix d.nix` (ffmpeg's closure) failed with
`undefined variable 'list'`, and several real nixpkgs packages
(`glib`, `gtk3`, `nix`) crashed in `test-nixpkgs-hash`. The small
fixture suite never exercised this because the bug only manifests once
the chunk allocator's memory gets reused enough times across many real
files -- something the handful of tiny `tests/e2e`/`tests/conformance`
fixtures never do.

**Root-caused via a targeted A/B test, not by reading code until something
looked wrong.** The error site (`compiler.c`'s "undefined variable"
fprintf) fires at COMPILE time, reading `node->as.var.name` off the
Ast node currently being compiled -- which can't be stale, since
nothing is freed until that file's whole compile() call returns. That
ruled out the obvious "stale Ast* read after free" theory. Poisoning
every freed chunk with `0xAA` before `free()` (to force any genuine
use-after-free to read obvious garbage) changed nothing -- same exact
error, same exact variable name, every time. That ruled out use-after-free
entirely.

The actual bug: `asnix_ast_new()`'s chunk allocator used plain
`malloc(sizeof(AstChunk))` for each fresh chunk. The arena it replaced
is backed by `mmap(MAP_ANONYMOUS)`, which the kernel zero-fills on
first access -- so every `Ast` node's fields that weren't explicitly
set by whichever constructor built it happened to read back as zero,
for the entire life of this project, with nobody ever having to notice
or rely on that *consciously*. `asnix_ast_new()` itself only ever sets
`n->kind`; the `as` union's node-kind-specific fields are initialized
field-by-field by each AST_* construction site in `parser.c`, and at
least one of those sites apparently leaves some field unset on the
assumption that it'll read back as zero/null. Once chunk memory starts
coming from `malloc` (uninitialized) and starts getting genuinely
*reused* across multiple files' compiles (freed, then re-malloc'd for
the next file, very plausibly handed back the exact same address),
that implicit zero-initialization assumption breaks, and a later file's
Ast node can inherit a previous file's stale field value for whichever
field its own constructor forgot to set.

**The fix**: `malloc(sizeof(AstChunk))` -> `calloc(1, sizeof(AstChunk))`.
One word. Confirmed via the same real-workload test that caught the
original bug: `./asnix d.nix` now produces the correct, known ffmpeg
hash, and the previously-crashing `test-nixpkgs-hash` packages
(`glib`/`gtk3`/`nix`) now pass.

This is a general lesson worth stating plainly for any FUTURE allocator
swap in this codebase: the main arena's `mmap`-backed zero-fill is a
silent, free correctness property every allocation in this project has
always had, whether or not any individual call site's author knew they
were relying on it. Any new allocator introduced to replace a slice of
the main arena (as this milestone and M87 both do) needs to either
preserve that property (`calloc`, or an explicit `memset` after
`malloc`) or audit every consumer for implicit zero-reliance -- the
former is cheap insurance, the latter is not something a single
investigation can realistically guarantee exhaustively.

**Measured, paired, same build**: peak RSS on `./asnix d.nix`, before
(AST living forever in the main arena) vs. after (freed per-file),
measured back-to-back in the same worktree/build to eliminate
machine-noise confounds: **736,920 KB -> 691,780 KB (~6.2% reduction)**.
Smaller than the ~101-114 MB raw AST-node byte count measured earlier
this session by independent investigations (the full theoretical
saving), consistent with chunk-size rounding and some AST memory
genuinely needing to outlive a single file's own compile call (e.g.
`asnix_bytecode_prefetch_imports` reads the AST after `asnix_compile`
returns but before the reset call, by design).

`make test`/`test-e2e`/`test-conformance`: unchanged, all green (one
transient `pass=654 fail=4` run reproduced as a clean `pass=655 fail=3`
on immediate retry -- the same shared-machine flakiness pattern
documented elsewhere in this file, not a real regression).
`make test-nix-conformance`: `pass=655 fail=3 skip=148`, identical to
the pre-existing baseline. `make test-nixpkgs-hash`: **`pass=148
fail=0`**, including the specific packages that crashed under the
original broken attempt.
## M111: `asnix_bshared_attrs_probe` -- point lookups on a lazy union no longer materialize

The user asked why asnix's `UnionHdr` (M88/M93's lazy `//`-layering) ends
up heavier than real Nix's layered `Bindings` in practice, and whether
it's fixable. Tracing the actual access path found the real answer isn't
primarily about struct-shape size (a `UnionHdr` header is cheap: 24 bytes
+ up to 64 leaf pointers) -- it's that **every single access, including
a plain `a.b` point lookup wanting exactly one key, fully flattens and
caches ALL leaves first**, via `asnix_bshared_attrs_resolve`
(`builtins_shared.c`) -- confirmed by reading every call site
(`asnix_bshared_attrs_find`/`_count`/`_sym`/`_value` all call it
unconditionally, and `op_select.S`'s own inlined fast path does too).
That means M88's lazy deferral provides essentially zero benefit the
moment a `//` result is read even once, which is nearly always true --
why build `a // b` and never touch it?

Real Nix's own layered `Bindings::get()` never has this problem: a point
lookup walks the layer chain directly (binary-search the top layer, fall
through to `baseLayer` on miss), with no flattened view ever required
unless something genuinely needs full iteration.

Added `asnix_bshared_attrs_probe(Value attrs, uint32_t sym, Value
*out_value)` (`builtins_shared.c`): for a flat attrs, an ordinary binary
search; for a union, walks `leaves` from **highest priority (last-
stored) to lowest** -- matching `//`'s right-biased override semantics,
confirmed directly against heap.h's own "`leaves` stored lowest-
priority-first" comment -- binary-searching each flat leaf directly and
returning on the first hit. Never touches `flat_cache`, never
allocates, never mutates the union. If the union was already
materialized by an earlier full-iteration caller, probes the cached
flat form directly instead (one binary search, no leaf-walk needed) --
correctness confirmed by direct test: `merged.a` read, then `attrNames
merged` (forces materialization), then `merged.b` read again, all
returned correct values.

Wired into `op_select.S`'s union branch only -- the single hottest,
most common real-world attrs operation (`a.b` in compiled Nix source)
-- replacing the `call asnix_bshared_attrs_resolve` sequence with a
call to the new probe, jumping directly into the shared thunk-forcing/
Cell-check/push logic (`.Lselect_resolve`) on a hit, or straight to the
existing `.Lselect_missing` fatal-error path on a genuine miss (the
probe already checked every leaf, so a miss there needs no fallback
re-check). Deliberately NOT applied to `asnix_bshared_attrs_find`/
`_count`/`_sym`/`_value`: their 35+ callers expect a stable *positional
index* into `v`'s own flat form (most immediately turn around and call
`attrs_value(v, idx)`), which a bounded leaf-probe can't provide without
materializing anyway -- changing that contract would need auditing
every one of those sites, out of scope for this fix.

**Caught and fixed one bug in my own edit before landing**: an
incomplete anchor match when patching `op_select.S` left a duplicate
`.Lselect_resolved:` label and an orphaned, now-dead "reload count"
instruction between the new probe path and the pre-existing flat-case
fallthrough -- would have been a hard assembler error (duplicate
label), caught immediately on the first build attempt, fixed before any
testing.

**Correctness verified directly**, not just via the test suite:
override semantics (`big // small` with a 17-entry LHS/2-entry RHS,
above/below M88's thresholds respectively, so genuinely builds a
`UnionHdr`) -- confirmed right-biased override, fallthrough for
non-overridden keys, missing-key fatal error unchanged, repeated access
before/after materialization, and a chained double-union (`(big // {a})
// {b,z}`) all give correct results.

`make test`/`test-e2e`/`test-conformance`: unchanged, all green.
`make test-nix-conformance`: `pass=655 fail=3 skip=148`, exact baseline
match (one transient regex-timeout flake on a contended run reproduced
clean in isolation and on rerun, not a real regression). `make
test-nixpkgs-hash`: `pass=148 fail=0` (one transient `bash.outPath`
crash on a contended run, same pattern, reproduced clean in isolation
and on rerun).

**Measured impact on `./asnix d.nix`** (real nixpkgs's `ffmpeg.outPath`,
`perf stat -r 3` / `/usr/bin/time -v`, against an M108 baseline built
side-by-side in a separate worktree for a clean comparison): peak RSS
**673,748 -> 665,108 KB (~1.3% reduction)** -- small but real. Instructions
**10.874B -> 10.938B**, essentially flat (within the ~0.7-0.8% run-to-run
measurement noise observed on both sides) -- not a clear win or loss on
CPU. The modest size of the RSS win is itself informative: it confirms
(rather than just asserts) that most unions in this real workload DO
eventually get fully materialized via some OTHER access path anyway
(`attrNames`, the printer, `derivation.c`'s own input-collection walk,
JSON encoding) regardless of this fix -- this fix only helps the subset
of unions that are read ONLY via point lookups and never via full
iteration, a real but limited class, not the dominant one. Consistent
with M93's own "roughly a wash on the real ffmpeg workload" finding and
the sibling fork's finding that *more* deferral (porting real Nix's
relative-size heuristic) made things *worse* -- the structural
overhead this milestone targets (forced full materialization on every
touch) was real and is now fixed for the single most common access
pattern, but the remaining materialize-on-full-iteration cost is
inherent to needing a flat, indexable, deduped view at all, and wasn't
and isn't attempted here.

## M112: `asnix_stats_attrs` now counts `asnix_attrs_eager_merge`'s real volume

A dedicated investigation into an "unattributed" ~142MB gap in the
arena (found by manually tallying `ASNIX_SHOW_STATS=1`'s counts x
exact struct sizes, and coming up ~42% short of
`asnix_arena.total_allocated`) traced the gap to `attrs_eager_merge`
(the `//`-operator eager-copy path, `attrs_update.c`): it allocates
worst-case-sized buffers for every eager merge but never incremented
`asnix_stats_attrs`/`asnix_stats_attrs_entries` (M108), making its
real cost -- measured independently at 116.0 MB across 158,007 calls,
nearly the entire gap -- completely invisible to the stats feature.

Added the missing increment at the end of the function, using the
actual post-dedup entry count (`k`, the real stored-entry count) rather
than the worst-case `acount+bcount` upper bound that gets allocated --
matching the convention `asnix_bshared_make_attrs` already uses
elsewhere in this file for the same reason (the stats feature should
report real occupancy, not allocated capacity).

`ASNIX_SHOW_STATS=1 ./asnix d.nix`: `sets` 246,871 -> 404,878,
`entries` 1,314,751 -> 10,742,641 -- this one call site alone now
accounts for the majority of both counters, matching its already-
established status as the single largest named allocation site in the
whole program.

`make test`/`test-e2e`/`test-conformance` unchanged, all green.
`make test-nix-conformance`: `pass=655 fail=3 skip=148` unchanged.
`make test-nixpkgs-hash`: `pass=148 fail=0` unchanged.

## M113: fuse mapAttrs/zipAttrsWith's per-element Env+Thunk into one allocation

The thunk/env-count investigation (see `docs/memory-accounting-asnix-
vs-nix.md`) found `map`/`mapAttrs`/`zipAttrsWith` allocate 2 separate
heap objects (one `Env`, one `Thunk`) per output element where real
Nix's own `FunctionApplicationThunk` mechanism needs something closer
to 1 -- the single largest contributor to both the env-count gap
(53.1%) and the thunk-count gap (48.3%) versus real Nix.

`asnix_bshared_make_lazy_call2_indexed`'s Env is private to exactly
one Thunk, created and consumed as a pair every time, never shared or
aliased elsewhere. Fused them into one `asnix_arena_alloc` call
(Thunk's 16 bytes immediately followed by the Env's 24 bytes in the
same block) instead of two separate allocations -- the Thunk's `env`
field is still just a plain pointer afterward, now computed to point
into the same block rather than a separately-allocated one, so this is
invisible to force.S or any other consumer. No new Value kind, no new
force-path case, unlike the fuller real-Nix-equivalent redesign (which
needs both and is already correctly deferred as a dedicated milestone).

Reduces mapAttrs/zipAttrsWith's own per-element allocation CALL count
2N -> N (same total bytes -- this is a call-count/instruction-count
optimization, not a memory-size one).

Verified directly: mapAttrs correctness (`mapAttrs (n: v: n +
toString v) {a=1;b=2;c=3;}` -> `{a="a1"; b="b2"; c="c3";}`), the
mapAttrs laziness canary (`attrNames (mapAttrs throw {...})` doesn't
throw), zipAttrsWith correctness. `make test`/`test-e2e`/
`test-conformance` all green (one transient flake on a rerun,
reproduced clean immediately after, matching this session's own
documented contention-flakiness pattern). `make test-nix-conformance`:
`pass=655 fail=3 skip=148` unchanged. `make test-nixpkgs-hash`:
`pass=148 fail=0` unchanged.

## M114: non-rec `{ ... }` with no hidden `inherit (expr)` slots skips `ib_frame_alloc` entirely -- real Nix never allocates an Env for this case either

A dedicated investigation this session (reading real Nix's `eval.cc`
directly against `compiler.c`) found: `compiler.c`'s `AST_ATTRSET`
non-`rec` branch unconditionally emitted `ib_frame_alloc(b, hidden_count)`
even when `hidden_count == 0` -- the overwhelming common case (any plain
`{ a = 1; b = foo; }` with no `inherit (expr) a b;` clause has
`hidden_count == 0`). `op_frame.S`'s `asnix_op_frame_alloc` unconditionally
calls `asnix_arena_alloc` and increments the env stats counter regardless
of slot count -- 0 slots still cost a real `Env` header allocation. Real
Nix's own non-recursive `ExprAttrs::eval` never allocates an `Env` at all
for this case: a non-`rec` attrset literal's bindings don't need their own
recursive scope (only `rec {}` and `let` need a frame, because only THOSE
let sibling bindings see each other -- a plain `{ a = 1; b = foo; }` has
`foo` resolve in the ENCLOSING scope, not against sibling `a`).

M80 had added a small, always-present `hidden_frame` (with `.up = scope`)
specifically so a multi-name `inherit (expr) a b;` clause's synthetic
shared slot has somewhere to live -- correct and necessary when
`hidden_count > 0`, but paid for unconditionally even when there is no
hidden slot at all, which is the normal case for almost every attrset
literal in real Nix code.

**The fix**: when `hidden_count == 0`, skip `ib_frame_alloc`/
`ib_frame_exit`/`hidden_frame` entirely and compile every binding's value
(and every `${expr} = value;` dynamic binding, M67) directly against the
ENCLOSING `scope` -- mechanically identical to real Nix's own
`ExprAttrs::eval` for this shape. The `hidden_count > 0` path (M80's own
fix for a real double-eval/self-reference bug, confirmed by
`eval-okay-getattrpos.nix`) is untouched and still takes the original
frame-allocating path exactly as before.

**Measured directly against real master (M113's tip), paired same-build
before/after, `./asnix d.nix` (real nixpkgs's `ffmpeg.outPath`)**:
- envs: **1,684,904 -> 1,494,995 (-189,909, -11.3%)** -- matches this
  session's own thunk/env-count investigation's predicted ~189,914-env
  reduction (20% of asnix's total env-count gap against real Nix for this
  evaluation) almost exactly.
- output hash unchanged: `/nix/store/29iacg6h530yx7rxz4k1fhvi0kxxhsam-ffmpeg-9.0.1-bin`,
  identical before and after.

`make test`/`make test-e2e`/`make test-conformance`: all green, no
regressions. `make test-nix-conformance`: `pass=655 fail=3 skip=148`,
identical before and after -- same 3 pre-existing, unrelated failures
(`eval-okay-getattrpos-functionargs.nix`, `eval-okay-getattrpos.nix`,
`eval-okay-inherit-attr-pos.nix`, all pos-tracking gaps, not Env-shape
related). `make test-nixpkgs-hash`: **`pass=148 fail=0`**, unchanged.

## M115: `read_file`'s source-text buffer freed after compile -- the one buffer M87 (tokens) and M110 (AST) left leaking

M87 freed the lexer's token array and M110 freed the AST itself once
`asnix_compile` is done with each, but `read_file`'s own return value
(`char *src`, the whole file's raw bytes) was never freed at any of its
5 call sites in `eval_file.c` -- a plain, unconditional leak for the
life of the process. An earlier investigation this session measured
this at ~24.41 MB of logical bytes, summed across a real nixpkgs
closure's ~1,057 imported files (`./asnix d.nix`, ffmpeg's closure).

**The one real subtlety**: `Ast` nodes don't copy strings out of `src`
-- `AstBinding.name`/`AstFormal.name` point directly into it (same
"names/strings point into src, not into toks" fact M87's own `free(toks)`
comment already relies on) -- so `src` must stay alive through the
*whole* `asnix_compile`/`asnix_compile_scoped` call, not just through
`asnix_parse`. That's trivially true in the main hot path
(`asnix_eval_file`): `src` is read, compiled, and could be freed all in
the same function scope, with nothing downstream (the already-reset
`Ast`, the compiled `IrProgram`) retaining a pointer into it afterward.
It was NOT already true for the other two real call sites:
`parse_resolved_file` (shared by `asnix_eval_file_for_derivation_bootstrap`
and `asnix_eval_file_scoped` via `parse_file`) read `src` locally and
returned only the `Ast*`, with the caller's own `asnix_compile` call
happening afterward in a DIFFERENT function -- freeing `src` inside
`parse_resolved_file` itself would have freed it out from under the
caller's still-pending compile. Fixed by threading a new `src_out`
parameter through `parse_resolved_file` -> `parse_file` so both callers
can free it themselves, in the same place they already free `resolved`/
`base_dir`, right after their own `asnix_compile(_scoped)` call and
`asnix_ast_arena_reset()` return. The fork()'d prefetch producer
(`asnix_prefetch_compile_and_cache`) got the same one-line fix for
consistency, though it's moot there (that child exits immediately after).

**Verified correct via `valgrind --leak-check=full`, not just RSS**:
RSS deltas for this one fix are noise-sized on `./asnix d.nix` (peak RSS
varied by up to ~1 MB run-to-run on this same closure; M114's own much
larger env-count fix only moved peak RSS by ~0.7% for comparison) --
freed heap chunks get reused by the glibc arena for later allocations in
the same process rather than shrinking the process's high-water mark, so
a single-run RSS comparison can't distinguish "freed but reused" from
"never freed". `valgrind --leak-check=full --show-leak-kinds=definite`
on the same `./asnix d.nix` run gives a direct, allocator-reuse-proof
signal instead: before this fix, `read_file`'s `malloc` (`eval_file.c`'s
`read_file`, called from `asnix_eval_file`) appears as a "definitely
lost" loss record for essentially every one of the ~1,057 imported
files; after, exactly 2 small records remain (291 + 1,143 bytes). Those
2 are not a bug in this fix: `builtins.tryEval`'s `longjmp`
(`tryeval.c`/`builtins_tryeval.c`) unwinds past any C stack frame
between its `setjmp` and the thrown error, skipping that frame's own
cleanup code entirely -- the exact same documented, already-accepted
limitation `builtins_tryeval.c`'s own comment describes for `op_*.S`/
`force.S` epilogues, now also covering this new `free(src)` call for the
rare case where a `tryEval`-wrapped import's compile is the frame being
unwound through.

`make test`/`make test-e2e`: all green (24/24 test binaries). `make
test-nix-conformance`: `pass=655 fail=3 skip=148`, identical to the
pre-existing baseline (same 3 pos-tracking failures). `make
test-nixpkgs-hash`: **`pass=148 fail=0`**, unchanged. `./asnix d.nix`
output unchanged: `/nix/store/29iacg6h530yx7rxz4k1fhvi0kxxhsam-ffmpeg-9.0.1-bin`.

## M116: generalizing the `builtins.elem a b` call-fusion peephole to the 4 next-highest-volume curried natives (`any`/`all`/`match`/`intersectAttrs`) -- and the real reason it barely moves the needle

A prior session proved a narrower, compile-time-only alternative to the
full `PrimOpApp`-style runtime redesign (explicitly ruled too large for
one pass): a peephole, `try_fused_native_call2` (`compiler.c`), that
recognizes the statically-verifiable shape `builtins.elem a b` (a
literal, fully-saturated, unshadowed 2-arg call directly off `builtins`)
and compiles one direct native call, skipping the curried native's own
2 Closure/Env hops entirely. That prior pass scoped itself to `elem`
alone and measured it firing only 10 times on `d.nix`'s real ffmpeg
closure -- explicitly left extending to the other ~31 curried natives as
a "documented, mechanically-clear follow-on," flagging the one real risk
as each native's own forcing variant (noforce vs. force-by-default).

**Measuring which natives actually matter first.** Rather than guess,
this pass set a `gdb` breakpoint on each of the ~32 curried-native
`*_impl` functions (`commands`/`silent`/`continue` on every hit) and ran
the real `d.nix` workload once. Five natives dominate by a wide margin
(next-highest, `compareVersions`, trails by 3x): `all` 18,151 hits,
`any` 12,015, `match` 9,835, `elem` 7,825, `intersectAttrs` 7,763 --
~86,000 combined, the large majority of all curried-native calls on this
workload.

**Generalizing the peephole.** `try_fused_native_call2` became
table-driven (`FUSED_NATIVES_2[]`: name, native fn pointer, noforce
flag), matching any of these 5 names off `builtins.<name>`. Reading
op_call.S's own primop dispatch (`.Lop_call_is_primop`) clarified that
the "noforce audit" the prior pass flagged as the main risk is actually
*asymmetric* in difficulty, the opposite of what it looks like at first
glance:
- `elem` (NOFORCE) needs its own native impl to force exactly what the
  ordinary curry chain would have forced by the time it got there (here,
  only `list`, deliberately leaving `x` unforced for `eqValues`-style
  slot-identity -- M92) -- a real, native-impl-specific fact that has to
  be re-verified per native before reusing this path.
- `any`/`all`/`match`/`intersectAttrs` (ordinary force-by-default) need
  **no native-impl-specific handling at all**: op_call.S's own
  post-dispatch force loop (M25/M30) already forces every argument
  before calling ANY non-NOFORCE primop, fused or not -- minting an
  ordinary (non-noforce) `PrimOp` via `asnix_bshared_make_primop` and
  compiling the arguments exactly like any other ordinary call argument
  (same `try_cell_ref`/`is_thunk_free_literal`/thunk fallback) reproduces
  the curry chain's own forcing behavior automatically, for free. These
  four were mechanically *simpler* to add correctly than `elem`'s own
  case, not harder -- the one real risk surface is the AST-shape
  recognition and shadow checks (unchanged, reused verbatim from the
  `elem`-only pass), not the forcing semantics.

`asnix_prim_{elem,any,all}2_impl` (`builtins_list2.c`),
`asnix_prim_match2_impl` (`builtins_regex.c`), and
`asnix_prim_intersectAttrs2_impl` (`builtins_m23.c`) were un-`static`'d
and exported (each file's own header) so `compiler.c` can reference them
directly, same mechanism the `elem`-only pass established.

**Verified**: both shadow-check cases re-confirmed for all 4 new natives
(`let builtins = { any = ...; }; in builtins.any ...` etc. -- each
returns the user's own shadowed value, fusion correctly declines);
basic correctness (`any (x: x>2) [1 2 3]`, `all (x: x>0) [1 2 3]`,
`match "(f)(o+)" "foo"`, `intersectAttrs {a=1;b=2;} {b=20;c=30;}`) and
laziness short-circuiting (`any`/`all` stop at the first
deciding element, never evaluating a later `throw`) all match real Nix.
`make test`/`make test-e2e`/`make test-conformance`: all green. `make
test-nix-conformance`: `pass=655 fail=3 skip=148`, exact match to
baseline (same 3 pre-existing pos-tracking failures). `make
test-nixpkgs-hash`: `pass=148 fail=0`. All of this re-verified a SECOND
time in a completely isolated `git archive`'d clone with only this
change's own patch applied (necessary -- see below), not just in the
shared worktree.

**Measured, and the real surprise.** Comparing against a *stale*
baseline (captured earlier in this same session, before an unrelated
concurrent M110 landed on this shared branch and changed the env count
on its own) first appeared to show a dramatic ~192K-env reduction --
actually almost entirely M114's own effect bleeding into the comparison,
a measurement mistake caught by re-running both sides as a true paired
comparison in a fresh `git archive`'d clone of the *current* HEAD, with
only this change's patch applied on one side. The honest, isolated,
paired numbers on `d.nix` (real nixpkgs's `ffmpeg.outPath`):
- envs: 1,485,165 -> 1,482,777 (**-2,388, -0.16%**)
- closures: 362,661 -> 361,467 (**-1,194, -0.33%**)
- primops: 61,308 -> 61,332 (+24 -- one fresh `PrimOp` per distinct
  *static* fused call site found across the whole evaluated closure, not
  per dynamic call; confirms only 24 source locations in this entire
  build matched the fused shape)
- peak RSS: 624,016 -> 623,348 KB (-668 KB, -0.11%)
- instructions (`perf stat -r 5`, pinned to one P-core to avoid this
  machine's hybrid-core PMU split): 10,640,582,084 -> 10,644,376,814,
  essentially flat (a tiny +0.036%, inside this measurement's noise
  floor, not a regression signal)

Real, but two orders of magnitude smaller than the ~86,000 raw call-hit
count suggested. **Why**: real nixpkgs's `lib` does not call
`builtins.<name>` directly at the use site for any of these 5 -- it
re-exports each one through an alias binding first (`lib/lists.nix`:
`any = builtins.any;`, `all = builtins.all;`; `lib/customisation.nix`:
`inherit (builtins) intersectAttrs;`, used inside `callPackageWith` as
the bare local name `intersectAttrs fargs autoArgs`, confirmed directly
against the real nixpkgs checkout this project tests against). Every
one of those call sites is a bare-variable application, not
`builtins.<name> a b` -- a shape this peephole, by design, cannot and
should not recognize (seeing through an alias to "this variable's value
happens to be exactly `builtins.foo`" is a value-flow fact, not an
AST-shape fact, and forcing it would need either real alias-tracking or
the very `PrimOpApp` runtime redesign this whole approach exists to
avoid). The 24 static matches that DO fire are the rare cases where
nixpkgs source writes `builtins.<name>` out directly in place (e.g.
`lib/trivial.nix`'s `match = builtins.match "..." str;`) rather than
through `lib`'s own re-export layer -- real, but a small minority of
this workload's actual call volume for these 5 natives.

**Scope note for any future continuation**: this is the ceiling for a
purely syntactic, compile-time-local peephole on real nixpkgs as
written today -- not a bug in the implementation, a structural fact
about how nixpkgs's `lib` exposes `builtins` (alias-first). Pushing
this approach further (e.g. recognizing `let x = builtins.foo;` /
`inherit (builtins) foo;` as a compile-time alias and fusing uses of `x`
the same way) is a qualitatively different, larger change -- it
requires tracking VALUE-level origin through a binding, not just
AST shape at the call site -- deliberately not attempted here, flagged
instead of forced, matching this change's own honest-scoping mandate.

## M117: `LazyApp` -- a lightweight `Value::mkApp`-style value kind for `map`/`mapAttrs`/`zipAttrsWith`, replacing a genuine Env+Thunk (or Env+Thunk-via-shared-Env) pair per output element

Real Nix builds each `map`/`mapAttrs` output element via `Value::mkApp`
(value.hh) -- a lightweight application thunk needing no Env allocation
until actually forced, and never counted as a genuine Thunk at all.
asnix's own `asnix_bshared_make_lazy_call1`/`_call2`
(builtins_shared.c) instead allocated a genuine Env AND a genuine Thunk
for EVERY output element, unconditionally, whether or not it was ever
forced -- the single largest simultaneous contributor to both the
env-count and thunk-count gap against real Nix on a real nixpkgs
closure. M109 had already carved out a narrower, mapAttrs/zipAttrsWith-
specific win here (one shared 1-slot Env holding `f`, so each
per-attribute thunk only needs a 2-slot Env instead of 3), and M113
further fused that 2-slot Env and its Thunk into a single
`asnix_arena_alloc` call -- real instruction-count wins, but neither
changed the actual OBJECT count: every output element was still one
genuine Env plus one genuine Thunk, just packed more cheaply.

`LazyApp` replaces that Env+Thunk pair (shared-env or not) with ONE
heap object `{marker; fn; arg1; arg2}` (32 bytes), riding on the
existing `ASNIX_TAG_PTR` reserved-marker scheme -- the same precedent
M92's `Cell` established -- with two marker values (`ASNIX_LAZYAPP_MARKER`
unresolved, `ASNIX_LAZYAPP_FORCED_MARKER` resolved) used as a tiny
two-state machine. `arg2.raw == 0` means "no second argument" (`map`'s
plain `fn arg1` case); any other value means the curried `(fn arg1)
arg2` case `mapAttrs`/`zipAttrsWith` need for `f name value`.
`asnix_make_lazyapp1`/`asnix_make_lazyapp2` (value_util.c) build one,
replacing `map`'s/`mapAttrs`'s/`zipAttrsWith`'s calls one-for-one
(builtins_list.c/builtins_attrs.c/builtins_m54.c) -- `asnix_bshared_
make_lazy_call1`/`_call2`/`_make_call2_shared_env`/
`_make_lazy_call2_indexed` and their shared `make_thunk_from` helper are
all now dead code, removed from builtins_shared.c/.h.

Resolved on demand via the identical 5 force chokepoints M92 already
enumerated for Cell (force.S's `asnix_force_for_print`, op_var_ref.S,
op_select.S, op_select_or.S, op_with.S's `OP_WITH_TRY`), calling the new
shared `asnix_resolve_lazyapp` and looping back to re-dispatch, exactly
mirroring `asnix_resolve_cell_chain`'s role. Memoized by mutating the
object in place on first success: `marker` flips to
`ASNIX_LAZYAPP_FORCED_MARKER` and the computed result overwrites the
`fn` slot (reused, since `fn`/`arg1`/`arg2` are all dead once resolved)
-- every later force of ANY copy of the tagged pointer just reads the
cache back, confirmed directly via a `map` callback wrapping
`builtins.trace`, forced twice through two independent `elemAt` reads
of the same output element, tracing exactly once.

Deliberately NOT given Thunk's full IN_PROGRESS/FAILED state machine
(would mean teaching the shared `asnix_inprogress_head` intrusive-stack
unwind walker, `asnix_tryeval_unwind_inprogress` in tryeval.c, to
recognize and write a different tag for a second node shape on the same
list -- real, fiddly, shared-mechanism risk, M82's own history warns
about exactly this class of bug). Two accepted, documented
consequences: (1) no bespoke blackhole detection for a constructed
self-referential LazyApp cycle -- it still aborts via the same
RETSTACK-overflow guard that already catches ordinary unbounded
Nix-level recursion, just with a different message than Thunk's
"blackhole" wording; (2) no memoized-failure replay -- a LazyApp whose
resolution throws and is caught by an enclosing `tryEval` re-runs `fn`
from scratch on a later force rather than re-raising the memoized
failure a Thunk would. Confirmed no fixture in numtide/nix-conformance's
gating suite combines `tryEval` with `map`/`mapAttrs`/`zipAttrsWith`.

Printer (`main.c`'s `print_peel_wrappers`) and
`asnix_bshared_slot_identical` (builtins_shared.c) both gained an
identical sibling case to their existing Cell/Thunk handling.

### Verification

Laziness canaries: `builtins.length (map (x: throw "boom") [1 2 3])` =>
`3`; `builtins.attrNames (builtins.mapAttrs (n: v: throw "boom") { a =
1; b = 2; })` => `[ "a" "b" ]`; `builtins.attrNames (builtins.
zipAttrsWith (n: v: throw "boom") [{a=1;} {a=2;}])` => `[ "a" ]` --
none throw. `make test`/`make test-e2e`: fully green. `make
test-nix-conformance`: `pass=655 fail=3 skip=148`, exact match to the
pre-change baseline (same 3 pre-existing pos-tracking failures). `make
test-nixpkgs-hash`: `pass=148 fail=0`.

**Measured on `d.nix` (real nixpkgs's `ffmpeg.outPath`), paired against
current master (post-M113) as the real baseline** -- not against the
pre-M109/M113 numbers an earlier draft of this change was measured
against, which are no longer comparable since M109/M113 already shrank
the starting gap:
- envs: 1,492,607 -> 978,030 (**-514,577, -34.5%**)
- thunks: 2,342,967 -> 1,834,828 (**-508,139, -21.7%**)
- lazyapps: 0 -> 502,964 (new -- one per `map`/`mapAttrs`/
  `zipAttrsWith` output element across the whole evaluated closure)
- peak RSS: 588,440 -> 584,592 KB (**-3,848 KB, -0.65%** -- much more
  modest than LazyApp's own object-size win alone would suggest,
  because M113 had already eliminated most of the malloc-call overhead
  this change also removes; the real remaining win here is the env/
  thunk COUNT reduction, not bytes)
- output hash unchanged (`/nix/store/29iacg6h530yx7rxz4k1fhvi0kxxhsam-ffmpeg-9.0.1-bin`)

## M118 scope notes: pointer compression (V8/LuaJIT-style compressed cage refs) for `Value`'s tag bits and for `Env`/`Thunk`/`Closure`/`Cell`'s internal pointers -- investigated, declined for `Thunk`/`Closure`/`Cell`, landed for `Env` (see M119)

**Net result: no code change.** Two independent wins were in scope: (1)
freeing spare bits in `Value.raw`'s own tag word by shrinking a tagged
pointer's payload from 64 to 32 bits, potentially reopening a
previously-blocked shared-descriptor/packed-index scheme for
`mapAttrs`/`zipAttrsWith` (out of scope to actually build here, just
asked to confirm/deny reachability); and (2) directly shrinking the raw,
untagged *internal* pointer fields (`Env.up`, `Thunk`'s env field,
`Closure.up`/`.prog`, `Cell.target`) from 8 to 4 bytes, independent of
`Value`'s tag scheme entirely. Ground truth was re-derived directly from
`include/asnix/{value,env,ir,heap,arena}.h`, `src/asm/{arena,env}.S`, and
a grep of every real call site -- not assumed from the task brief's own
(correctly-flagged-as-secondhand) summary.

**Win #1's bit budget, confirmed exactly**: `ASNIX_TAG_MASK` is 3 bits
and all 8 values are already assigned (`value.h`: PTR/INT/IMM/ATTRS/
LIST/CLOSURE/THUNK/PRIMOP). A pointer-tagged word today uses the
remaining 61 bits as a raw 64-bit pointer verbatim. Shrinking that
payload to a 32-bit cage offset would use 3+32=35 of the 64 bits,
leaving exactly **29 spare bits** above the tag -- confirmed arithmetic,
not an estimate.

**Reservation mechanism, tested empirically on this host** (Linux 6.8,
x86_64) before building anything on top of it: `MAP_32BIT` was tried
first since it's the simplest option, but turned out to be far weaker
than its name suggests. A standalone test program
(`mmap(NULL, n, ..., MAP_32BIT|MAP_NORESERVE, -1, 0)`) showed requests
above 1 GiB reliably fail `ENOMEM` -- 1024 MiB succeeded (placed at
exactly `0x40000000`-`0x80000000`), 1536 MiB and 1920 MiB both failed.
This matches Linux's actual implementation: despite the "first 2GB"
description, the search window is hardcoded to start at `0x40000000`
(1 GiB) and end at `0x80000000` (2 GiB), so the real usable budget is
**~1 GiB, not ~2 GiB** -- too tight to be a serious option on its own.
A manual low fixed-address reservation (`mmap(hint, n, ...,
MAP_FIXED_NOREPLACE, ...)` at an arbitrary hint like `0x10000000`)
worked cleanly up to 4 GiB with no retry logic needed. But this
distinction turned out to be moot (see below): the right reconstruction
scheme is additive (`full = base + zext32(offset)`), which places no
constraint on the base address at all (unlike V8's OR-based scheme,
which needs a 4 GiB-aligned base) -- so neither `MAP_32BIT` nor a
low-address hint is actually required; an ordinary anywhere-`mmap`
works identically well as the reservation, once you have one.

**The real blocker, found by tracing where every candidate pointer
field's target actually lives**: `asnix_arena_alloc` (arena.S) is the
*single, shared* bump allocator behind every heap-allocated kind in
this codebase -- String, Path, Float, Cell, List, Attrs, PrimOp, Env,
Thunk, and Closure all go through it (confirmed by grep: dozens of call
sites across `src/c/*.c` and every env-frame-allocating asm file). It
grows via repeated, address-unconstrained `mmap(NULL, chunk_size, ...)`
calls with **no contiguity guarantee between chunks** (`arena.S`'s
`.Lgrow` path). Pointer compression -- for EITHER win #1 (Value's own
tagged pointers) or win #2 (internal fields) -- requires every object a
compressed pointer can ever address to live inside one bounded,
contiguous, upfront-reserved region. That is not a per-field tweak; it
is a prerequisite rearchitecture of the arena itself, touching every
heap kind in the runtime, not just the four candidate structs.

**Granting that prerequisite hypothetically** (migrating `Env`/`Thunk`/
`Closure`/`Cell` into one dedicated bounded cage) and redoing the
per-struct byte arithmetic against `asnix_arena_alloc`'s real
`round_up_8` rounding (`addq $7; andq $-8` in arena.S) -- this is the
same rounding-defeats-narrowing effect M100's and M106's own writeups
already hit twice on this codebase, re-derived independently here and
landing on the identical conclusion:

- **`Env{up(8); values[n](8n)}` = `8(1+n)`, always already a multiple of
  8.** Shrinking `up` alone to 4 bytes gives `4+8n`, which
  `round_up_8` restores to `8+8n` -- bit-for-bit IDENTICAL to today, for
  every `n`. Zero bytes saved. `Env` has only one raw pointer field, so
  there is no second field to pair it with to recover the rounding
  loss -- unlike the task brief's framing, `Env.up` is NOT the
  "simplest/highest-confidence" candidate; it is a proven zero.
- **`Thunk{state/prog(8); env(8)}` = 16 (M106, already packed).** `env`
  cannot shrink at all, independent of rounding: M106 already
  established (confirmed again here by inspection of `ir.h`'s own
  comment) that this field caches a full 8-byte `Value.raw` once
  `FORCED`, and `Value.raw` can't narrow -- `TAG_INT`'s 61-bit immediate
  and the `TAG_IMM` subtags need the full word regardless of any
  pointer-compression scheme applied to OTHER tags. Shrinking the other
  field (`state`/`prog`) alone hits the identical rounding wall as `Env`
  (12 bytes rounds back to 16). `Thunk` is a double dead end: blocked by
  rounding AND by field-reuse.
- **`Closure{up(8); prog(8); arity(8); formals(8)}` = 32.** This is the
  one struct where compressing TWO fields together survives rounding:
  `up`+`prog` at 4+4 bytes gives `4+4+8+8=24`, a real 8-byte (25%)
  reduction. But `prog` (an `IrProgram*`) does not live in the arena at
  all -- confirmed directly: `ib_finish` (`irbuild.c:271`) allocates
  every `IrProgram` via plain `calloc`, and
  `asnix_bytecode_deserialize` (`bytecode.c:905`) via plain `malloc`;
  placement is wherever glibc's allocator puts it, with zero proximity
  guarantee to the arena or to anything else. Compressing `prog` would
  require rerouting BOTH of those call sites through a brand-new
  bounded-cage allocator instead of calloc/malloc, including
  preserving `calloc`'s zero-init behavior by hand. (Its one existing
  `free()`, `bytecode.c:900`, is on a corrupt-bytecode-cache error path
  only -- not itself a hard blocker, just confirming `prog`'s current
  allocation lifecycle is genuinely independent of the arena.)
- **`Cell{marker(8); target(8)}` = 16.** `target` alone: `8+4=12` rounds
  back to 16, zero saved -- same pattern again. `marker` can't shrink
  without touching the shared "first word of a `TAG_PTR`-kind object"
  dispatch convention it shares with String's `len` and Path's/Float's
  own markers (`heap.h`) -- a cross-cutting change to three OTHER value
  kinds, explicitly out of this task's scope.

**Quantified payoff if the one non-zero case (`Closure`) were pushed
through anyway**: `ASNIX_SHOW_STATS=1 ./asnix d.nix` (ffmpeg's real
closure; re-measured against this repo's actual merged tip, post-M117
`LazyApp`, not the earlier pre-rebase number this paragraph originally
cited -- see M119's own note on why that distinction matters) reports
360,937 closures allocated. `8 bytes * 360,937 = 2,887,496 bytes (~2.75
MiB)` against a measured peak RSS of **~584,239 KB (~570.5 MiB)**
(3-run average: 584,308 / 584,468 / 583,940 KB) -- **~0.48% of peak
RSS**, essentially unchanged from the original estimate. That is not worth taking on an arena rearchitecture plus a
separate `IrProgram`-allocator rewrite for, especially given the new
hard constraint it would introduce: `asnix_arena.max_memory` defaults to
0 (unlimited) today, but any cage sized to fit a 32-bit offset is
capped at <=4 GiB, hard, with no larger-than-single-package real
workload fixture in this repo (`bench/`'s `d.nix`/`e.nix` are both
single-package nixpkgs closures) to check that a full system-level
closure would stay under it.

**Win #1, confirmed NOT reopened by any of the above**: the 29 spare
bits are only unlockable by compressing `Value`'s own tagged *payload*
pointers (`ATTRS`/`LIST`/`CLOSURE`/`THUNK`/`PRIMOP`/`PTR`), which is an
entirely different, much larger change than anything investigated here
-- it touches `value.S`'s tagging macros and every op that constructs
or dereferences a tagged pointer, i.e. effectively the whole evaluator,
not just four internal struct fields. Since no internal-field
compression was implemented (all four candidates are either a proven
zero or require a disproportionate prerequisite), this work makes zero
progress toward win #1 and does not reopen the blocked shared-
descriptor/packed-index `mapAttrs` idea.

**Decision**: stop at the research phase, as explicitly sanctioned by
this task's own gate ("if the prototype reveals the approach is unsound
or not worthwhile... STOP HERE, do not force it further"). No `Env`/
`Thunk`/`Closure`/`Cell` field was converted and no arena code was
touched -- doing so would have been pure risk (the hottest, most
heavily-shared allocator and the five force-dispatch chokepoints
`force.S`/`op_var_ref.S`/`op_select.S`/`op_select_or.S`/`op_with.S`,
all re-confirmed as the right chokepoint list via grep) for a payoff
already shown, by direct calculation against this struct's own
definition and the arena's own rounding behavior, to be at most
~0.48% of peak RSS even in the one non-zero case for `Closure` --
and `Thunk`/`Cell` are zero regardless. `Env`, however, turned out to
be a genuine miss in this first pass: see M119, which found and fixed
the actual blind spot (a dedicated arena is free to pick ITS OWN
rounding granularity, decoupled from the general arena's `round_up_8`)
and landed a real `Env.up` compression on top of this research.

## M119: a dedicated, bounded Env arena -- `Env.up` compressed to a 32-bit offset, fixing the blind spot M118's first pass missed

**The correction, in one sentence**: M118's rounding argument against
`Env.up` ("`4+8n` rounds right back to `8+8n`, zero bytes saved")
silently assumed any new dedicated arena would keep reusing the general
arena's `round_up_8` convention. It doesn't have to. `round_up_8` exists
*only* because `Value.raw`'s 3-bit tag scheme needs every TAGGED pointer
(String/Path/Float/Cell/Attrs/List/Closure/Thunk/PrimOp) to be 8-byte
aligned -- `Env` is never itself a tagged `Value`, so a dedicated,
Env-only arena can round to 4 instead, and `4+8n` really is smaller
than `8+8n`, for every `n`, with nothing clawing it back. This was
flagged directly, mid-session, by feedback questioning why the
projected win looked too small for a field that's "literally halved" --
the halved-field framing was right; what was missing was checking
whether the SURROUNDING struct's rounding convention was actually
fixed or just inherited by default.

**Mechanism**: a brand-new `src/asm/env_arena.S`, structurally similar
to `arena.S` but deliberately simpler and separate from it -- ONE
upfront `mmap(ASNIX_ENV_ARENA_SIZE)` reservation (no `.Lgrow`-style
repeated, address-unconstrained growth: a compressed 32-bit offset is
only valid if every object it can address lives inside one bounded,
contiguous region, which the general arena's own growth strategy
cannot guarantee -- see M118), lazily self-initialized on first call
(checked via the bump cursor being exactly 0) so no caller anywhere,
production or test, needs to remember an explicit init step. Bump
cursor starts at `base+8`, not `base+0`, so a stored offset of 0 can
always mean NULL unambiguously. Reconstruction is additive
(`full = base + zext32(offset)`), not V8's OR-based 4-GiB-aligned-cage
scheme -- additive places no alignment requirement on the reservation's
base address at all, which is also why the session's own empirical
finding that Linux's `MAP_32BIT` only really delivers ~1 GiB (not ~2
GiB; M118) turned out to be moot: an ordinary anywhere-`mmap` works
identically well once you're not relying on address magnitude.

`ASNIX_ENV_OFF_UP` stays conceptually offset 0 but narrows to a 4-byte
compressed offset; `ASNIX_ENV_OFF_VALUES` drops from 8 to 4 -- every
real access site in this codebase reads that offset through the macro
(none hardcode a bare `8`), so the slot-access offset update was
automatic everywhere except the handful of allocation-size computations
that spelled "8" as a literal (`leaq 8(, %rsi, 8), %rdi`), which were
switched to reference `ASNIX_ENV_OFF_VALUES` explicitly. `Env`'s C
struct is now `__attribute__((packed))` with `uint32_t up` (was
`struct Env *up`) so `values[]` genuinely sits at byte offset 4 -- an
un-packed struct would have silently re-inserted the 4 bytes of padding
this whole change exists to remove, to keep `Value` 8-aligned.

**Compress/decompress at every touch site** (re-derived via grep, not
assumed): allocation sites compress the new frame's `up` before storing
it (`env.S`'s `asnix_env_alloc`, `op_frame.S`, `op_let.S`, `op_with.S`,
and the Closure-call frame setup in `op_call.S`/`apply.S`, which copies
a Closure's own -- still full-width, uncompressed -- `up` pointer into
a freshly compressed child frame); depth-walk/exit sites decompress
(`env.S`'s `asnix_env_lookup`, `op_var_ref.S`/`op_var_ref_cell.S`/
`op_var_ref_raw.S`'s depth walks, `op_frame.S`'s `OP_FRAME_EXIT`,
`op_with.S`'s `OP_WITH_EXIT`) -- these are exactly the sites M118
identified as the real blast radius, confirmed unchanged by re-deriving
them a second time independently here. `ASNIX_ENV_WITH_TAG` (the
with-frame marker bit) survives compression intact: both the arena base
(page-aligned, from `mmap`) and every real Env address within it
(`round_up_4`) stay at least 4-byte aligned, so subtracting one from a
tagged (odd) address stays odd, exactly the same way it did on the full
64-bit pointer -- four sites that previously over-masked with `andq
$-8` (relying on 8-byte alignment that no longer holds) were narrowed
to `andq $-2` (bit 0 only), matching a fifth site (`op_with.S`'s
`OP_WITH_EXIT`) that already did this correctly before this change.
NULL-safety: `up` is unconditionally live/non-NULL at the three
hot-path-inlined allocation sites (`op_frame.S`/`op_let.S`/`op_with.S`
only ever compress the CURRENT, already-live ENV), but genuinely can be
NULL at three other sites -- `env.S`'s general-purpose `asnix_env_alloc`
entry point (called with `up=NULL` for every root Env) and the two
Closure-call frame-setup sites (a native-wrapper Closure can have
`up=NULL`, no captured env) -- each guarded with an explicit
`testq`/branch so NULL compresses to 0, not a garbage subtraction.

**Fallback/cap design, per this session's explicit direction**: a
single flat, generously-sized hard cap (`ASNIX_ENV_ARENA_SIZE` = 1
GiB) with a clean `asnix_fatal` abort on exhaustion -- the SAME
philosophy the general arena's own `ASNIX_MAX_MEMORY` already uses, not
the alternative (a dual-path fallback to plain 64-bit pointers from the
general arena once the dedicated arena fills, with a marker bit
distinguishing which kind of pointer a given `up` field holds) this
session's own earlier message offered as an option. The flat cap was
chosen specifically because the marker-fallback's cost lands exactly
where it hurts most: an extra branch on EVERY depth-walk hop, the
hottest of the sites this change touches, for a case (filling a
1-GiB-not-yet-stressed-by-any-real-workload arena) this session has no
evidence is a real risk. 1 GiB is ~36x the ~28 MB (978,030 envs, M117's
own post-`LazyApp` count) this session's one real benchmark actually
uses -- comfortably short of the hard 4 GiB ceiling a 32-bit offset
imposes regardless of chosen cap, confirmed to abort cleanly (not
corrupt memory) via a standalone throwaway test that forced the arena
to fill: `asnix: Env arena exhausted (ASNIX_ENV_ARENA_SIZE), aborting`,
exit code 1.

**M113's fusion note, overtaken by events**: the plan going into this
milestone was to unwind M113's fused single-allocation Env+Thunk
helper in `builtins_shared.c` (`asnix_bshared_make_lazy_call2_indexed`),
since `Env` and `Thunk` can no longer share one allocation once they
live in different arenas. By the time this milestone's code was
written, M117 (`LazyApp`, landed concurrently on `master` by a
different session) had already removed that entire helper and its
siblings outright, replacing the whole Env+Thunk-per-`mapAttrs`-element
mechanism with a lighter-weight value kind that allocates neither --
so there was nothing left to unwind. Discovered via a real merge
conflict (both sessions picked the same next milestone number, M117,
independently) rather than assumed; the rebase onto the real `master`
tip surfaced it directly.

**Measured** (fresh, against this repo's actual immediate parent commit
-- M117/`LazyApp`, not the earlier pre-rebase baseline some of M118's
own numbers were measured against before this merge): on `./asnix
d.nix` (ffmpeg's real closure), output unchanged
(`/nix/store/29iacg6h530yx7rxz4k1fhvi0kxxhsam-ffmpeg-9.0.1-bin`),
allocation COUNTS unchanged (978,030 envs, 1,721,601 elements -- this
is a byte-size change, not an allocation-count change):
- `sizeof` per Env: `8+8n -> 4+8n` bytes, exactly (no rounding
  clawback) -- e.g. a 1-slot Env: 16 -> 12 bytes (25%); average over
  this workload's real slot distribution (1,721,601 elements /
  978,030 envs ~= 1.76 slots/env): ~22.1 -> ~18.1 bytes/env (~18.1%).
- peak RSS: 584,239 -> 580,408 KB (3-run averages; **-3,831 KB,
  -0.66%**) -- matches the byte-counting prediction almost exactly
  (978,030 envs * 4 bytes = 3,820 KB predicted vs. 3,831 KB measured).
- instructions (`perf stat`, `cpu_core` counter, 4 runs each side on
  this shared, concurrently-loaded machine): ~10,671.7M -> ~10,733.4M
  average (**+61.7M, ~+0.58%**) -- within this measurement's own
  run-to-run noise band (before-group spread ~0.84%, after-group
  spread ~2.95%), so this is honestly reported as "roughly flat, maybe
  a small real cost" rather than a clean win either way: the extra
  `movl`+`addq`(+`andq`) per decompression and the `testq`+branch at
  the three NULL-safe compression sites are real added instructions,
  just apparently small enough to sit inside the noise floor on this
  machine. Reported plainly rather than rounded to "no cost" or
  oversold as a speedup.
- `make test`/`test-e2e`/`test-conformance`: all green. `make
  test-nix-conformance`: `pass=655 fail=3 skip=148`, exact match to
  the pre-existing baseline (same 3 documented `getattrpos`/
  `inherit-attr-pos` gaps). `make test-nixpkgs-hash`: `pass=148
  fail=0`.

**New hard constraint introduced**: a permanent 1 GiB cap on live Env
memory specifically (not overall process memory -- the general arena's
own `ASNIX_MAX_MEMORY` is untouched and still defaults to unlimited),
with a clean `asnix_fatal` abort if a program's live Env count ever
reaches it. Acceptable given the ~36x headroom over this session's one
real benchmark, but a genuine new ceiling this codebase did not have
before, and this project has no larger-than-single-package real
workload fixture to stress-test it against.

**Win #1 (freeing `Value`'s own spare tag bits), confirmed NOT
reopened**: this change only touches a field INSIDE an already-
allocated `Env` object -- it never touches `Value.raw`'s own tag
scheme, which is what any real progress on the previously-blocked
shared-descriptor/packed-index `mapAttrs` idea would need (compressing
the `ATTRS`/`LIST`/`CLOSURE`/`THUNK`/`PRIMOP`/`PTR` tags' own payload
pointers, an entirely different and much larger change -- see M118).
`Thunk`/`Cell` remain unconverted for the same reasons M118 found
(field-reuse and cross-cutting-marker blockers respectively, both
independent of the rounding fix this milestone applied); `Closure`
remains unconverted because its `prog` field's target (`IrProgram`,
heap-`malloc`'d/`calloc`'d, never arena-allocated) would need its own,
separate allocator migration first -- noted in M118, unchanged by this
milestone.

**Commit**: `include/asnix/env.h`, `src/asm/env_arena.S` (new),
`src/asm/env.S`, `src/asm/apply.S`,
`src/asm/ops/{op_call,op_frame,op_let,op_var_ref,op_var_ref_cell,
op_var_ref_raw,op_with}.S`, ten hand-rolled-root-Env test fixtures
(`tests/{ir,asm,c}/*.c`) switched to the real `asnix_env_alloc` API
instead of a raw general-arena poke (required for correctness, not
just style -- a hand-rolled Env outside the dedicated arena can't be
correctly compressed if anything ever points `up` at it), plus
`tests/asm/test_env.c`'s one direct `up`-comparison check updated for
the new compressed representation.

## M120: a bytecode-to-bytecode optimization-pass framework, plus one proof-of-concept pass (int constant folding)

Directive: now that this project has a real compiled bytecode format (the
flat, fixed-width `IrOp` stream, ir.h) and a companion decoder (`irdump`,
M99), can a proper optimizing compiler be layered on top of it -- and can
testing/verifying such transformations be made systematic rather than
ad hoc? This milestone builds the framework and one small, honest example
pass to prove it end to end; it does NOT attempt a bytecode->assembly JIT
(scope note at the end).

**Design**: `include/asnix/irpass.h` + `src/c/irpass.c`. A pass is
`int (*)(IrOp *ops, size_t *len)`, registered via `asnix_irpass_register`,
run to a fixpoint by `asnix_irpass_run` -- which `ib_finish()` (irbuild.c)
now calls unconditionally, immediately before its own `ir_link()`. With
ZERO passes registered (every normal build/run, including the shipped
`asnix` binary with no env var set), this is a no-op -- `ib_finish()`'s
behavior is byte-for-byte identical to before this milestone. A pass
becomes live only by explicit registration (a test harness, or
`ASNIX_IR_OPT=1` -- same opt-in-env-var convention as `ASNIX_SHOW_STATS`,
wired into both `main.c` and `irdump.c`). Because `ib_finish()` is the one
chokepoint every `IrBuilder` in this codebase goes through (the top-level
program, every lambda body, every thunk body -- each its own builder
instance), registering a pass covers the WHOLE compiled program tree with
no change needed at any of `compiler.c`'s many call sites.

**The one real design problem this framework had to solve**: the IR is
flat and fixed-width with RELATIVE BYTE-DELTA jumps (`OP_IF`/`OP_JMP`/
`OP_WITH_TRY`/`OP_SELECT_OR`/`OP_SELECT_DYNAMIC_OR` -- exhaustive, per
ir.h's own per-op comments), so removing ops to shrink the stream means
every jump elsewhere in the program -- including ones compiled long before
the removed region and targeting long after it -- must have its delta
recomputed, or it silently lands on the wrong instruction. `asnix_irpass_
remove(ops, len, start, count)` is the one shrink primitive every pass
uses: it verifies no live jump's target falls INSIDE the removed range
(fatal if one does -- a pass may only remove self-contained,
unreferenced sequences), then re-derives every jump's old absolute
position/target via the inverse of the memmove, and rewrites each delta
