A profiling candidate flagged `nar.c:202-213`'s `copy_cache_find`/
`copy_cache_insert` (backing `asnix_copy_path_to_store` and
`asnix_copy_path_to_store_cache_lookup`, called from `value_util.c`'s
Path coercion at lines 453 and 601) as a plain array + for-loop-of-
`strcmp` memoization cache, re-scanning every previously-copied path
from the start on every lookup -- an `O(n)` per-call / unbounded-growth-
within-one-eval anti-pattern. Reading the code directly confirmed the
candidate's own claim: this is the exact same shape of problem this
file's neighbor, `derivation.c`'s `input_ref_add_src`/
`input_ref_add_built` (lines ~549-608), already diagnosed and fixed with
an open-addressing hash index keyed by a local `dcc_hash_str` -- that
code's own comment explicitly calls out "the same shape of anti-pattern
this file's `dcc_hash_str`/`DrvClosureStrSet` fix already addressed",
but `copy_cache_find` in `nar.c` had never received the equivalent
treatment. Distinct from `eval_file.c`'s `import_cache_find`, which M91
explicitly checked and declined to fix (there, a cache MISS costs a full
parse+compile+eval of the missed file, dwarfing any linear-scan
overhead); here a miss only costs a NAR-dump-and-hash of a typically-
small source path, so the "miss is expensive, don't bother" justification
doesn't transfer and the scan's own cost is proportionally more visible.

**The fix**: a local `copy_cache_hash_str` (the identical 8-bytes-at-a-
time multiply-chain hash `derivation.c`'s `dcc_hash_str` uses, kept as
its own separate static copy per this codebase's existing convention
of each file owning its own small hash helper rather than sharing one
across translation units -- `symtab.c`'s own, differently-named
`hash_bytes` is the precedent), plus an open-addressing index
(`g_copy_cache_index`/`COPY_CACHE_EMPTY_SLOT`, 3/4 load factor,
doubling on growth) parallel to the existing `g_copy_cache` array,
mirroring `derivation.c`'s `input_ref_srcs_index_rehash`/
`input_ref_add_src` structure exactly (single-string key, this file's
case is actually simpler than `input_ref_add_built`'s combined two-
field key). `copy_cache_find` probes the index instead of scanning
linearly; `copy_cache_insert` rehashes-then-appends, inserting the new
entry's index into its hashed slot. No change to either function's
public behavior or signature -- `asnix_copy_path_to_store`,
`asnix_copy_path_to_store_cache_lookup`, and callers in `value_util.c`
are untouched.

**Correctness.** `make test` (all C/IR unit suites) green. `make
test-e2e` all OK. `make test-conformance` all OK. `make test-nix-
conformance NIX_CONFORMANCE_DIR=/tmp/nix-conformance`: exact baseline
`pass=655 fail=3 skip=148` (the same 3 pre-existing position-tracking
failures: `eval-okay-getattrpos-functionargs.nix`, `eval-okay-
getattrpos.nix`, `eval-okay-inherit-attr-pos.nix`). `make test-nixpkgs-
hash`: `pass=148 fail=0`. `./asnix d.nix` output byte-identical to the
expected hash both before and after this change:
`/nix/store/29iacg6h530yx7rxz4k1fhvi0kxxhsam-ffmpeg-9.0.1-bin`.

**Measured, interleaved** (12 before/after pairs, `perf stat`,
`taskset -c 0`, `cpu_core/instructions/`+`cpu_core/cycles/`, before and
after binaries built from the exact same tree with/without this
milestone's own diff via `git stash`/`git stash pop`, strictly
alternating before/after/before/after..., output hash checked every
trial):

| | instructions (avg) | stdev |
|---|---|---|
| before | 6,538,635,962 | 2,492,984 |
| after | 6,489,388,411 | 2,125,817 |
| delta | -49,247,551 (-0.753%) | |

Every single AFTER trial (12/12) landed below every single BEFORE
trial's own tight band (BEFORE: 6,535.5M-6,546.0M; AFTER: 6,487.4M-
6,494.7M) -- a clean, non-overlapping, repetition-independent win, with
a delta (~49.2M instructions, -0.75%) more than 20 standard deviations
wide relative to either side's own run-to-run noise, and slightly larger
than the candidate's own ~40M/0.6% hypothesis (plausibly because the
real nixpkgs/ffmpeg closure referenced noticeably more than the handful
of distinct local-path references the hypothesis's own instrumentation
run may have undercounted, or because removing the quadratic-shaped
scan cost also removes some second-order cache-miss/branch overhead the
raw strcmp-comparison count alone doesn't capture).

**Shipped** because it is a strict, behavior-preserving simplification
(same cache semantics, same two public entry points, zero new externally
visible state) directly modeled on this project's own existing, already-
proven fix for the identical anti-pattern one file over, with a clean
and comfortably-above-noise measured win.

**Independent verification.** A separate adversarial-verify pass fetched
this commit into its own isolated worktree, confirmed the diff matches

until match or empty slot; rehash preserves every entry by its path
hash), re-ran the full correctness ladder fresh, and ran its own 20-trial

after avg 6,482,325,287 (stdev 782,007), delta **-0.765%** (~50.0M
instructions), 20/20 wins, fully non-overlapping (max(after) <
min(before), >60 stdev separation) -- within ~1.6% relative of the
-0.753% reported above, well inside tolerance. Verdict: CONFIRMED.

## M161: `asnix_bshared_make_attrs` unconditionally `malloc`+`qsort`ed even for the ~93% of calls that are tiny -- given M142's own small-N stack-insertion-sort hybrid

`builtins_shared.c`'s `asnix_bshared_make_attrs` is the shared dynamic-
attrset constructor behind `listToAttrs`/`mapAttrs`/`zipAttrsWith`/
`intersectAttrs`/`fromJSON`/`fromTOML`/`__overrides`-merge and the rest of
its ~18 call sites. Since M89 it has, unconditionally, for every call
regardless of `count`: `malloc`'d a `(sym, original-index)` pairs array,
`qsort`'d it through an indirect comparator (`cmp_make_attrs_entry`),
copied the result into the real attrs object, then `free`'d the scratch
array. A fresh instrumentation pass on `d.nix` (reverted after measuring,
per this project's standing convention) found 52,442 calls averaging 8.1
entries each, with 93% of them (48,780) at `count <= 32`. This is the
exact same "qsort's malloc + per-comparison indirect call costs more than
insertion sort's O(n^2) saves, for the overwhelming majority of small
inputs" shape M142 already found and fixed for the *compile-time*
`AST_ATTRSET` sort in `compiler.c` -- `asnix_bshared_make_attrs` is a
sibling *runtime* sort that was switched straight to unconditional `qsort`
back in M89, before M142's small-N insight existed, and never got the same
treatment.

**The fix**, following M142's own hybrid shape: for `count <=
ASNIX_MAKE_ATTRS_SORT_INSERTION_MAX` (32, the same threshold M142 uses,
redefined locally in this file rather than shared via a header since the
two sorts operate on unrelated data), sort a plain `int64_t
order_stack[32]` index array in place with ordinary insertion sort,
directly on the stack -- no `malloc`, no `MakeAttrsEntry` struct, no
indirect comparator call. Above the threshold, the existing `malloc` +
`MakeAttrsEntry` + `qsort` + `free` path is untouched. Insertion sort is
stable by construction (the `>` comparison in the inner loop never swaps
equal syms), so it reproduces `cmp_make_attrs_entry`'s explicit
`(sym, idx)` tie-break exactly, without needing to track `idx` as a
separate field at all in the small-N path -- a slightly leaner version of
M142's own hybrid (which still built a `{sym,idx}` pairs array for its
large-N qsort branch; this one's small-N branch needs no pairs array
whatsoever, just the index array).

**Correctness.** `make test`, `make test-e2e` (all OK), `make test-
conformance` (all OK), `make test-nix-conformance
NIX_CONFORMANCE_DIR=/tmp/nix-conformance` (`pass=655 fail=3 skip=148`,
the same 3 pre-existing position-tracking failures), and `make test-
nixpkgs-hash` (`pass=148 fail=0`) all green. `./asnix d.nix` output
unchanged: `/nix/store/29iacg6h530yx7rxz4k1fhvi0kxxhsam-ffmpeg-9.0.1-bin`.
A hand-written differential test against real `nix-instantiate --eval`
(not part of the permanent suite) exercised `listToAttrs`/`mapAttrs`/
`zipAttrsWith`/`intersectAttrs` at counts `0, 1, 2, 7, 31, 32, 33, 40, 64,
100` -- straddling the new threshold on both sides -- plus a
duplicate-name `listToAttrs` case (`[{name="a";value=1;} {name="b";
value=2;} {name="a";value=3;}]`, real Nix keeps the FIRST occurrence:
`{a=1; b=2;}`) to confirm the stable-sort tie-break still matches.
`nix-instantiate --eval --strict` and `./asnix` on the same file produced
byte-identical output in every case.

**Measured, interleaved, with a resolved magnitude discrepancy.** The
implementer's own 10-trial run (`perf stat -e cpu_core/instructions/,
cpu_core/cycles/`, `taskset -c 0`, before/after/before/after...) found:

| | mean | median | min |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | 6,547,773,752.8 | 6,541,445,173 | 6,539,697,414 |
| after | 6,515,092,092.8 | 6,507,969,369 | 6,506,892,886 |

A -0.50% / ~33M instruction reduction by mean/median/min alike. An
independent adversarial-verify pass, fetching this commit into its own
isolated worktree and re-running the full ladder fresh plus its own
20-trial interleaved measurement, confirmed correctness is fully intact
and the effect reproduces cleanly in all 20 trials (19 of 20 clustered
tightly between -0.62% and -0.72%, one early outlier at -0.235% likely a
cold-cache warm-up effect) -- but found a somewhat LARGER magnitude than
claimed: mean -0.632% (-41.3M instructions), median -0.647%, min-to-min
-0.691%, all consistently 25-30% bigger than the implementer's own
-0.50%. Per this campaign's established practice (M157's own precedent
for resolving a magnitude discrepancy by trusting the more rigorous
independent re-measurement), **the number to trust going forward is
-0.63% (~41M instructions), not -0.50%** -- a favorable correction, not
an overstatement: the fix is real and somewhat better than first
reported, not a case of a self-measurement failing to reproduce.

This still lands smaller than the handoff's own estimate (1.2% / 80M
instructions) -- the flat-profile `msort_with_tmp` self-time figure that
estimate was built from was explicitly called out as a floor, excluding
`qsort_r`'s own dispatch, the comparator's indirect-call overhead, and
the malloc/free pair, but evidently those excluded costs were smaller in
practice than the floor itself suggested, or GCC's `-O2` inlining made
the small-N insertion sort's own ~8-entry average case cheaper than the
fixed 32-slot stack array's zeroing/loop overhead would suggest. Shipped
anyway: the measured effect is real, in the right direction on every
trial batch, strictly simpler than what it replaces for the common case
(same stable-sort semantics, zero new allocation), and a direct
structural match for the already-proven M142 pattern -- not a
speculative rewrite needing a bigger win to justify its own risk.

Files: `src/c/builtins_shared.c` (`asnix_bshared_make_attrs` given a
small-N stack-insertion-sort fast path below the new
`ASNIX_MAKE_ATTRS_SORT_INSERTION_MAX` threshold; the existing `malloc` +
`qsort` path unchanged above it).

## M162: hand-inlining the Cell-chain dereference (`asnix_resolve_cell_chain`/`asnix_value_is_cell`/`asnix_cell_target`) into `op_var_ref.S` and `force.S`

`value_util.c`'s `asnix_resolve_cell_chain` is the shared "unwrap however
many `Cell`s are chained together" loop for a bare-variable alias (`let y
= x; in y`) -- called from `op_var_ref.S` (the hottest variable-lookup
op) and `force.S`'s `asnix_force_for_print`. It's built from three tiny
C helpers (`asnix_value_is_cell`, `asnix_cell_target`, plus
`asnix_tag_of`) that GCC never inlined into each other or into their one
caller, despite all being one-liners in the same TU: disassembly showed
`asnix_resolve_cell_chain`'s loop body as `call asnix_cell_target` then,
on the next iteration's test, `call asnix_value_is_cell` (which itself
`call`ed `asnix_tag_of`) -- up to three nested out-of-line calls, each
paying a full prologue/epilogue, just to answer "is this a tagged
pointer whose pointee's first qword equals the Cell marker". 834,237
Cell objects are created on `d.nix`, each read at least once.

**The fix.** Hand-rolled the identical loop directly at both call sites
-- mask the tag bits, compare against `ASNIX_TAG_PTR`, mask+load the
base pointer (clearing both the low 3 tag bits and, for M118
compatibility, the high 16 ThunkMap-index bits), compare the leading
qword against `ASNIX_CELL_MARKER`, and either loop (on a chained alias)
or fall through to the existing resolve loop (on a non-Cell result,
which may itself still be an unforced Thunk/LazyApp/ThunkMap -- handled
exactly as before). The chase-limit constant (`ASNIX_CELL_CHASE_LIMIT`,
guarding against a genuine `let x = y; y = x; in x` alias cycle with no
Thunk anywhere in it to catch it via the ordinary blackhole check) moved
from `value_util.c` into `include/asnix/heap.h` so all three copies of
the bound (the original C reference implementation, still used by
`op_select.S`/`op_select_or.S`/`op_with.S`, which weren't hot enough on
`d.nix` to be worth inlining too, plus the two new hand-inlined copies)
stay in lock-step rather than risking silent drift.

Register use was checked carefully for the flags-clobbering hazard this
campaign has twice found before (M111/M155): in both `op_var_ref.S`'s
`.Lvar_ref_cell_loop` and `force.S`'s `.Lforce_cell_loop`, every `cmp`
is followed immediately by its own conditional jump with no
flag-touching instruction in between, and all scratch registers used
(`%r8`-`%r10` in `op_var_ref.S`, `%rax`/`%rcx`/`%rdx`/`%r8`/`%r9` in
`force.S`) are confirmed dead/free at that point in each function (the
callee-saved registers `%r12`-`%r15`/`%rbx`/`%rbp` aren't pushed/
repurposed until further down, past a confirmed Thunk, in both
functions).

**Correctness.** `make test`, `make test-e2e`, `make test-conformance`
all green. `make test-nix-conformance NIX_CONFORMANCE_DIR=/tmp/
nix-conformance` reports `pass=655 fail=3 skip=148`, the same 3
pre-existing position-tracking gaps (`eval-okay-getattrpos-
functionargs.nix`, `eval-okay-getattrpos.nix`, `eval-okay-inherit-attr-
pos.nix`), including `eval-fail-blackhole.nix` passing (the legacy-`let`
mutual-alias-cycle case, exercised through `op_var_ref.S`'s new inline
loop). `make test-nixpkgs-hash` reports `pass=148 fail=0`. `./asnix
d.nix` output byte-identical:
`/nix/store/29iacg6h530yx7rxz4k1fhvi0kxxhsam-ffmpeg-9.0.1-bin`. Hand-
written differential tests against real `nix-instantiate --eval` (not
part of the permanent suite): a simple alias chain (`let a=1; b=a; c=b;
d=c; e=d; in d+e`), a chain through an attrset selection, a chain
through a curried function application, and a legitimately deep
(2000-hop) non-cyclic alias chain -- all four matched `nix-instantiate`
exactly, confirming both the chained-Cell loop and its chase-limit
termination behave correctly on both the common (0-1 hop) and
chained/deep cases.

**Measured, interleaved, 10 trials each** (`perf stat -e
cpu_core/instructions/,cpu_core/cycles/`, `taskset -c 0`,
before/after/before/after...):

| | mean | stdev |
|---|---|---|
| before | 6,321,864,051.8 | 1,959,820.6 |
| after | 6,243,035,227.6 | 1,101,697.2 |

A -1.25% / ~78.8M instruction reduction, with the delta roughly 40x
either side's stdev -- comfortably exceeding noise, and somewhat larger
than the handoff's own 0.9-1.0% estimate (the three collapsed call/ret
pairs' ABI prologue/epilogue overhead was evidently worth slightly more
than the flat-profile self-time figures alone suggested, consistent
with this campaign's repeated finding that call/dispatch overhead, not
the underlying algorithm, is the real cost at these hot sites). Shipped.

Files: `include/asnix/heap.h` (`ASNIX_CELL_CHASE_LIMIT` moved here from
`value_util.c`), `src/asm/ops/op_var_ref.S` (`.Lvar_ref_check_cell`'s
`call asnix_resolve_cell_chain` replaced with an inline
`.Lvar_ref_cell_loop`), `src/asm/force.S` (`.Lforce_check_cell`'s `call
asnix_resolve_cell_chain` replaced with an inline `.Lforce_cell_loop`),
`src/c/value_util.c` (comment update only -- `asnix_resolve_cell_chain`
itself is unchanged, still the reference implementation for
`op_select.S`/`op_select_or.S`/`op_with.S`).

## M163: `asnix_bshared_attrs_resolve` on `op_with.S`'s lazy-union fallback -- investigated, confirmed real work not call overhead, AND confirmed the call site itself is nearly unreachable on the real workload, declined

Directed candidate (same family as the `attrs_probe` case a prior
milestone examined): `asnix_bshared_attrs_resolve` (`builtins_shared.c`)
shows up at ~0.5% self-time on `d.nix`, called from `op_with.S`'s
`OP_WITH_TRY` handler only on the lazy-union (negative-count) branch --
the common already-flat case is handled entirely inline by
`op_with_try`'s own binary search, no call at all.

**Read the implementation first.** `asnix_bshared_attrs_resolve`
(`builtins_shared.c`) does three things when it actually has work to do:
check a one-word flat-cache, then a bottom-up *pairwise* merge across the
union's leaves (not a left-to-right fold -- that shape was itself a
deliberate M88 fix, per the function's own comment, to avoid
O(total_size * nleaves) re-copying), calling `asnix_attrs_eager_merge`
(`attrs_update.c`) per pair. `asnix_attrs_eager_merge` itself is a
two-pointer sorted merge of `Attr` entries with a `memcpy` per entry and
one `asnix_arena_alloc` for the output -- genuine data-copying work, not
dispatch filler.

**Measured via `perf record --call-graph dwarf,4096` on `d.nix`** (real
nixpkgs/ffmpeg eval): `asnix_bshared_attrs_resolve` is 2.34% of samples
with children, but only **0.51% self** -- the other ~1.83% is time spent
*inside* `asnix_attrs_eager_merge` (3.35% w/ children, **1.58% self**,
mostly in its `memcpy` calls) that `resolve` calls into. This directly
confirms the hypothesis: resolving a union is dominated by the actual
merge/copy work, not by `resolve`'s own dispatch/branch/call overhead --
hand-writing `resolve` itself in asm would at best shave the ~0.5%
self-time's call/ret and flat-cache-check overhead, while leaving the
real cost (the merge's allocation + memcpys, which stay in C regardless)
untouched.

**Then checked how much of that cost is even reachable from the
assigned call site specifically**, via temporary call-counter
instrumentation (a `uint64_t` global incremented at the top of
`asnix_bshared_attrs_resolve`, another incremented only on its real-merge
path past the flat-cache check, and a third incremented in `op_with.S`
right before its `call asnix_bshared_attrs_resolve`, all dumped via an
`__attribute__((destructor))` printer -- reverted before this commit,
confirmed via `git status`/`git diff` both clean). Result on the full
`d.nix` eval:

```
resolve_calls=2009207 real_merge=21343 with_try_calls=1568
```

`op_with.S`'s lazy-union branch fires **1,568 times** out of 2,009,207
total `asnix_bshared_attrs_resolve` calls (0.08%) and 21,343 real merges
(7.3%) -- i.e. even among the already-rare "a union actually needs
resolving" cases, the vast majority are reached from other call sites
(`OP_SELECT`/`OP_SELECT_OR`/`OP_HAS_ATTR`'s own `attrs_probe`-style
callers, `builtins_attrs.c`, `derivation.c`, `main.c`, etc.), not
`op_with`. Against a 6.3-billion-instruction eval, even a
(unrealistically optimistic) zero-cost hand-asm `resolve` saving 10-20
instructions of call/ret+register-save overhead per call on only 1,568
calls is on the order of 15,000-30,000 instructions -- roughly
0.0002%-0.0005% of the total, two to three orders of magnitude below
this campaign's noise floor on interleaved `d.nix` trials.

**Conclusion**: declined. The candidate's own hypothesis holds up on
inspection (this *is* genuine copying/merging work, not call-overhead
filler), and is further undercut by the call site in question being
almost never taken at all on the representative real-workload benchmark.
Either finding alone would be enough to decline; together they leave no
plausible path to a measurable win here. No source files changed
(temporary instrumentation added and fully reverted). Files:
`docs/architecture.md` only.

## M164: branch-fused `OP_HAS_ATTR_IF`/`OP_EQ_IF`/`OP_NEQ_IF`/`OP_LT_IF`/`OP_GE_IF` -- `if` no longer materializes a `TRUE`/`FALSE` `Value` for a condition that was already a bare comparison/`?` test

Two prior investigations into opcode fusion this campaign (a histogram of
real `(op, next_op)` dispatch-pair frequencies, and an actually-built-
and-measured `MK_THUNK`->`FRAME_SET` fusion prototype) both correctly
declined fusion as not worth it -- but both only ever targeted
eliminating the generic dispatch-TAIL overhead (the advance/load/jmp and
a push/pop, ~3-9 instructions/occurrence). Re-examining the same measured
top-20 `(op, next_op)` pairs on a real `d.nix`/ffmpeg eval
(14,656,701 total dispatch steps) through a different lens -- does
fusion eliminate real REDUNDANT WORK, not just dispatch tail? -- found a
qualitatively different case: `(HAS_ATTR, IF)`, 352,692 occurrences.
`op_has_attr.S`'s `OP_HAS_ATTR` computes a definitive true/false answer
in its own internal control flow, then pays ~2 instructions to push it as
a tagged `Value` onto VALSTACK (store + pointer bump). `op_if.S`'s
`OP_IF` then pays ~10 more to pop it back, re-derive its tag, mask it,
compare against `TAG_IMM`, shift, and compare against `TRUE`/`FALSE` --
fully RE-VERIFYING a type the producer already knew with certainty. That
is genuine redundant work, confirmed structural via `compiler.c`'s
`AST_IF` case (the condition was ALWAYS compiled fully generically --
`compile_expr` then `ib_if`, zero special-casing for what produced the
boolean), unlike `&&`/`||`, which `ir.h`'s own comment already flags as
deliberately compiled branch-shaped instead of eager. Comparison ops
(`op_cmp.S`'s `EQ`/`NEQ`/`LT`/`GT`/`LE`/`GE`) produce booleans the
identical way and share the exact same opportunity, though none
individually appeared in this benchmark's own top-20 pairs (their real
volume on `d.nix` specifically was unmeasured going in).

**The fix.** Five new IR ops (`ir.h`): `OP_HAS_ATTR_IF` (`a` = byte delta
to the else-branch, patched via `ib_patch_delta`, same self-relative
convention as `OP_IF`/`OP_JMP`; `b` = symbol id, same a/b roles as
`OP_WITH_TRY`/`OP_SELECT_OR`) and `OP_EQ_IF`/`OP_NEQ_IF`/`OP_LT_IF`/
`OP_GE_IF` (`a` = byte delta only). Each branches DIRECTLY off the same
internal true/false result the plain op already computes -- a TRUE
result falls through to the very next op (the compiled "then" branch); a
FALSE result jumps by `a` to the "else" branch -- never tagging/pushing/
popping/re-deriving a `Value` at all. New asm:
`src/asm/ops/op_has_attr_if.S` (lifted directly from `op_has_attr.S`,
including its M154 union-probe fast path and never-forces/never-fatal-
on-non-attrset semantics, unchanged) and `src/asm/ops/op_cmp_if.S` (all
four comparisons, each lifted directly from its `op_cmp.S` counterpart --
`OP_LT_IF`/`OP_GE_IF` keep the identical INT fast path and the identical
C fallback, `asnix_cmp_lt_values`/`asnix_cmp_ge_values`, for anything
else, fatal on a genuine type mismatch exactly as before; `OP_EQ_IF`/
`OP_NEQ_IF` keep the identical `asnix_bshared_value_eq_op` call).
`OP_GT`/`OP_LE` themselves get no fused form -- they're already dead code
per the existing M51 comment (`>`/`<=` never compile to the native
`OP_GT`/`OP_LE`, only to swapped `OP_LT`/`OP_NOT`).

`compiler.c`'s `AST_IF` case now special-cases its own `cond` node: a
bare `AST_HAS_ATTR` (static symbol only, not the `? ${expr}` dynamic
form -- out of scope, no measured volume justifying the extra
complexity) emits `OP_HAS_ATTR_IF` directly; a bare comparison
`AST_BINOP` (`e`/`n`/`l`/`G`/`g`/`L`) emits the matching `_IF` op, with
`g` (`>`) and `L` (`<=`) reusing `OP_LT_IF` via the exact same swapped-
operand-push trick the ordinary (non-`if`) `>`/`<=` path already uses
(M51's own comment) -- `<=` additionally swaps which compiled branch is
the fallthrough vs. the jump target, since `a <= b` is `!(b < a)`: the
fallthrough-on-true side of `OP_LT_IF(b, a)` means "`b < a` is true",
i.e. "`a <= b` is false", i.e. the caller's ELSE; the jump-target side is
the caller's THEN. A constant-foldable comparison (literal int/float
operands on both sides) is explicitly excluded via a cheap
`try_fold_const_binop` probe-and-discard before taking the fused path,
so it falls through unchanged to the ordinary `PUSH_TRUE/FALSE` + `OP_IF`
compile -- this fusion never interacts with that separate, pre-existing
optimization. Every other `if`-condition shape (a variable, `&&`/`||`,
a call result, ...) is completely unaffected, still compiling through
the original generic `compile_expr(cond); ib_if(b);` path.

**The jump-retargeting hazard, handled.** All five new ops carry a
self-relative byte-delta operand in `a`, exactly like `OP_IF`/`OP_JMP`/
`OP_WITH_TRY`/`OP_SELECT_OR`/`OP_SELECT_DYNAMIC_OR` -- which means every
one of the (opt-in, `ASNIX_IR_OPT=1`-only) bytecode-optimization passes'
own `op_is_jump`-style predicate, used both by `irpass.c`'s
`asnix_irpass_remove` (the shared delta-fixup-on-removal primitive) and
by each pass's own incoming-jump safety check, had to be extended to
recognize the five new ops too -- otherwise a pass removing/relocating
ops around one of them would silently leave its delta stale (exactly the
hazard class this project's own `cmpnot`/`strconcat` bug history already
established). Updated in all ten call sites: `irpass.c`,
`irpass_dce.c`, `irpass_dce_if.c`, `irpass_deadframe.c`,
`irpass_jmpnop.c`, `irpass_jmpthread.c`, `irpass_notfold.c`,
`irpass_strconcat.c`, `irpass_streq.c`, `irpass_cmpnot.c`. None of
these passes are registered by default (opt-in only, no Makefile test
target sets `ASNIX_IR_OPT`), so this wasn't exercised by the correctness
ladder, but left unfixed it would have been a latent miscompile waiting
for whoever next ran with `ASNIX_IR_OPT=1` -- not something to leave for
later. `bytecode.c`'s serializer/deserializer needed one addition
(`OP_HAS_ATTR_IF` joins `OP_WITH_TRY`/`OP_SELECT_OR` in the existing
`PTAG_OP_SYM_B` case -- symbol re-interned by name, not replayed as a
stale cross-process integer, same M103-era fix those two ops already
have); `OP_EQ_IF`/`OP_NEQ_IF`/`OP_LT_IF`/`OP_GE_IF` need no special
case at all, falling through to the existing generic `PTAG_OP` path
exactly like `OP_IF`/`OP_JMP` already do (a plain delta, no symbol, no
pool reference). `dispatch_table.c` and `irdump.c` (op name table +
disassembly operand printing) updated for all five.

**Correctness.** `make test`, `make test-e2e` (296 OK), `make test-
conformance` (all OK) all green. `make test-nix-conformance
NIX_CONFORMANCE_DIR=/tmp/nix-conformance`: `pass=655 fail=3 skip=148`,
the same 3 pre-existing position-tracking failures
(`eval-okay-getattrpos-functionargs.nix`, `eval-okay-getattrpos.nix`,
`eval-okay-inherit-attr-pos.nix`). `make test-nixpkgs-hash`: `pass=148
fail=0`. `./asnix d.nix` output byte-identical:
`/nix/store/29iacg6h530yx7rxz4k1fhvi0kxxhsam-ffmpeg-9.0.1-bin`. Hand-
written differential checks against `? attr` on an attrset/non-attrset/
missing-key target, all six comparison operators on int/string/float
operands (including both orderings of `<`/`>`/`<=`/`>=`), a NaN-float
comparison (`0 < n` / `0 >= n` both `false`, matching the existing non-
total-order NaN behavior `irpass_cmpnot.c`'s own comment already
documents -- this fusion calls the identical C fallback, so it couldn't
diverge from that even if it tried), a non-int/non-string ordering
comparison (fatal, correct error message preserved), the dynamic `?
${name}` form (confirmed still routed through the unchanged generic
`OP_HAS_ATTR_DYNAMIC` + `OP_IF` path, untouched by this milestone's
scope), and nested/non-`if`-condition uses of `?`/comparisons (a sub-
expression compiled the ordinary way, never accidentally branch-fused)
-- all matched expected semantics via `irdump` inspection and direct
`./asnix` runs.

**Measured, interleaved, 20 trials (`perf stat -e cpu_core/instructions/,
cpu_core/cycles/`, `taskset -c 0`, before/after/before/after..., two
batches of 10 run hours apart to rule out a time-of-day confound).** Raw
instruction counts were noisier run-to-run than expected for a
deterministic program (~0.08% spread within repeated runs of the SAME
binary) -- too noisy for a trustworthy unpaired mean comparison alone --
but the PAIRED per-trial difference (this milestone's whole reason for
insisting on interleaved, not batched, trials) was unanimous: all 20 of
20 trials showed `after < before`, zero exceptions. The implementer's own
mean paired reduction: -3,604,174 instructions (-0.057%, 95% CI
[-0.070%, -0.044%]) out of a ~6.32B-instruction baseline.

**Independent verification found a materially larger effect.** A
separate adversarial-verify pass ran 35 total interleaved paired trials
(20 before/after + 15 reversed after/before, fresh isolated builds,
output hash checked on every one of the 35+15 control runs) -- unanimous
in 35/35, same hard-win signature. Combined mean: **-0.132%** (95% CI
[-0.142%, -0.122%], ~-8.3M instructions out of a ~6.322B baseline) --
roughly 2.3x larger than the implementer's own -0.057%. A same-binary-
vs-itself order-bias control (15 trials, baseline measured in both
slots) found only a -0.0078% slot-order bias, NOT unanimous in sign
(10/15) -- about 17x smaller than the real signal and inconsistent in
sign, ruling out measurement-order artifacts as the explanation for
either number. Per this campaign's established practice for resolving a
magnitude discrepancy (M157/M161's own precedent), **the number to trust
going forward is -0.132% (~8.3M instructions), not -0.057%** -- a
favorable correction: the fix is real and noticeably better than first
reported. The verify pass also ran 54 hand-written adversarial
correctness cases (bare `?`/all six comparisons on int/string/float/
mixed operands, fatal non-comparable-type orderings, NaN comparisons,
negated and `&&`/`||`-wrapped conditions confirmed NOT fused, paren-
wrapped/let-bound conditions confirmed NOT fused, the dynamic `?
${name}` form confirmed untouched) cross-checked against real
`nix-instantiate`, all 54/54 agreeing with real Nix where comparable --
including confirming one pre-existing, unrelated asnix gap (list
ordering comparison is fatal here where real Nix allows lexicographic
`<`) is identical in both the baseline and this fix, i.e. not a
regression this milestone introduced.
Cycles/wall-clock, as this campaign's own M154 entry would predict for
an effect this size, were too noisy to read a consistent sign from
directly (mixed signs across paired diffs in both the implementer's and
verifier's runs); instruction count, where the paired signal was
unanimous both times, is the trustworthy one here.

**Honest verdict: a genuine, fully-correctness-preserving win --
shipped.** -0.132% is modest but real, bigger than the implementer's own
first estimate and bigger than a couple of this campaign's other shipped
small fixes (M157, M159, M160, M161). The implementation reuses every
existing op's exact semantics byte-for-byte (no new C fallback
functions, no behavioral drift), and the architectural pattern
(branch-fuse a boolean-producing op directly into its own `if`-consumer,
mirroring `&&`/`||`'s existing precedent) generalizes for free to any
future comparison-shaped op this project adds. Shipped because the risk
was low (every hazard class this kind of change could hit --
jump-retargeting, type-check semantics, constant-fold interaction -- was
identified and verified closed above, and an unusually large 54-case
adversarial correctness battery found nothing) and the win, independently
reproduced twice, is unambiguous.

Files: `include/asnix/ir.h` (five new `OP_*_IF` enum entries + comments),

`ib_lt_if`/`ib_ge_if`/`ib_has_attr_if`), `src/asm/ops/op_has_attr_if.S`
(new), `src/asm/ops/op_cmp_if.S` (new), `src/c/dispatch_table.c`,

(`AST_IF` case), and the `op_is_jump` predicate in all ten irpass files
(`irpass.c`, `irpass_dce.c`, `irpass_dce_if.c`, `irpass_deadframe.c`,
`irpass_jmpnop.c`, `irpass_jmpthread.c`, `irpass_notfold.c`,

## M165: fuse the repeated `subq $8, %r12` / `movq (%r12), %rX` VALSTACK pop pairs into one `subq` + N independent-offset `movq`s, across every binary/ternary operator op

Directed candidate: every binary operator and every dynamic-attr op pops
its 2 (or 3) operands off VALSTACK with N repetitions of the pair `subq
$8, %r12` / `movq (%r12), %rX` written back to back. Each `subq`
computes a new address that the *next* `subq` then further decrements,
so the two (or three) loads are serialized through an address-generation
chain (`sub -> load -> sub -> load`) purely because they share the same
counter register, even though the loaded values are otherwise completely
independent of each other and nothing downstream reads any intermediate
value of `%r12` or the flags the `subq`s set.

**Read every site first, in the current source** (16 found, not the 17
originally guessed -- see below): `src/asm/ops/op_arith.S`
(`asnix_op_add`/`sub`/`mul`/`div`, one 2-pop sequence each),
`src/asm/ops/op_cmp.S` (all six comparison ops `eq`/`neq`/`lt`/`gt`/`le`/
`ge`, each a 2-pop sequence), `src/asm/ops/op_concat.S` (2-pop),
`src/asm/ops/op_update.S` (2-pop), `src/asm/ops/op_has_attr_dynamic.S`
(2-pop), `src/asm/ops/op_select_dynamic.S` (2-pop),
`src/asm/ops/op_select_dynamic_or.S` (2-pop), and a 3-deep case in
`src/asm/ops/op_insert_dynamic_attr.S` (value, name, attrs) -- 4 + 6 + 1
+ 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 16 sites, not 17; a repo-wide grep for every other
`%r12`-touching file (`apply.S`, `dispatch.S`, `force.S`,
`stacklimits.S`, and every other `op_*.S`) turned up no further instance
of this exact repeated-pop shape -- the other `%r12` users are either
single-slot pops (nothing to fuse), bulk N-slot pops via a single
pre-computed `subq $imm, %r12` already (`op_path_concat.S`/
`op_str_concat.S`'s varargs, `op_call.S`'s callee+args teardown), or
plain pushes. `op_with.S` has two *single*-pop sites
(`asnix_op_with`/`asnix_op_with_try`) that happen to share the file but
are different functions on different VALSTACK epochs, not a fusable
back-to-back pair.

**Safety, checked instruction-by-instruction per M111/M155's own
warning about this exact codebase area**: at every one of the 16 sites,
the instruction immediately after the pop block is either (a) a plain
`movq`/`movl` that just copies a popped register (reads no flags), or
(b) the start of a fresh type-check (`movq %rax, %r8` / `andq
$ASNIX_TAG_MASK` / `cmpq`) that generates its own flags before branching
-- never a conditional jump or `cmov` that depends on the `subq`'s own
flags. `%r12` itself is write-only/pop-only at every site until the
handler's own tail `movq ..., (%r12)` / `addq $8, %r12` push, so
collapsing N `subq`s into one changes no intermediate value anything
else reads. Confirmed by re-reading each file's current line numbers
directly (several had drifted from the original guess, e.g. op_arith.S's
four sites are now at lines 55/110/164/231, not whatever an earlier
survey assumed) rather than trusting the description alone.

**The fix**: each site's `N * (subq $8, %r12; movq (%r12), %rX)` became
one `subq $8*N, %r12` followed by N `movq`s at fixed offsets `8*(N-1)
(%r12)` down to `(%r12)`, preserving the exact pop order (and therefore
which register ends up holding which logical operand) byte-for-byte
except for the instruction count. Example (`asnix_op_add`):

```
-    subq $8, %r12
-    movq (%r12), %rcx                   // rhs raw (pushed last, popped first)
-    subq $8, %r12
-    movq (%r12), %rax                   // lhs raw
+    subq $16, %r12                      // pop both operands with one address computation
+    movq 8(%r12), %rcx                  // rhs raw (pushed last, popped first)
+    movq (%r12), %rax                   // lhs raw
```

and the 3-deep case (`asnix_op_insert_dynamic_attr`):

```
-    subq $8, %r12
-    movq (%r12), %rcx                   // value -- pushed last, popped first
-    subq $8, %r12
-    movq (%r12), %rdx                   // name
-    subq $8, %r12
-    movq (%r12), %rax                   // attrs -- pushed first
+    subq $24, %r12                      // pop all three operands with one address computation
+    movq 16(%r12), %rcx                 // value -- pushed last, popped first
+    movq 8(%r12), %rdx                  // name
+    movq (%r12), %rax                   // attrs -- pushed first
```

The three loads are now siblings off one earlier-available address
computation instead of a 2-or-3-hop `sub -> load -> sub -> load -> sub
-> load` chain.

**Verification ladder, all green**: `make test`, `make test-e2e` (one
transient failure in ~5 runs on a totally unrelated fixture,
`m39_addErrorContext.nix`'s successor in the glob order, not reproduced
in 4 more consecutive clean runs -- attributed to this shared,
contended machine, not this change; see also the `test-nix-conformance`/
`test-nixpkgs-hash` numbers below, which are exact-match and
deterministic), `make test-conformance`, `make test-nix-conformance
NIX_CONFORMANCE_DIR=/tmp/nix-conformance` (`pass=655 fail=3 skip=148`,
the same 3 pre-existing position-tracking gaps), `make
test-nixpkgs-hash` (`pass=148 fail=0`), and `./asnix d.nix` byte-
identical to `"/nix/store/29iacg6h530yx7rxz4k1fhvi0kxxhsam-ffmpeg-9.0.1-
bin"`.

**Measured on `d.nix`, 20 INTERLEAVED trials (before, after, before,
after, ... x20), `perf stat -e cpu_core/instructions/,cpu_core/cycles/`
under `taskset -c 0`**:

- **Instructions**: before mean 6,242,142,240; after mean 6,240,872,428
  -- a real but tiny **-0.020%** drop, exactly the shape predicted (N
  static `subq`s collapsing to 1, saving 1 instruction per 2-pop call
  and 2 per the one 3-pop call; the ~1.2M total instructions saved
  across the whole eval imply these 16 ops fire on the order of a
  million times combined over `d.nix`, which is plausible against a
  6.2-billion-instruction real-nixpkgs eval).
- **Cycles**: before mean 3,628,505,528; after mean 3,635,854,844 -- a
  nominal **+0.2%**, but the paired per-trial deltas range from -6.5% to
  +3.2% with a stdev (~1.9 points) several times larger than the mean
  delta itself: this signal is noise-dominated on this shared, contended
  host, not a real regression or a real win either way. This matches
  the brief's own stated expectation going in -- "don't be surprised if
  cycles ... are too noisy on this shared machine to confirm cleanly" --
  and that is exactly what happened: the dependency-chain shortening is
  real on paper (confirmed by inspection, not just hoped-for) but too
  small relative to this specific workload's total serialized work (the
  16 fused ops are a small fraction of `d.nix`'s dominated-by-import/
  attrset/string-store-path work) to rise above machine noise on cycles.

**Conclusion**: shipped. The rewrite is a pure, verified-safe
reordering with zero semantic change (same addresses read, same
registers populated, same pop order), a small but real and correctly-
predicted instruction-count win, and a cycle count that's genuinely
inconclusive on this noisy shared machine rather than a demonstrated
regression -- consistent with the task's own framing that an
inconclusive cycles read here would be an honest result, not a failure.

**Not covered, left for a future pass**: this milestone's own base
commit predates M164's `op_cmp_if.S` (branch-fused comparisons), which
was "lifted directly" from `op_cmp.S`'s own pre-fusion 2-pop sequences --
so `op_cmp_if.S` still carries the unfused `subq`/`movq` pattern this
milestone just removed from `op_cmp.S` itself. Not revisited here to
keep this milestone's own diff scoped to what was actually measured;
a trivial follow-up for whoever next touches that file.
