## M166: `op_has_attr.S`'s union-probe result branch (`testl`/`jnz`/`jmp` into `.Lhas_attr_true`/`.Lhas_attr_false`) -- investigated the same cmov conversion `op_cmp.S` already uses, measured a net regression, declined

Directed candidate: `asnix_op_has_attr`'s lazy-union probe path (the
`asnix_bshared_attrs_probe` call on the negative-count/union-header
branch, see M154) ends with

```
testl %eax, %eax
jnz .Lhas_attr_true
jmp .Lhas_attr_false
```

falling into `.Lhas_attr_true`/`.Lhas_attr_false`, each of which just
loads a different `TRUE`/`FALSE` tagged immediate before falling
through to the shared push epilogue. This is superficially the same
shape `op_cmp.S`'s `asnix_op_eq`/`asnix_op_neq` already converted to a
single `cmov` between two pre-loaded constants (M-numbered earlier,
see `op_cmp.S`'s own `testl %eax, %eax` / `cmoveq %rdx, %rax` pair).

**Read `op_cmp.S`'s existing conversion first**, then **all** of
`op_has_attr.S`'s control flow (not just the three lines above) before
touching anything, per this milestone's own briefing -- `.Lhas_attr_true`
has a *second* caller: the binary-search loop's own `je .Lhas_attr_true`
(around line 79), which must keep working as a plain `jmp` target
regardless of what the probe-result branch above it is rewritten to.
Converting only the probe-result branch to a `cmov` (leaving
`.Lhas_attr_true`/`.Lhas_attr_false` as-is for the binary-search loop's
`je`/`jge` to keep targeting) composes fine: the probe path would
compute the result directly and jump straight to the shared push point,
bypassing the two labels entirely, without disturbing the other caller.
Implemented and built clean; `make test`, `make test-e2e`,
`make test-conformance` all green;
`make test-nix-conformance NIX_CONFORMANCE_DIR=/tmp/nix-conformance`
reported `pass=655 fail=3 skip=148` (the 3 known pre-existing
position-tracking gaps, unchanged); `make test-nixpkgs-hash` reported
`pass=148 fail=0`; `./asnix d.nix` stayed byte-identical to the expected
store path.

**But measured it anyway before trusting the shape-match**, via 10
interleaved `perf stat -e cpu_core/instructions/,cpu_core/cycles/`
trials on `d.nix` (real nixpkgs/ffmpeg eval), `taskset -c 0`, alternating
before/after:

```
instructions: before avg 6,236,260,470   after avg 6,240,328,225   (+4,067,755, +0.065%)
cycles:       before avg 3,538,790,432   after avg 3,551,341,952   (+12,551,520, +0.35%)
```

Both metrics regressed, consistently, in essentially every one of the
10 interleaved trials (not just on average) -- the opposite of the
hypothesis. `objdump -d` on the built `.o` explains why: unlike
`op_cmp.S`'s `asnix_op_eq`/`asnix_op_neq`, where the pre-`cmov` sequence
already sits inline right before the shared store (no extra control
transfer needed either way), `op_has_attr.S`'s probe-result branch sits
*in the middle* of the function, ahead of the binary-search block --
the old `jnz`/`jmp` pair reaches the shared push epilogue by falling
into one of the two existing labels (`.Lhas_attr_true`: `mov`+`jmp`;
`.Lhas_attr_false`: `mov`, falls straight into the push with no `jmp`
needed), for **4 retired instructions total either way**
(`test`+`jnz`+`mov`+`jmp` taken, or `test`+`jnz`+`jmp`+`mov` not taken).
The `cmov` version needs both constants preloaded into registers *before*
the `cmov` can pick between them (`movq $FALSE,%rdx` / `movq $TRUE,%rax`
/ `cmoveq` -- 3 instructions, not fewer than the 2 branches it replaces),
**plus** its own explicit `jmp` to skip the still-present binary-search
block and reach the shared push point, since the `cmov` site itself is
no longer adjacent to it -- 5 retired instructions total, every time,
not 4. The `op_cmp.S` win came from the branch *and* the constant-load
already being on the only path to the store with nothing to jump over;
here there's a binary-search block in between that something always has
to jump past, and the pre-existing two-label `jnz`/`jmp` shape already
paid for that jump as part of reaching one of two single-`mov` targets,
for free. The one subtlety flagged going in (two call sites composing
correctly into the same labels) was real and was resolved correctly;
the actual blocker was a different, non-obvious asymmetry between this
call site and `op_cmp.S`'s that only showed up by reading the generated
machine code and measuring, not by pattern-matching the source shape.

**Conclusion**: declined. Change fully reverted (`git diff` against the
pre-change tree is empty); no source files modified. Files:
`docs/architecture.md` only.

## M167: extending M162's hand-inlined Cell-chain walk to `op_select.S`/`op_select_or.S`/`op_with.S`'s own `call asnix_resolve_cell_chain` sites

M162 hand-inlined the "unwrap however many `Cell`s are chained together"
loop (a bare-variable alias, e.g. `let y = x; in y`) directly into
`op_var_ref.S`/`force.S`, but left `op_select.S`/`op_select_or.S`/
`op_with.S`'s own identical `call asnix_resolve_cell_chain` sites alone.
M162's own comment asserted those three "weren't hot enough on `d.nix`
to be worth inlining too" -- but that claim was never actually measured
against this specific benchmark at the time; it was an assumption, not a
finding. This milestone checked it directly.

**Read `op_var_ref.S`'s own M162 implementation first** (`.Lvar_ref_cell_
loop`/`.Lforce_cell_loop` in `force.S`) to confirm the exact shape being
proposed: mask the tag bits, compare against `ASNIX_TAG_PTR`, mask+load
the base pointer (clearing the low 3 tag bits and, for M118 compatibility,
the high 16 ThunkMap-index bits), compare the leading qword against
`ASNIX_CELL_MARKER`, loop on a hit (chained alias) up to
`ASNIX_CELL_CHASE_LIMIT` (heap.h), or fall through to the existing resolve
label on a miss (which may itself still be an unforced Thunk/LazyApp/
ThunkMap, handled exactly as before).

**Confirmed the three target call sites genuinely match this shape**
before assuming it: `op_select.S:214`, `op_select_or.S:203`, and
`op_with.S:226` (`OP_WITH_TRY`, not `OP_WITH` -- a different function in
the same file; `OP_WITH`'s own `ASNIX_ENV_WITH_TAG` frame-tagging logic
lives entirely in `asnix_op_with`/`asnix_op_with_exit` and is untouched by
this change) are byte-for-byte the same `pushq %rsi; pushq %rdi; movq
%rax, %rdi; call asnix_resolve_cell_chain; popq %rdi; popq %rsi; jmp
.L*_resolve` pattern M162 already replaced twice over.

**Measured the real volume first**, the same way M163 did before deciding
anything (temporary per-call-site `incq` counters directly in the three
`.S` files, a matching hit-count global + `__attribute__((destructor))`
printer in `value_util.c`, reverted before committing -- confirmed via
`git status`/`git diff` both clean after reverting). Result on the full
`d.nix` eval:

```
DBG select_cell=77236 select_or_cell=22490 with_cell=1128 total_hops=122709
```

100,854 total Cell-hit calls across the three sites (122,709 chase hops,
~1.22 hops/call -- overwhelmingly single-hop, same as M162's own `let y =
x; in y` common case) -- nowhere near M163's 1,568-call "almost never
reached" verdict that justified declining there. `objdump` on
`asnix_resolve_cell_chain` confirmed the same nested-call shape M162's
own investigation found at `op_var_ref.S`'s site: `asnix_resolve_cell_
chain` itself was never inlined with `asnix_value_is_cell` (which itself
calls `asnix_tag_of`) or `asnix_cell_target` by GCC, so every one of
these 100,854 calls paid 2-3 nested out-of-line calls just to mask tag
bits/compare a marker/load a pointer, on top of the `call`/`ret` and
push/pop pair at the `.S` call site itself.

**The fix.** Hand-rolled the identical loop directly at all three sites,
named `.Lselect_cell_loop`/`.Lselect_or_cell_loop`/`.Lwith_try_cell_loop`
to match each file's own existing label-naming convention. Register
liveness was checked at each site (not assumed): in all three, the
`call`'s immediate predecessor is the binary search's `.L*_found` label
(or the `attrs_probe` hit path, which re-converges on the same `resolve`
label with the same registers free), so `%r9`/`%r10`/`%r11`/`%rdx` are
all confirmed dead at the "it's a Cell" label and free to reuse as the
chase-limit counter/scratch, exactly like `op_var_ref.S`'s own
`.Lvar_ref_cell_loop` reuses `%rdx`/`%r8`-`%r10`.

**`op_select_or.S`'s fallback/default-value path, checked specifically**
per this milestone's own correctness concern: a Cell is only ever reached
at this label *after* the binary search (or `attrs_probe`) already found
a matching entry -- the `or` default/`.Lselect_or_not_found` path is a
completely separate, earlier branch (taken on a miss or a non-attrset
target), never entered from inside the Cell loop. The only way the Cell
loop diverts away from the ordinary resolve/push flow is the chase-limit-
exceeded case, which jumps to `.Lselect_or_blackhole` (fatal) -- the same
outcome the old `call`-based version had via `asnix_resolve_cell_chain`'s
own `exit(1)` on exceeding the limit, just now consistent with how
`op_var_ref.S`/`force.S` already report it (a catchable-by-nothing fatal
message rather than a bare `exit(1)`, a strict improvement, not a
behavior change in any passing test). This does NOT change `or`'s miss
semantics: a miss is decided entirely before a Cell is ever examined.

**`op_with.S`'s `ASNIX_ENV_WITH_TAG` frame-tagging, checked specifically**
per the same concern: `OP_WITH_TRY`'s new `.Lwith_try_cell_loop` only
reads/writes `%rax`/`%rcx`/`%rdx`/`%r8`/`%r9`/`%r10`, none of which carry
ENV or frame-tag state -- that logic lives entirely in `asnix_op_with`
(the frame-allocation function above `asnix_op_with_try` in the same
file) and `asnix_op_with_exit`, neither of which this change touches at
all.

**Correctness.** `make test`, `make test-e2e`, `make test-conformance`
all green. `make test-nix-conformance NIX_CONFORMANCE_DIR=/tmp/
nix-conformance` reports `pass=655 fail=3 skip=148`, the same 3
pre-existing position-tracking gaps as every prior milestone
(`eval-okay-getattrpos-functionargs.nix`, `eval-okay-getattrpos.nix`,
`eval-okay-inherit-attr-pos.nix`). `make test-nixpkgs-hash` reports
`pass=148 fail=0`. `./asnix d.nix` output byte-identical:
`/nix/store/29iacg6h530yx7rxz4k1fhvi0kxxhsam-ffmpeg-9.0.1-bin`.
Hand-written differential tests against real `nix-instantiate --eval`
(not part of the permanent suite), covering exactly the three touched op
codes: a bare-alias attrset select (`let a={...}; b=a; c={inherit (b)
x;}; in c.x`), a select-with-default hit and miss through an alias
(`b.x or 99` / `b.y or 99`), a `with` over an alias (`with b; x + y`), a
2000-hop non-cyclic alias chain resolved via `OP_SELECT` (`e.x` after
2000 `let`-chained aliases), a 2000-hop `OP_WITH_TRY` chain, and a
genuine `let x = y; y = x; in x.foo` alias cycle (caught by `op_var_ref.
S`'s own already-inlined blackhole, confirming the shared
`ASNIX_CELL_CHASE_LIMIT` constant still terminates correctly) -- all
matched `nix-instantiate` exactly (including one deliberately-not-a-bug
case, `with b; y or 55`, which both evaluators reject identically with
"undefined variable 'y'", since a bare-variable `or` default is parsed
as plain variable resolution, not attribute-select-with-default).

**Measured (10 interleaved `perf stat` trials, `taskset -c 0`, `d.nix`,
before/after/before/after...)**:

| | mean | stdev |
|---|---|---|
| before (all 10) | 6,243,948,568.2 | 8,942,782.6 |
| after (all 10) | 6,234,909,754.3 | 4,327,168.5 |

One trial pair (#4) carried a shared-machine contention spike common to
both before and after (+27-29M instructions on both sides relative to the
other 9 pairs) that inflated `before`'s raw stdev well above its usual
~880K; excluding that single pair (both sides, not cherry-picked):

| | mean | stdev |
|---|---|---|
| before (9 trials) | 6,241,132,786.0 | 879,175.3 |
| after (9 trials) | 6,233,597,250.6 | 1,298,053.4 |

A -0.12% / ~7.5M instruction reduction, ~8.6x either side's stdev --
smaller than M162's own -1.25%/-78.8M (expected: 100,854 calls here vs.
834,237 Cell reads there, and split across three colder op codes instead
of one hot one), but comfortably above the noise floor and, critically,
in the same direction in **all 10 of 10** trials with no exceptions
(including the noisy #4 pair) -- a result that would occur by chance with
probability 1/1024 if the true effect were zero. Shipped.

**Conclusion**: M162's own comment calling these three sites "not hot
enough to be worth inlining" was a reasonable-sounding but unverified
assumption, not a measured finding -- actually counting hits on `d.nix`
found over 100K combined calls, enough to produce a small but real,
consistently-signed win once applied. Smaller than M162 itself, but a
genuine instruction-count reduction at effectively zero risk (identical,
already-proven logic, copied three more times with per-site register-
liveness checks, not a new design).

Files: `src/asm/ops/op_select.S`, `src/asm/ops/op_select_or.S`,
`src/asm/ops/op_with.S`, `docs/architecture.md`.

## M168: `eval_file.c`'s `read_file` -- `fopen`+`fseek(SEEK_END)`+`ftell`+`fseek(SEEK_SET)` idiom replaced with one `fstat(fileno(f), ...)`

Directed candidate from a syscall trace (`strace -c -f ./asnix d.nix`,
real ffmpeg-closure eval): `read_file` (the function every `import`
goes through -- called once per imported file, ~1057 distinct files on
this corpus per M107/M115) sizes the file with the classic
`fseek(SEEK_END)` / `ftell` / `fseek(SEEK_SET)` idiom before `fread`ing
it whole. The hypothesis going in (per this milestone's own briefing)
was that glibc implements this idiom via `fstat`+`lseek`+`lseek`
under the hood -- 4 syscalls total -- so collapsing it to one direct
`fstat(fileno(f), &st)` right after `fopen` (no need to seek back to
`SEEK_SET` either, since the file position is already 0 right after
`fopen`, before anything has read from it) would collapse this to 1
syscall per file read.

**Read the existing code's own comment before touching anything**: the
`if (size < 0)` check right after `ftell` isn't incidental -- it's a
real, previously-fixed heap-corruption guard. `ftell` can report a
value that doesn't describe a regular file's actual byte count when
the path turns out to be a directory (`fopen` "succeeds" opening a
directory on Linux even though it isn't a regular file); without this
check, a bogus `size` reaching `malloc(size+1)`/`buf[size]='\0'` below
corrupts the heap instead of erroring cleanly. `fstat` does NOT give
this protection for free -- `fstat` on a directory fd *succeeds* and
just reports `S_ISDIR` in `st_mode`, it doesn't fail the way the old
code assumed `ftell` would -- so the replacement needs its own,
different-shaped guard: an explicit `S_ISREG(st.st_mode)` check,
rejecting anything else via the exact same error path and message
(`"asnix: cannot read '%s' (not a regular file?)\n"`, `exit(1)`) the
old code used.

**Differential-tested this exact scenario before shipping**, with a
pair of standalone, throwaway (not checked in) harness programs
(`/tmp/asnix_dirtest/old_read_file.c` / `new_read_file.c`) that each
embed one verbatim copy of the old/new `read_file` body and call it
directly on a real directory path, bypassing `resolve_file_path`'s own
earlier directory-to-`default.nix` rewrite (which is the only reason
production `read_file` never actually sees a raw directory today --
this check is explicitly "defense in depth... even from a future call
site that isn't as careful", per the old code's own comment, so testing
it directly, not just through today's callers, is the right bar).
Result, on this exact machine/kernel/filesystem: the OLD code's
`if (size < 0)` guard turned out to be *unsound here* -- confirmed via
`strace` that `lseek(fd, 0, SEEK_END)` on a directory fd on this
tmpfs/overlayfs returns `LONG_MAX` (`9223372036854775807`), not `-1`,
so the guard never fires; the old code instead ran
`malloc((size_t)LONG_MAX + 1)` (fails, returns `NULL`) followed by
`fread(NULL, ...)`, which **segfaults** (confirmed: `old_read_file
/tmp/asnix_dirtest/adir` → SIGSEGV, exit 139). The NEW `S_ISREG`-based
code gave the clean, intended error instead (`asnix: cannot read
'.../adir' (not a regular file?)`, exit 1, no crash) on the identical
input. So the differential test did not find an old/new behavior
mismatch to preserve -- it found that the *old* code's own documented
protection doesn't actually hold on this filesystem, and the new
`fstat`/`S_ISREG` check is strictly more robust (doesn't depend on any
filesystem-specific `lseek`/`ftell` quirk), not just faster. Both
`import <directory-with-default.nix>` and `builtins.readFile
<regular-file>` behave identically before/after (verified directly:
`import` of a directory with a `default.nix` present still evaluates
it; `readFile` of an ordinary file still returns its exact contents).
`builtins.readFile` on a directory (the separate, near-identical
idiom in `builtins_m23.c`'s `read_whole_file` -- explicitly out of
scope for this milestone, confirmed only ~11 total `readFile` calls
on this corpus) is untouched and unaffected either way -- still
returns `""` on this filesystem (its `size`, also `LONG_MAX` here, is
never written through, since its own `fread` returns `0` for `EISDIR`
and nothing indexes `buf` past that).

Implemented (`src/c/eval_file.c`'s `read_file` only); built clean, no
new warnings. `make test`, `make test-e2e`, `make test-conformance` all
green; `make test-nix-conformance NIX_CONFORMANCE_DIR=/tmp/nix-conformance`
reported `pass=655 fail=3 skip=148` (the 3 known pre-existing
position-tracking gaps, unchanged); `make test-nixpkgs-hash` reported
`pass=148 fail=0`; `./asnix d.nix` stayed byte-identical to the
expected store path.

**Measured the actual syscall reduction before trusting the
hypothesis**: `strace -c -f` on `d.nix` showed `lseek` dropping from
2,136 calls to 22 (essentially all of it was this idiom -- `~1057`
files `x` 2 `lseek`s each, `fseek(SEEK_END)`+`fseek(SEEK_SET)`,
roughly matches), but `fstat` stayed **exactly flat at 3,490 calls
both before and after** -- not the hoped-for 4-syscalls-to-1 collapse.
Traced why with a single-file `strace` on the standalone harness
programs: glibc's own `fopen()` already issues one implicit `fstat` on
the fd for its own internal buffering-mode setup, on *every* `fopen`
call, regardless of what happens afterward -- so the old idiom was
really `fstat`(fopen-internal) + `fstat`+`lseek`(the `fseek(SEEK_END)`
call) + `lseek`(`fseek(SEEK_SET)`) = 2 `fstat` + 2 `lseek` = 4 syscalls
per file, and the new code is `fstat`(fopen-internal) +
`fstat`(this milestone's explicit call) = 2 `fstat` + 0 `lseek` = 2
syscalls per file. A real 4-to-2 reduction, confirmed directly, just
not the 4-to-1 the briefing's syscall-count hypothesis assumed --
`fopen`'s own internal `fstat` isn't something a `fopen`-based
implementation can avoid without dropping down to raw `open`+`read`
(out of scope here: a bigger, more invasive rewrite than this
milestone's minimal-fix mandate called for).

10 interleaved `perf stat -e cpu_core/instructions/,cpu_core/cycles/`
trials on `d.nix`, `taskset -c 0`, alternating old/new (never batched):

```
instructions: old avg 6,321,509,551.8   new avg 6,316,512,343.2   (-4,997,208.6, -0.079%)
cycles:       old avg 3,608,458,950.4   new avg 3,632,022,303.6   (+23,563,353.2, +0.653%)
```

Instructions improved consistently -- `new < old` in every single one
of the 10 interleaved pairs, not just on average, matching the
confirmed syscall reduction (fewer `lseek`s retire fewer instructions
in both the libc wrapper and the kernel entry/exit path). Cycles moved
the other way by a small amount; given this machine's documented
measurement noise and that cycles (unlike retired-instruction count)
are sensitive to scheduling/cache-timing jitter this kind of syscall
change wouldn't obviously explain, and that instructions -- the more
deterministic, lower-noise metric -- moved favorably and consistently
across all 10 trials, this is treated as a genuine (if modest) win, not
a regression: `read_file` is one `fopen`/`fread` pair out of the
entire eval's instruction budget, so a few thousand saved syscalls
summing to ~5M fewer retired instructions (~0.08%) across ~1057 files
is the expected order of magnitude, not a surprise needing
further explanation.

**Conclusion**: shipped. Files: `src/c/eval_file.c`.

## M169: `IrOp` shrunk 24 -> 16 bytes (`int64_t a, b` -> `int32_t a, b`) -- `OP_PUSH_INT` rerouted through the constant pool

A read-only operand-field-width survey (directed candidate, prior
session) across 3.1M compiled ops on a real nixpkgs eval (`d.nix`,
ffmpeg's closure, including the largest single compiled program at
19,439 ops) found every `IrOp.a`/`.b` field value comfortably fits in
32 bits **except one**: `OP_PUSH_INT.a`, which used to carry the
literal integer value straight from Nix source -- real Nix integers
are full 64-bit values (nixpkgs has a literal exactly at `2^32`, plus
negative literals), so that one field genuinely needs more than 32
bits of range. Every other op's `a`/`b` is internal bookkeeping (a De
Bruijn depth/slot, a frame slot index, a pool index, a symbol id, a
self-relative jump byte-delta, an element count) bounded by the size
of the compiled program or the symbol table itself -- nowhere near the
32-bit ceiling, because those are compiler-assigned values, not
user-supplied data.

**The change**: `IrOp` (`include/asnix/ir.h`) narrowed from `{void
*handler; int64_t a; int64_t b;}` (24 bytes) to `{void *handler;
int32_t a; int32_t b;}` (16 bytes) -- `ASNIX_IROP_SIZE` 24 -> 16,
`ASNIX_IROP_OFF_B` 16 -> 12 (`OFF_HANDLER`/`OFF_A` unchanged at 0/8). A
16-byte record (8-byte pointer + two 4-byte ints) is still naturally
8-byte-aligned with no compiler-inserted padding (confirmed directly:
`sizeof(IrOp) == 16 == ASNIX_IROP_SIZE`), same as the old 24-byte
layout -- this is a 33% reduction in compiled-IR memory and better
cache density for the dispatch loop, with a clean precedent: M105
already narrowed `ASNIX_ATTR_SIZE` 16->12 the same way.

`OP_PUSH_INT` can no longer carry an arbitrary int64 literal inline, so
it now routes through the constant pool exactly like `OP_PUSH_CONST`
does for string/etc. constants (`b` = pool index of the raw, untagged
int64 literal; `a` unused/0): `ib_push_int` (`irbuild.c`) calls
`ib_pool_add` instead of writing `v` straight into the op; the asm
handler (`op_push.S`'s `asnix_op_push_int`) loads the pool entry first,
then runs the exact same `ASNIX_INT_MIN`/`MAX` range check + tag-and-push
it always did, just against the pool-loaded value instead of an inline
operand -- the overflow-check semantics (a literal outside asnix's own
±2^60-ish representable window still aborts, matching the M56 guard
this op already had) are completely unchanged.

**Every op handler in `src/asm/ops/*.S` that reads `a`/`b` via
`ASNIX_IROP_OFF_A`/`_B`** needed its load width updated from an 8-byte
`movq` to either a 4-byte `movl` (zero-extending into the 64-bit
destination register -- used for every field that's provably always
non-negative: depths, slots, counts, pool indices, symbol ids) or
`movslq` (sign-extending -- used only for the handful of ops whose `a`
is a self-relative jump byte-delta: `OP_IF`/`OP_JMP`/`OP_WITH_TRY`/
`OP_SELECT_OR`/`OP_SELECT_DYNAMIC_OR`/`OP_HAS_ATTR_IF`/`OP_EQ_IF`/
`OP_NEQ_IF`/`OP_LT_IF`/`OP_GE_IF`, since the field's own declared type
permits a negative delta even though this compiler, in practice, only
ever emits forward jumps). The IP-advance (`addq $ASNIX_IROP_SIZE,
%rsi`) and every `irpass_*.c`/`irbuild.c`/`irpass.c` byte-delta
computation already went through the named `ASNIX_IROP_SIZE` constant,
so those needed no per-site edit at all -- only the macro's own
definition changed.

**`src/c/bytecode.c`'s on-disk cache wire format turned out to need
far less surgery than the task briefing anticipated**: it was already
discovered (M102) to serialize every op field as a value-based
zigzag+LEB128 varint (`wbuf_i64`/`rcur_i64`), never a raw `IrOp` struct
dump -- so narrowing the in-memory struct changes nothing about most
ops' wire shape. The one real wire-format change is `OP_PUSH_INT`
itself: a new `PTAG_OP_PUSHINT` tag (mirroring `PTAG_OP_CONST`'s shape
exactly, except the payload is a bare int64, not an already-tagged
`Value`) replaces the old plain-`PTAG_OP`-with-inline-`a` encoding.
Magic bumped `ASNXBC02` -> `ASNXBC03` (same mechanism M102 itself
established) specifically because a stale pre-M169 `ASNXBC02` entry's
`OP_PUSH_INT` records would otherwise be misread under the new
convention -- not a crash, a **silent truncation** of any literal
outside ±2^31, exactly the hazard class this change was warned to
guard against. `src/c/irdump.c`'s `OP_PUSH_INT` disassembly case
updated to print the pool-resolved value instead of `op->a` directly.

**`src/c/irpass_cfold.c`** (the one pass that reads/writes
`OP_PUSH_INT` operands directly, not just jump deltas) needed a real
logic change, not just a recompile: both folded operands are now read
via `(*pool)[ops[i].b]` instead of `ops[i].a`, and a successful
non-boolean fold overwrites the result back into `ops[i]`'s own
already-owned pool slot in place (`ops[i].b` left unchanged, pointing
at the same slot, now holding the new value) rather than needing any
pool growth. The other eight `irpass_*.c` files only do jump-delta
arithmetic through `ASNIX_IROP_SIZE`, already covered by the macro
change.

**Test fallout, found by `make test` (not anticipated going in)**:
`tests/ir/test_irpass_dce.c`'s one hand-built fixture (`mk(OP_PUSH_INT,
<value>, 0)`, raw `IrOp[]` construction bypassing `IrBuilder`/the pool
entirely, with `prog.pool = NULL` for its `ir_link`+`asnix_eval` check)
segfaulted immediately -- `asnix_op_push_int` now unconditionally
dereferences `pool[op->b]`, and this fixture had no pool at all.
Fixed by giving the fixture a real backing pool array matching the new
convention and pointing `prog.pool` at it. `tests/c/test_bytecode.c`
had one hardcoded `"ASNXBC02"` magic-string assertion in its
new-format round-trip fixture that needed updating to `"ASNXBC03"`,
plus its `fixture_old_format_is_rejected_cleanly` case gained an
explicit check that a bare `ASNXBC02` magic (now ALSO a stale pre-M169
format) is rejected the same clean way `ASNXBC01` always was.

Verification ladder: `make test`, `make test-e2e`, `make
test-conformance`, `make test-flake` all green. `make
test-nix-conformance NIX_CONFORMANCE_DIR=/tmp/nix-conformance`
reported `pass=655 fail=3 skip=148` (the same 3 known pre-existing
position-tracking gaps) across three separate re-runs in a row -- a
fourth, earlier run reported one additional failure
(`eval-okay-regex-201.nix`) that did not reproduce on any other run
(confirmed passing in 8 direct standalone invocations immediately
after) and is attributed to this session's own documented shared-
machine contention interacting with that target's `timeout 10`
per-case budget, not a correctness regression from this change. `make
test-nixpkgs-hash` reported `pass=148 fail=0`. `./asnix d.nix` stayed
byte-identical to the expected store path. `sizeof(IrOp) == 16`
confirmed directly (no padding). Also exercised the opt-in
`ASNIX_IR_OPT=1`/`ASNIX_IR_OPT=diff` bytecode-pass pipeline directly
(`irdump`/`asnix` both), including hand-written fixtures exercising
`cfold` folding a sum that exceeds `int32` (`2147483647 + 2147483647 =
4294967294`, confirmed NOT truncated -- though this one specific case
turned out to already be folded at the AST level by M136's own
existing fold, not the bytecode-level `cfold` pass) and nested
`if`/`with`/`select or` chains whose jump byte-deltas get rewritten by
`dce`/`dce_if`/`jmpthread` under the new 16-byte stride (spot-checked
several `-> op #N` targets in `irdump`'s annotated output by hand
against the `(target - site) * 16` formula); also ran the full
`ASNIX_IR_OPT=1` pipeline against the real `d.nix`/ffmpeg eval itself
(405 `jmpthread` + 13 `cmpnot` + 1 `dce_if` firings), same correct
output.

Measured 10 interleaved `perf stat -e
cpu_core/instructions/,cpu_core/cycles/` trials on `d.nix`, `taskset -c
0`, alternating old(24-byte)/new(16-byte) (never batched):

```
instructions: old avg 6,226,229,946.7   new avg 6,193,246,773.6   (-32,983,173.1, -0.530%)
cycles:       old avg 3,670,095,001.6   new avg 3,738,398,745.7   (+68,303,744.1, +1.861%)
```

Instructions improved consistently -- `new < old` in every single one
of the 10 interleaved pairs, not just on average, consistent with the
smaller `IrOp` record meaning fewer bytes read per dispatch step and
better cache density across the ~3.1M compiled ops this eval walks.
Cycles moved the other way, but on inspection this is measurement
noise, not a real regression: one single "after" trial (#2) spiked to
5.31B cycles while its OWN instruction count for that same run was
completely unremarkable (6.19B, right in line with every other "after"
trial) -- a pure scheduling/cache-timing outlier on this shared,
contended machine, not something caused by this change (the same
machine/contention caveat this session's own measurement methodology
already flags). Excluding that one outlier trial brings the cycles
average back in line with "before" (consistent with a modest but real
win, same as instructions). Given a 33%-smaller IR record touches only
the dispatch loop's own per-op field reads/advances -- a small slice of
this eval's total instruction budget, most of which is spent inside
builtins/attrs/string machinery untouched by this change -- a ~0.5%
whole-program instruction-count win is the right order of magnitude
for this change's actual scope, not a surprise needing further
explanation.

**Conclusion**: shipped. Files: `include/asnix/ir.h`,
`src/asm/ops/op_assert.S`, `op_call.S`, `op_check_formals.S`,
`op_cmp_if.S`, `op_frame.S`, `op_has_attr.S`, `op_has_attr_if.S`,
`op_if.S`, `op_lambda.S`, `op_let.S`, `op_mk_attrs.S`, `op_mk_list.S`,
`op_mk_thunk.S`, `op_path_concat.S`, `op_push.S`,
`op_rec_overrides_merge.S`, `op_select.S`, `op_select_dynamic_or.S`,
`op_select_or.S`, `op_str_concat.S`, `op_var_ref.S`,
`op_var_ref_cell.S`, `op_var_ref_raw.S`, `op_with.S`,
`src/c/bytecode.c`, `src/c/irbuild.c`, `src/c/irdump.c`,
`src/c/irpass_cfold.c`, `tests/c/test_bytecode.c`,
`tests/ir/test_irpass_dce.c`.

## M170: `docs/irop-compaction-proposal.md`'s "Proposal B, lookup-table variant" -- implemented in full, measured at +0.616% instructions (not the hand-estimated +14,656,701/+0.237%), consistently regressed in all 15 interleaved trials, declined

Directed candidate: Proposal B itself (`docs/irop-compaction-proposal.md`,
written against M169's then-still-24-byte `IrOp` and later updated once
M169 landed) -- stop having `ir_link()` bake a real handler *address*
into every `IrOp.handler` at link time; leave `handler` holding the
small op-id the builder emitted for the op's entire lifetime, and have
every dispatch tail do `asnix_handler_table[op_id]` itself, at run time,
on every single dispatch. The proposal's own "review finding" argued
this should cost a deterministic **+1 instruction per dispatch**
(`+14,656,701` total on this eval, `+0.237%` against this session's
baseline instruction count) -- at or below the rejected bucketed-stride
alternative's own 14.7-29.3M estimate, and the better starting candidate
of the two. This milestone built it and measured it, rather than taking
that estimate on faith.

**Implemented in full**, not a partial prototype: every op handler's
dispatch tail (all 31 files under `src/asm/ops/*.S` with a `jmp *%rax`
tail, 66 call sites total), `src/asm/dispatch.S`'s `asnix_eval` entry
dispatch, and -- found only by tracing every consumer of `IrOp.handler`,
not just the obvious per-op tails -- `src/asm/force.S`/`apply.S`'s own
synthetic sentinel-`IrOp` return dispatch (`.Lforce_sentinel_ir`/
`.Lapply_sentinel_ir`, used as a `RetFrame.IP` so `OP_RET`'s ordinary
jmp-chain lands back in native-callable C-entry code instead of another
real op). That last site was the one real correctness trap in this
change: pre-M170, a sentinel could simply stash `asnix_force_epilogue`'s/
`asnix_apply_epilogue`'s *real address* directly in its `handler` field,
since by the time anything dispatched to it every `handler` field
everywhere was already a real address and `OP_RET`'s generic tail had no
way to (and no need to) tell a sentinel apart from an ordinary op. Once
`OP_RET`'s tail becomes "treat `handler` as a small op-id and look it up
in `asnix_handler_table`", a sentinel holding a real code address instead
would be interpreted as a wild out-of-bounds table index -- a correctness
bug, not just a missed optimization, that a change scoped to "the obvious
per-op handler files" alone would have shipped with a latent crash the
first time a thunk forced via `asnix_force_for_print` (the printer path)
or a closure/primop applied via `asnix_apply` (`map`/`filter`/`foldl'`
and friends) actually returned. Fixed by reserving two extra slots at the
end of `asnix_handler_table` (`ASNIX_SENTINEL_FORCE_EPILOGUE`/
`ASNIX_SENTINEL_APPLY_EPILOGUE`, `ir.h`, kept in sync with `OP_COUNT` via
a `_Static_assert` since the sentinel constants have to be plain
`#define`s outside the `__ASSEMBLER__` guard to be usable from
`force.S`/`apply.S` directly) and giving each sentinel its own reserved
op-id instead of a bare address. `ir_link()` itself (`dispatch_table.c`)
became what the proposal document itself predicted it could become: a
one-time **validation** pass (every op-id must be in `[0, OP_COUNT)`,
loud `abort()` otherwise) instead of an address-rewrite, since there is
no more address-baking left for it to do. `bytecode.c`'s
`handler_to_op_id`/`irdump.c`'s `op_id_of` (both used to reverse
ir_link()'s address back to an op-id by linear-scanning
`asnix_handler_table` for a pointer match) needed the identical fix in
the other direction -- post-M170 that scan would never match anything
(`handler` holds a tiny integer; every real table entry is a large code
address), silently breaking bytecode-cache serialization and `irdump`
both. Simplified to a direct cast-plus-range-check instead, which is
also strictly simpler than the scan it replaced.

Built clean; `make test`, `make test-e2e`, `make test-conformance` all
green; `make test-nix-conformance NIX_CONFORMANCE_DIR=/tmp/nix-conformance`
reported `pass=655 fail=3 skip=148` (the 3 known pre-existing
position-tracking gaps, unchanged); `make test-nixpkgs-hash` reported
`pass=148 fail=0`; `./asnix d.nix` stayed byte-identical to the expected
store path. Manually re-verified the sentinel-dispatch fix specifically
(not just relying on the test suite having happened to exercise it):
`builtins.map`/`builtins.foldl'` (exercises `apply.S`'s sentinel return)
and printing a result containing nested lists/attrsets/thunks (exercises
`force.S`'s) both still produce correct output.

**Measured it anyway before trusting the "at or below the bucketed
scheme" framing**, via **15** interleaved `perf stat -e
cpu_core/instructions/,cpu_core/cycles/` trials (more than this
session's usual 10, per this milestone's own brief, since the open
design question here mattered more than most) on `d.nix` (real
nixpkgs/ffmpeg eval), `taskset -c 0`, alternating before/after (M169,
pre-M170, as "before"; this milestone as "after"), never batched:

```
instructions: before avg 6,191,083,515.3   after avg 6,229,226,672.4   (+38,143,157.1, +0.616%)
cycles:       before avg 3,490,727,044.1   after avg 3,506,297,371.6   (+15,570,327.5, +0.446%)
```

Both metrics regressed, consistently, in literally every one of the 15
interleaved pairs for instructions (range +0.517% to +0.666%, no
exceptions either direction) -- a clean, one-directional signal, not
noise. This is **2.6x worse than the document's own prediction**
(+0.616% measured vs. +0.237% predicted), for a reason the prediction
explicitly didn't account for: `asnix` builds as a PIE executable
(confirmed via `file ./asnix`: `ELF ... pie executable`), and this
project's own existing asm consistently uses RIP-relative addressing for
every global (`leaq foo(%rip), %reg` / `movq foo(%rip), %reg`) -- there
is no form of `movq table(%rip,%rax,8), %rax` in x86-64 (RIP-relative
addressing cannot itself carry a scaled index), so the table lookup the
proposal costed at "+1 instruction" (`load index, load table[index]`)
actually needs **two** instructions in this binary (`leaq
asnix_handler_table(%rip), %rcx` to materialize the table's base address,
*then* `movq (%rcx,%rax,8), %rax` to index into it) -- `+2` per dispatch,
not `+1`, before even accounting for whether the real measured dispatch
volume on current nixpkgs still matches the `14,656,701` figure the
proposal's own op-pair histogram instrumentation found in an earlier
session (not re-verified directly here; the gap between a predicted
`2 x 14,656,701 = 29,313,402` and the actually-measured `~38,143,157`
average delta suggests it's somewhat higher now, consistent with
nixpkgs itself having grown in the interim, but this milestone didn't
re-run that specific instrumentation to confirm it precisely -- the
`perf stat` instruction-count delta is the number that actually matters
for the ship/no-ship call, and it was measured directly, not inferred).
A non-PIE build (`-no-pie`) would close most of this specific gap (one
`movq` with an absolute base + scaled index, same `+1` the proposal
assumed), but changing the whole binary's PIE-ness is well outside this
milestone's scope and has its own independent security/ASLR tradeoffs
not evaluated here.

**Conclusion**: declined. The core design-document claim this milestone
was built to test -- that the lookup-table variant's dispatch-time cost
is "at or below" the rejected bucketed-stride alternative's -- doesn't
survive contact with this binary's actual PIE addressing constraints;
real cost is roughly double the naive estimate, and the result is a
real, consistently-reproduced regression on this project's own trusted
metric (instruction count), not a wash. `docs/irop-compaction-proposal.md`
updated with this real measured result in place of the hand-estimated
one, explicitly marked measured vs. predicted, and Proposal B's status
updated from "design exploration" to "implemented, measured, declined".
Change fully reverted (`git diff` against the pre-change tree is empty
for every file except the two listed below); no source files modified,
including `docs/ir-format.md`/`docs/abi.md`, both briefly updated while
the implementation existed in the tree and reverted along with it, since
describing dispatch machinery that no longer exists would be actively
misleading rather than merely stale. Files: `docs/architecture.md`,
`docs/irop-compaction-proposal.md` only.

## M171: `ib_finish`'s shrink-to-fit `realloc()` on `ops`/`pool` -- routed through `arena.h`'s bump allocator instead, since neither array is ever freed

Directed candidate: `irbuild.c`'s `ib_finish` (the IrBuilder -> IrProgram
conversion that runs once per compiled function/thunk/attrset-element/
etc. -- 585,631 times across a real nixpkgs eval per M132's own measured
count). Its shrink-to-fit `realloc()` on `ops`/`pool` (pre-M100 era,
tuned further by M96) exists purely as a MEMORY fix: `ib_emit`/
`ib_pool_add` grow both arrays by doubling from a 24-slot initial guess
(M132), so without this trim, every builder would permanently carry
however much doubling slack it happened to land on when built -- M86's
own comment on this call site called that "hundreds of MB" across a full
nixpkgs eval. A fresh instruction-weighted profile (`perf record`, DWARF
unwinding) found `mi_theap_realloc` at 2.87% self-time overall, with
2.53 of those 2.87 points landing specifically under `ib_finish` (vs
only 0.71% under `ib_emit`'s own growth-realloc path, which only fires
15k-16k times, not 585k) -- confirmed via temporary, reverted
instrumentation, not just symbol-name guessing. M149 had explicitly
flagged this exact call site as open and out of scope at the time
("a different technique, if any, would be needed there"); no milestone
between M150 and M170 picked it up.

Read `ib_finish` and the surrounding growth code before picking a
technique (`ib_new`/`ib_emit`/`ib_pool_add`, same file). The average
builder emits only ~5.3 ops / ~5.8 pool entries (M132's own measured
figure) against a 24-slot initial allocation, so almost every one of
these 585,631 `realloc()`-to-shrink calls crosses a mimalloc size-class
boundary (e.g. ~85 bytes down from 384 for `ops`) -- not a cheap
in-place truncation, a real alloc-new+copy+free-old round trip under the
hood, done 585,631 times for arrays that are then **never freed again**:
`ib_finish` hands `ops`/`pool` straight to a freshly `calloc`'d
`IrProgram` that lives for the rest of the process (grep `irbuild.c`/
`ir.h`/`bytecode.c` -- there is no `free_program()` anywhere in the
tree; the one other place an `IrProgram`'s `ops`/`pool` get built,
`asnix_bytecode_deserialize` in `bytecode.c`, has the same "never freed"
property and uses plain `malloc`, not `realloc`-shrink, since it already
knows the exact final op count up front per M137).

That "allocated once, lives forever, never freed" lifetime is exactly
what `asnix/arena.h`'s never-free bump allocator already exists for --
it's used throughout the rest of the runtime (`builtins_shared.c`,
`attrs_update.c`, `builtins_list.c`, etc.) for precisely this shape of
allocation. Changed `ib_finish`'s shrink step: instead of
`realloc(b->ops, b->len * sizeof(IrOp))`, allocate the exact final size
via `asnix_arena_alloc`, `memcpy` the live prefix into it, then `free()`
the old oversized scratch buffer and repoint `b->ops` at the arena copy
(same treatment for `pool`). `asnix_arena_alloc` is a handful of
instructions -- bump-pointer-and-bounds-check, no mimalloc size-class
lookup, no free-list search (`src/asm/arena.S`) -- so this trades one
mimalloc-internal alloc+copy+free (the realloc) for one plain mimalloc
`free()` (strictly simpler than a shrinking realloc) plus one bump
allocation plus an explicit `memcpy`. The `b->len == b->cap` (no slack)
case is untouched: it was never reallocated before this change either
(nothing to shrink), so it still carries its original malloc'd buffer
forever, exactly as before. `asnix_arena_init(0)` (uncapped) is called
once at process start (`main.c`), so there is no `ASNIX_MAX_MEMORY`
interaction to worry about here.

Built clean; `make test`, `make test-e2e`, `make test-conformance` all
green; `make test-nix-conformance NIX_CONFORMANCE_DIR=/tmp/nix-conformance`
reported `pass=655 fail=3 skip=148` (the same 3 known pre-existing
position-tracking gaps, unchanged); `make test-nixpkgs-hash` reported
`pass=148 fail=0`; `./asnix d.nix` stayed byte-identical to the expected
store path (`/nix/store/29iacg6h530yx7rxz4k1fhvi0kxxhsam-ffmpeg-9.0.1-bin`).

**Measured both axes this candidate explicitly asked for** -- instruction
count AND peak RSS, both via **10** interleaved trials on `d.nix`
(real nixpkgs/ffmpeg eval), `taskset -c 0`, alternating before/after,
never batched. Instructions/cycles via `perf stat -e
cpu_core/instructions/,cpu_core/cycles/`; peak RSS via `/usr/bin/time -v`
`Maximum resident set size`:

```
instructions: before avg 6,185,243,459.0   after avg 6,132,424,692.6   (-52,818,766.4, -0.854%)
cycles:       before avg 3,563,036,351.5   after avg 3,488,215,996.2   (-74,820,355.3, -2.10%)
peak RSS:     before 521,488 KB            after 509,344 KB            (-12,144 KB, -2.33%)
```

Instructions: every single one of the 10 after-trials was lower than
every single one of the 10 before-trials (ranges didn't overlap at
all) -- a clean, one-directional signal, not noise. Peak RSS was
bit-for-bit identical across all 10 trials on each side (521,488 KB
every time before, 509,344 KB every time after) -- fully deterministic
for this workload, so a single pair of measurements would have sufficed
for RSS specifically, but it was measured 10 times anyway per this
session's own interleaving discipline. Peak RSS went down, not up: the
arena's 8-byte-aligned bump allocation has less per-object rounding
waste than mimalloc's small-object size classes do at these odd sizes
(~85 bytes for the average `ops` array, ~46 bytes for the average
`pool` array), so packing these 585,631 x 2 never-freed allocations into
dense 2 MiB arena chunks instead of mimalloc's own size-classed bins
ends up using *less* memory overall, not more -- the open tension this
candidate was framed around (CPU win vs. memory regression) didn't
actually materialize; both axes improved together.

**Conclusion**: shipped. A genuine, cleanly-reproduced win on both of
the metrics this candidate cared about, with no tradeoff to report
either way. Files: `src/c/irbuild.c`, `docs/architecture.md`.
